roles.name: member
roles.description: 실명 또는 별칭 기반으로 가입한 일반 회원. 게시글/댓글 작성, 수정, 삭제(본인 한정), 신고, 북마크, 팔로우, 투표/리액션, 알림 설정을 수행한다. 커뮤니티 규칙을 준수하며 제재 대상이 될 수 있다.

roles.name: expert
roles.description: 정치/경제 분야 전문성 검증을 통해 승격된 회원. member 권한 포함 + 전문가 배지 노출, 전문가 전용 주제 제안, 심층 글(리서치/인사이트) 게시, 전문가 Q&A 참여 등 신뢰도 기반의 추가 권한을 가진다.

roles.name: moderator
roles.description: 커뮤니티 운영을 담당하는 중재자. 신고 접수 큐 열람, 콘텐츠 임시 숨김/삭제, 사용자 제재(경고/일시정지) 요청, 분쟁 조정, 투명성 로그 기록 관리 등 커뮤니티 가이드라인 집행 권한을 가진다.

roles.name: editor
roles.description: 콘텐츠 품질을 책임지는 에디터. 말머리/주제 편집, 특집 큐레이션, 공지/고정글 관리, 홈·섹션 피처링 운영을 수행하며, 정책 위반 판단 권한은 moderator와 협업한다.

roles.name: admin
roles.description: 전사 시스템 운영 권한. 모든 리소스에 대한 접근(감사 검토 포함), 역할 관리, 정책/설정 변경, 법적 요청 대응 워크플로 관리, 서비스 상태/지표 관리를 총괄한다.

# pol-econ-board Documentation Index

## Document Purpose
Provides a complete, navigable map of the pol-econ-board documentation set so stakeholders can quickly locate the appropriate document, understand its scope, and follow a recommended reading sequence. Clarifies how documents relate across business objectives, requirements, governance, and compliance.

## Document List and Brief Descriptions
- [Service Overview for pol-econ-board](./01-pol-econ-board-service-overview.md) — Summarizes vision, goals, target users, value proposition, scope, differentiation, success metrics (KPI), and a phased roadmap from beta to expansion with business context and justification.
- [Business Model and Operating Strategy](./02-pol-econ-board-business-model.md) — Defines monetization pillars (ads, sponsorships, premium membership, data/insight reports), user acquisition and growth strategies, operating model and cost structure, regulatory risks, and KPI monitoring.
- [User Roles and Authentication Requirements](./03-pol-econ-board-user-roles-and-authentication.md) — Specifies registration, login, logout, email verification, password reset, JWT-based session policies, full role definitions (member, expert, moderator, editor, admin), permission matrix, and audit/security expectations in business terms.
- [Functional Requirements Specification](./04-pol-econ-board-functional-requirements.md) — Details business functionality: posts, comments, categories/tags/follows, votes/reactions, bookmarks, search/sort/filter, reporting and blocking, draft/review/publish workflows, notices and featured curation, feeds and subscriptions, notification triggers, rate limits, and acceptance criteria.
- [User Stories and Acceptance Criteria](./05-pol-econ-board-user-stories.md) — Presents personas (member, expert, moderator, editor, admin), key success scenarios, edge cases, misuse/abuse prevention, and Definition of Done with measurable acceptance criteria.
- [User Flows and Process Diagrams](./06-pol-econ-board-user-flows.md) — Visualizes major workflows (left-to-right Mermaid): account creation/authentication, authoring and publishing, reporting to moderation and appeal, notification settings and delivery, and exception branches with rollbacks.
- [Community Governance and Moderation Policies](./07-pol-econ-board-community-governance-and-moderation.md) — Defines community rules, allowed/forbidden content, political-sensitivity guardrails, report taxonomy and SLA, sanction ladders and triggers, transparency reporting, appeal/review/restore procedures, and election-period policies.
- [Non-Functional Requirements](./08-pol-econ-board-non-functional-requirements.md) — Establishes measurable performance expectations (response times, throughput, concurrency), availability and recovery targets (RTO/RPO concepts), scalability, observability, data minimization, scheduling windows, and capacity planning.
- [Security and Compliance Requirements](./09-pol-econ-board-security-and-compliance.md) — Outlines privacy principles and consent, data subject rights processing, age/identity and sensitive periods policy (if required), legal compliance (e.g., PIPA), auditability and transparency, abuse/spam/bot mitigation with rate limiting, and incident communication.
- [Data Lifecycle and Retention Policy](./10-pol-econ-board-data-lifecycle-and-retention.md) — Describes conceptual data flows; lifecycles for posts/comments (draft/publish/edit/archive/delete); moderation evidence retention; logs/metrics/backups retention and disposal; anonymization/pseudonymization; user-initiated deletion and recovery.
- [Notifications and Communications Policy](./11-pol-econ-board-notifications-and-communications.md) — Standardizes notification types (real-time, batch, digest), triggers, channels (in-app, email), frequency/rate limits, subscription/follow/digest policies, consent and preferences, composition guidelines, and retry/fallback.
- [Exception Handling and Error Scenarios](./12-pol-econ-board-exception-handling-and-error-scenarios.md) — Catalogs error classes and messaging principles; auth and authorization failures; content operation errors (upload/save/conflict); moderation workflow failures; external integration errors; rate-limiting and spam controls; data integrity and deduplication; and user recovery procedures.

## Document Relationships and Recommended Reading Order
Documents progress from context and strategy to detailed requirements and operational policies. Recommended path: Overview → Business Model → Roles & Auth → Functional Requirements → User Flows → Governance → Non-Functional → Security & Compliance → Data Lifecycle → Notifications → Exceptions.

```mermaid
graph LR
  subgraph "Context & Strategy"
    A1["Service Overview"] --> A2["Business Model"]
  end

  subgraph "Core Requirements"
    B1["User Roles & Authentication"] --> B2["Functional Requirements"]
    B2 --> B3["User Flows"]
  end

  subgraph "Operations & Governance"
    C1["Community Governance & Moderation"]
    C2["Notifications & Communications"]
  end

  subgraph "Quality & Compliance"
    D1["Non-Functional Requirements"]
    D2["Security & Compliance"]
    D3["Data Lifecycle & Retention"]
    D4["Exception Handling & Errors"]
  end

  A2 --> B1
  B3 --> C1
  B3 --> C2
  B2 --> D1
  D1 --> D2
  D2 --> D3
  B2 --> D4
```

Role-specific shortcuts:
- Product and business stakeholders: Start with the [Service Overview for pol-econ-board](./01-pol-econ-board-service-overview.md) and the [Business Model and Operating Strategy](./02-pol-econ-board-business-model.md), then review the [Non-Functional Requirements](./08-pol-econ-board-non-functional-requirements.md) and the [Security and Compliance Requirements](./09-pol-econ-board-security-and-compliance.md).
- Backend developers and QA: Begin with the [User Roles and Authentication Requirements](./03-pol-econ-board-user-roles-and-authentication.md) and the [Functional Requirements Specification](./04-pol-econ-board-functional-requirements.md), followed by the [User Flows and Process Diagrams](./06-pol-econ-board-user-flows.md), then consult governance, NFRs, compliance, data lifecycle, notifications, and error handling.
- Moderation and editorial teams: Focus on the [Community Governance and Moderation Policies](./07-pol-econ-board-community-governance-and-moderation.md) and the [Notifications and Communications Policy](./11-pol-econ-board-notifications-and-communications.md), then reference the [Exception Handling and Error Scenarios](./12-pol-econ-board-exception-handling-and-error-scenarios.md) and the [Security and Compliance Requirements](./09-pol-econ-board-security-and-compliance.md).

## Terms and Acronyms Guide
The glossary standardizes key terms used across documents.

| Term/Acronym | Definition | Where Used |
|--------------|------------|------------|
| pol-econ-board | Service prefix and identifier for this project focused on political and economic discourse. | All documents |
| EARS | Easy Approach to Requirements Syntax; unambiguous, testable requirement statements. | Requirements documents (03, 04, 07, 08, 09, 11, 12) |
| JWT | JSON Web Token used for access and refresh tokens to manage user sessions. | 03, 06, 09 |
| RBAC | Role-Based Access Control; roles include member, expert, moderator, editor, admin. | 03, 04 |
| SLA | Service Level Agreement; time targets for moderation and other workflows. | 07, 08 |
| KPI | Key Performance Indicator; metrics like MAU/DAU, retention rate, and content quality measures. | 01, 02 |
| NFR | Non-Functional Requirements; performance, availability, scalability, observability expectations. | 08 |
| PIPA | Personal Information Protection Act (Korea); privacy regulation relevant to data handling. | 09, 10 |
| RTO/RPO | Recovery Time Objective / Recovery Point Objective; continuity and recovery targets. | 08, 10 |
| MAU/DAU | Monthly/Daily Active Users. | 01, 02 |
| Sanction Ladder | Progressive discipline model: warning → suspension → permanent action. | 07 |
| Digest | Aggregated periodic notification summarizing content updates. | 11 |
| Transparency Log | Record of moderation and policy enforcement actions. | 07, 09 |
| Data Subject Rights | Rights to access, rectify, delete, and port personal data. | 09, 10 |
| Rate Limiting | Business rules that cap actions per user/time window to prevent abuse. | 04, 08, 09, 11 |

Role definitions used throughout:
- member — Registered user (real name or alias) with permissions to create, edit, and delete own posts/comments; report content; bookmark; follow; vote/react; and manage notifications; subject to community rules and potential sanctions.
- expert — Verified political/economic domain expert; inherits member permissions and can publish deeper research/insights, propose expert-only topics, and participate in expert Q&A with a trust badge.
- moderator — Community operator handling report queues; temporarily hide/delete content; propose user sanctions (warning/suspension); mediate disputes; and oversee transparency logs.
- editor — Content quality owner managing topics/tags; special curation; announcements/pins; and featuring operations; collaborates with moderators on policy violations.
- admin — Organization-level operator with access to all resources for audits; role management; policy/config changes; legal request workflows; service health; and metrics governance.

> Developer Note: This document defines business requirements only for the pol-econ-board documentation set. All technical implementation decisions (architecture, APIs, database design, and infrastructure) are at the discretion of the development team.

# pol-econ-board Service Overview

## Service Vision and Objectives
pol-econ-board is a trust-focused political and economic discussion and analysis community that enables informed conversations, expert insights, and transparent moderation. The service exists to reduce noise, polarization, and misinformation by combining community participation with clear governance and role-based accountability.

Objectives (12–18 months horizon):
- Establish a reliable forum for policy and market discourse with measurable trust signals and transparent moderation.
- Attract qualified experts and elevate high-quality insights to inform public understanding and decision-making.
- Build a sustainable, scalable business with diversified revenue streams and strong user retention.

Guiding principles:
- Truth and verifiability over virality.
- Community participation with accountability.
- Transparency in moderation and policy enforcement.
- Measurable outcomes and continuously improved operations.

## Problem Definition and Opportunity
- Information overload: Political and economic content is high-volume but low-signal. Users struggle to find reliable, contextualized analysis.
- Trust deficit: Anonymous or low-accountability forums enable misinformation and low-quality discourse.
- Expert–public gap: Experts lack structured ways to share insights with context and receive meaningful feedback.
- Fragmented experiences: Insights, debate, curation, and policy enforcement are spread across disparate platforms without consistent standards.

Opportunity:
- Provide a specialized, moderated environment that privileges sourced, contextual analysis and civil debate.
- Create a tiered role system (member, expert, moderator, editor, admin) to align incentives and responsibilities.
- Offer transparent governance, auditable decisions, and topic-focused discovery to increase user confidence and time-on-platform.

## Target Users and Core Value Proposition
Primary personas and value delivered:
- Members (general participants):
  - Value: Access to high-signal discussions, topic follow for personalization, bookmarking, reactions, and clear rules for safe participation.
  - Use cases: Post viewpoints with sources, ask questions, follow topics/experts, receive notifications, report problematic content.
- Experts (verified domain specialists):
  - Value: Credibility badge, dedicated long-form analysis and research formats, expert Q&A, topic leadership, and influence.
  - Use cases: Publish research notes, host Q&A threads, propose expert topics, respond to member questions.
- Moderators (community governance):
  - Value: Efficient intake queue, policy-aligned actions (hide, remove, warning/suspension requests), transparent records.
  - Use cases: Process reports, apply sanctions per policy, manage appeals, maintain a transparency log.
- Editors (content quality):
  - Value: Curate features, manage tags/topics, headline and topic hygiene, special coverage packages and featured placements.
  - Use cases: Tag and topic grooming, curated home/section features, announcements and pinning.
- Admins (operational owners):
  - Value: End-to-end oversight, policy configuration, role assignments, legal/compliance workflows, and audit visibility.
  - Use cases: Manage roles and policies, oversee indicators and risk, respond to lawful requests.

Core value proposition:
- High-signal community powered by verified expertise and transparent governance.
- Clear norms, predictable enforcement, and visible trust indicators.
- Topic-centric discovery with measurable quality and relevance.

## Business Model (Why/How/What)
### Why This Service Exists
- Address the trust and quality gap in political/economic discourse with an accountability-first community.
- Serve a growing audience seeking reliable analysis and expert commentary without the noise of general-purpose social platforms.

### Revenue Strategy
- Advertising and sponsorships: Brand-safe placements in featured sections and expert channels.
- Premium membership: Ad-light experience, advanced filters, expert AMAs access, early access to curated reports.
- Sponsored expert series: Cohort-based expert columns or Q&A programs, clearly labeled.
- Data-rich summaries and reports (business-level packaging): Periodic, curated digests for professionals.

### Growth Plan
- Supply-side seeding: Onboard a core cohort of verified experts and editors to set quality bar.
- Community credibility: Transparency logs, clear sanctions policy, and measurable content quality indicators.
- Partnerships: Think tanks, universities, and reputable media for co-produced series.
- Retention loops: Topic follow, expert follow, personalized digests, and earned status for positive contributions.

### Success Metrics
- Trust and safety: Low reversal rate in moderation decisions, timely SLA adherence.
- Engagement: Repeat sessions/week, quality reactions, follow actions, save/bookmark rates.
- Expert participation: Number of active experts and expert-originated threads per week.
- Monetization: Premium conversion rate, sponsorship bookings, ad yield.

## Core Features Summary
Business-level capability statements using EARS for testability.

Content creation and management:
- THE service SHALL allow members to create, edit, and delete their own posts and comments within policy-compliant boundaries.
- WHEN a user publishes content, THE service SHALL record topic tags, sources (if provided), and attribution for later policy checks and discovery.
- WHERE the user is an expert, THE service SHALL enable long-form analyses and expert Q&A threads with expert badges.
- IF content is reported, THEN THE service SHALL route it to the moderation queue and apply configured timelines for action.
- WHILE content is under review, THE service SHALL optionally restrict visibility according to policy.

Discovery and curation:
- THE service SHALL provide topic follow, expert follow, and curated features to surface relevant content.
- WHEN users follow topics or experts, THE service SHALL generate personalized feeds and digests subject to user preferences.
- WHERE editors curate features, THE service SHALL support announcements, pinned posts, and special packages.

Reactions and community signals:
- THE service SHALL support reactions, voting, and bookmarking to quantify engagement and relevance.
- WHEN a user reacts or votes, THE service SHALL update engagement signals used for ranking and curation.
- IF abnormal engagement patterns are detected, THEN THE service SHALL flag items for review (anti-gaming).

Reporting and governance:
- THE service SHALL provide a report feature with clear categories (e.g., misinformation, harassment, spam, off-topic).
- WHEN reports are submitted, THE service SHALL acknowledge receipt and communicate outcomes per policy.
- WHERE sanctions are applied, THE service SHALL log the action to a transparency record with reason codes.

Notifications (business-level):
- WHEN followed experts or topics publish, THE service SHALL notify followers subject to frequency limits and user consent.
- IF the system detects notification fatigue, THEN THE service SHALL throttle non-critical notifications.

Role-based capabilities (high level):
- WHERE the user is a moderator, THE service SHALL provide tools to hide/remove content, warn, and request suspensions per policy.
- WHERE the user is an editor, THE service SHALL manage tags/topics, featured lists, and announcements.
- WHERE the user is an admin, THE service SHALL manage roles, policies, and compliance workflows.

Performance experience (business expectation):
- WHEN users perform common actions (login, open feed, view post), THE service SHALL respond within a user-perceived 1–2 seconds for typical conditions.
- WHERE complex searches and filters are executed, THE service SHALL return initial results within 3 seconds for common queries.

## Scope and Out of Scope
In scope (business outcomes):
- Account registration, login/logout, email verification, password reset.
- Role-based permissions: member, expert, moderator, editor, admin.
- Posts, comments, replies, mentions, reactions, votes, bookmarks.
- Topic/tag management, topic/expert follow, curated features.
- Reporting, moderation workflow, sanctions policy, transparency logs.
- Personalized feeds and configurable notifications.

Out of scope (initial phases):
- Real-time audio/video debates and live streaming.
- Direct monetization between users (tips, paywalled posts) before compliance readiness.
- Public API for third-party integrations in Beta/GA.
- Frontend design specifications (layouts, colors, interactions).

Boundary requirements (EARS):
- THE service SHALL avoid collecting unnecessary personal data beyond business needs.
- IF a feature introduces legal/compliance implications, THEN THE service SHALL require policy and compliance review before launch.
- WHERE experimental features are enabled, THE service SHALL be opt-in and reversible at the cohort level.

## Competitive Landscape and Differentiation
Competitive sets:
- General social networks: Broad reach but low context, volatile quality.
- Traditional forums: Community-led but uneven moderation and limited expert validation.
- Publisher comment sections and Q&A: Limited interaction depth, weak governance transparency.

Differentiators:
- Verified expert participation with visible credentials and specialized formats.
- Transparent governance with clear reason codes, SLAs, and public transparency records.
- Topic- and expert-centric discovery that privileges sourced, contextual contributions.
- Role separation (moderator vs. editor) to balance policy enforcement and content quality.

## Success Metrics (KPIs) and Target Levels
Timeframes reference post-General Availability (GA). Targets define success thresholds that inform go/no-go decisions and iteration priorities.

Engagement and growth:
- THE service SHALL achieve 25–35% 28-day retention for new registered members by Month 6 post-GA.
- THE service SHALL achieve at least 4 sessions/week median among retained members by Month 6 post-GA.
- THE service SHALL reach 150–250 active experts with 400+ expert-originated threads/month by Month 6 post-GA.

Quality and trust:
- THE service SHALL maintain a moderation decision reversal rate under 5% monthly.
- THE service SHALL process 90% of standard reports within 24 hours and 99% within 72 hours.
- THE service SHALL keep repeat sanctions (within 90 days) under 10% of sanctioned accounts.

Monetization:
- THE service SHALL achieve 2.0–3.5% premium conversion among MAUs by Month 12 post-GA.
- THE service SHALL secure at least two sponsorship packages per month by Month 6 post-GA.

Reliability and responsiveness (user-perceived):
- THE service SHALL serve core feed and post views within 1–2 seconds p50 and under 4 seconds p95 for typical conditions.

## Phased Roadmap (Beta → GA → Expansion)
Principles:
- Deliver trust and quality foundations first (roles, governance, transparency).
- Validate expert and editor workflows alongside member value loops (follow, digest, reactions).
- Use measurable gates to progress phases.

Phase 1: Private Beta (target window: Q4 2025)
- Cohort: ~1,000 members, 50–75 experts, 5–8 moderators, 3–5 editors.
- Scope highlights: Core posting/comments, topic follow, expert badges and long-form posts, reporting and basic moderation queue, limited notifications.
- Gates (must meet to exit):
  - THE service SHALL achieve at least 30% weekly active rate among Beta cohort for four consecutive weeks.
  - THE service SHALL process 95% of reports within 48 hours during Beta.
  - THE service SHALL onboard minimum 50 verified experts with ≥2 posts each.

Phase 2: Public Beta (target window: Q1–Q2 2026)
- Scope highlights: Transparency logs, editor curation packages, expanded notification controls, improved discovery filters, sanctions and appeals process.
- Gates:
  - THE service SHALL demonstrate moderation reversal rate under 7% across two consecutive months.
  - THE service SHALL reach 20–25% 28-day retention for new sign-ups in Public Beta.
  - THE service SHALL sustain p95 perceived response under 4 seconds for feeds and posts under typical conditions.

Phase 3: General Availability (GA) (target window: Q3 2026)
- Scope highlights: Premium membership v1, sponsorship placements, expert Q&A programs, expanded governance reporting.
- Gates:
  - THE service SHALL reach 25–35% 28-day retention within three months post-GA.
  - THE service SHALL onboard 150+ active experts with ongoing production.
  - THE service SHALL meet monetization targets (≥2 sponsorships/month steady state).

Phase 4: Expansion (post-GA, ongoing)
- Possible directions: Regional topic verticals, institutional partnerships, digest products for professionals, advanced trust signals.
- Governance maturity: More granular sanctions matrix and election-period policies aligned with local regulations.

### Visual: Trust-Centric Content Lifecycle (Business Level)
```mermaid
graph LR
  subgraph "Authoring"
    A1["Draft Content"] --> A2["Add Sources/Tags"]
    A2 --> A3["Publish"]
  end

  subgraph "Community & Signals"
    B1["Topic/Expert Follow"] --> B2["Reactions/Votes/Bookmarks"]
    B2 --> B3["Personalized Feeds/Digests"]
  end

  subgraph "Governance"
    C1["Reports Submitted"] --> C2["Moderation Queue"]
    C2 --> C3{"Action Needed?"}
    C3 -->|"Yes"| C4["Hide/Remove/Warn"]
    C3 -->|"No"| C5["Maintain Visibility"]
    C4 --> C6["Transparency Log"]
    C5 --> C6
  end

  A3 --> B1
  B2 -.-> C1
```

## Document Scope and Implementation Ownership
Business requirements and objectives are defined in natural language without prescribing technical implementations. All technical decisions—including architecture, APIs, data models, and infrastructure—belong to the development team. The content specifies what the service should do, not how to build it.

## Related Documents
- Review the [Business Model and Monetization Strategy](./02-pol-econ-board-business-model.md) for business assumptions and revenue details.
- Review the [User Roles and Authentication Requirements](./03-pol-econ-board-user-roles-and-authentication.md) for role definitions and authorization policies.
- Review the [Functional Requirements Specification](./04-pol-econ-board-functional-requirements.md) for comprehensive feature-level requirements.
- Review the [Community Governance and Moderation Policy](./07-pol-econ-board-community-governance-and-moderation.md) for rules, sanctions, and transparency requirements.
- Review the [Non-Functional Requirements Guide](./08-pol-econ-board-non-functional-requirements.md) for performance and reliability expectations.
- Review the [Notifications and Communications Policy](./11-pol-econ-board-notifications-and-communications.md) for business-level notification rules.

# pol-econ-board Business Model

## Executive Summary
pol-econ-board is a trust-centered community for evidence-based political and economic discourse that connects Members with verified Experts, supported by Editors and Moderators, and overseen by Admins. The model blends four revenue pillars—contextual Ads, ethical Sponsorships, Premium Memberships, and aggregated Data & Insight Reports—operated under transparent governance to sustain credibility. Growth is driven by an expert-led content engine, curated discovery, visible moderation, and institutional partnerships. The operating model favors lean fixed costs with scalable variable spend, codified SLAs for content quality, sponsorship disclosure, and compliance.

This document provides business requirements only. All technical implementation decisions belong to the development team; it defines WHAT the system should do, not HOW to build it.

## Why This Service Should Exist (Market Gap & Pain Points)
- Information noise and polarization reduce the value of political/economic discussions; users lack credible, verifiable expert insights and clear norms.
- General forums underinvest in moderation, driving low trust, toxicity, and regulatory risk for operators and advertisers.
- Media outlets publish one-to-many; few enable sustained, moderated expert–member interaction with transparent standards.
- Professionals/institutions need synthesized insights and sentiment but face high discovery, verification, and brand safety costs.

Differentiation
- Verified Experts produce deep research, host Q&A, and model evidence-first debate to improve trust and retention.
- Transparent governance: auditable moderator actions, reason codes, SLAs, and appeal paths.
- Editorial curation: Editors spotlight high-signal threads, thematic series, and special coverage packages.
- Evidence/Attribution norms: source citations and labeling that reduce misinformation risk and enable informed discourse.

Primary Users & Roles
- Members: create posts/comments, follow topics, react/vote, report, bookmark, manage preferences.
- Experts: all Member capabilities plus long-form insight posts, expert-only topic proposals, expert Q&A participation, trust badge.
- Moderators: handle reports, hide/remove, request sanctions, maintain transparency logs, support dispute resolution.
- Editors: curate features, manage topics/tags, announcements, pins, and special series; collaborate with Moderators.
- Admins: system-wide policy/role management, legal requests, metrics oversight, and compliance.

## Revenue Model
Revenue Pillars
1) Contextual Advertising (Ads)
- Inventory: in-feed display units, topic page banners, newsletter placements, and contextually relevant sponsor tags.
- Targeting: context/topic-based; no sale of personally identifiable profiles; privacy-first measurement.
- Load policies: ad-light defaults that prioritize user trust and content integrity.
- Exclusions: political campaign/advocacy ads and sensitive categories restricted per policy and law.

2) Sponsorships
- Thematic sponsorship of premium series, expert AMAs, newsletters, and special coverage.
- Strict disclosure and separation between sponsored and editorial content.
- Pre-approval workflow across Editors and Moderators for brand safety and policy fit.

3) Premium Memberships
- Benefits: ad-light or ad-free tiers, priority in expert Q&A, exclusive long-form content, advanced digests, higher bookmark/export quotas, early feature access.
- Pricing & terms: monthly and annual options, free trial windows, limited-time promotions.
- Eligibility: authenticated users; gift and institutional licenses permitted per policy.

4) Data & Insight Reports
- Aggregated, anonymized trend/readership/sentiment reports; no personal data exports.
- Audience: institutions (universities, think tanks, media, finance) and professional power users.
- Distribution: one-off reports and annual subscriptions with quarterly refresh.

Revenue Policy Requirements (EARS)
- THE pol-econ-board service SHALL display no more than 1 ad slot per 10 content units in default feeds.
- THE pol-econ-board service SHALL cap ad frequency at 2 impressions per user per advertiser per day by default.
- WHERE a Premium tier includes "ad-free", THE pol-econ-board service SHALL suppress all paid ad placements for that user during the active subscription period.
- WHEN a post is sponsored, THE pol-econ-board service SHALL render a prominent "Sponsored" label with a link to disclosure at the start of the content unit.
- IF a sponsorship conflicts with prohibited categories, THEN THE pol-econ-board service SHALL block publication and notify Editors and Moderators for review.
- THE pol-econ-board service SHALL provide Data Reports only as aggregated/anonymized outputs without exposing personal data or individual behavioral traces.
- WHEN a Premium subscription lapses, THE pol-econ-board service SHALL revert entitlements to free tier within 1 hour.

Pricing and Unit Economics (Business-Level Assumptions)
- Ads: eCPM USD 1.5–6.0 depending on placement/seasonality; ad-light reduces fill, increases retention.
- Sponsorships: USD 8k–30k per themed series per month; AMAs USD 3k–10k per event; newsletter footer USD 1k–5k per send.
- Premium: USD 6.99/month or USD 69/year; free trial 14 days; annual discount up to 20%.
- Data Reports: USD 1.5k–5k per report; institutional annual USD 12k–40k.

Monetization Governance & Controls (EARS)
- THE pol-econ-board service SHALL maintain a prohibited and restricted categories list for ads and sponsorships with examples and disclosure rules.
- WHEN a booking is created, THE pol-econ-board service SHALL validate brand safety rules and conflict exclusions before accepting.
- WHERE labeling is required, THE pol-econ-board service SHALL ensure labels are visible in primary placements and listings.
- IF an advertiser or sponsor is placed on a temporary hold list, THEN THE pol-econ-board service SHALL block delivery until the hold is cleared.
- WHEN a complaint about mislabeled sponsored content is received, THE pol-econ-board service SHALL investigate within 2 business days and correct labeling or pause delivery.

Promotions, Coupons, and Discounts (EARS)
- WHERE promotional codes are enabled, THE pol-econ-board service SHALL apply the discount to eligible Premium plans during checkout and display the adjusted term and renewal price.
- WHEN a promotion expires, THE pol-econ-board service SHALL prevent further redemptions and honor already-granted terms until their end dates.
- IF a user attempts to stack incompatible promotions, THEN THE pol-econ-board service SHALL apply the highest-value eligible promotion and inform the user.

Refunds, Chargebacks, and Disputes (EARS)
- WHEN a Premium subscriber requests a refund within a configured cooling-off window (e.g., 7 days), THE pol-econ-board service SHALL honor the policy and revoke entitlements upon refund approval.
- IF a chargeback is received, THEN THE pol-econ-board service SHALL suspend Premium entitlements pending resolution and record the case in a finance dispute log.
- WHERE recurring billing fails, THE pol-econ-board service SHALL attempt collection per policy (e.g., 3 retries over 7 days) and then downgrade entitlements if unresolved.

Fraud and Abuse Prevention (Monetization) (EARS)
- WHEN suspicious subscription activity is detected (e.g., repeated trials), THE pol-econ-board service SHALL deny additional free trials and flag the account for review.
- WHERE bulk redemptions from the same payment instrument exceed thresholds, THE pol-econ-board service SHALL pause fulfilment and require additional verification.
- IF exploitation of ad-serving or sponsorship delivery is suspected, THEN THE pol-econ-board service SHALL halt affected placements and trigger brand-safety review.

## User Acquisition & Growth Strategy
Content Engine
- Expert-led long-form and Q&A cadences establish authority, improve SEO/distribution, and drive organic growth.
- Editors curate high-signal threads and publish weekly analytical digests for shareability.
- Topic and expert follow mechanics create recurring engagement loops for Members and Experts.

Community & Network Effects
- Reputation and expert badges reinforce credibility and repeat visitation; transparency logs foster trust.
- Member referrals, co-reading, and inter-topic surfacing promote cross-pollination among sub-communities.
- Visible, timely moderation reduces churn driven by toxicity and low-quality interactions.

Partnerships
- Universities/think tanks for expert onboarding and content syndication.
- Media partners for co-publishing/backlinks; podcasts/webinars for distribution.
- Professional associations to drive institutional report subscriptions.

Growth Requirements (EARS)
- THE pol-econ-board service SHALL publish at least 2 expert long-form pieces per week during the first 6 months post-launch.
- THE pol-econ-board service SHALL provide a referral mechanism attributing new sign-ups to referrers for reward calculation.
- WHERE a user follows a topic, THE pol-econ-board service SHALL include it in weekly digests and real-time alerts per preferences.
- WHEN an Expert publishes a new piece, THE pol-econ-board service SHALL notify eligible followers within 5 minutes.
- IF a reported item exceeds toxicity thresholds, THEN THE pol-econ-board service SHALL reduce its distribution pending moderation.
- WHERE partner co-publishing is active, THE pol-econ-board service SHALL include partner attribution and link-back in visible metadata.

```mermaid
  A["Expert Content"] --> B["Search & Social Traffic"]

```

## Operating Model & Cost Structure
People (Core Team, phased)
- Editorial & Curation: 1 Lead Editor, 1–2 Editors (phase 1); scale to 3–5 as volume grows.
- Moderation & Trust: 1 Lead Moderator, 2–4 Moderators; part-time experts for sensitive topics during election periods.
- Community & Growth: 1 Community Manager, 1 Growth PMM; contractor support for campaigns.
- Partnerships & Sales: 1 Partnerships Lead, 1 Sponsorship Sales, 1 Account Manager.
- Data & Insights: 1 Analyst for report production; scale to 2–3 with institutional demand.
- Compliance & Policy: shared counsel or part-time compliance officer; election-period escalation rota.

Tools (Business-Level)
- Content planning and editorial calendar; sponsorship CRM; analytics/attribution; billing/subscription management; moderation queue and transparency ledger; brand safety review tools.

Processes & SLAs
- Editorial Calendar: weekly planning and monthly thematic cycles.
- Sponsorship Review: brand fit and policy compliance approval before booking confirmation.
- Moderation SLA: actionable reports triaged within 4 hours during business hours; severe harm flagged within 60 minutes.
- Transparency: public monthly summary of moderation actions and sponsorship disclosures.

Costs (Business-Level Estimates)
- Fixed: core salaries, counsel retainer, core tools/licenses, brand and PR.
- Variable: content stipends, sponsorship fulfilment assets, payment processing fees, promotional spend, translation/transcription.

Illustrative Cost Structure (Phase 1–2)
| Category | Monthly Estimate (USD) | Notes |
|---------|-------------------------|-------|
| Editorial & Moderation | 45k–85k | Staffing and stipends |
| Community & Growth | 20k–40k | Campaigns and tools |
| Partnerships & Sales | 25k–50k | Base plus commission |
| Data & Insights | 12k–25k | Analyst and tooling |
| Compliance & Legal | 8k–20k | Counsel retainer and audits |
| Tools & Services | 10k–25k | Analytics, CRM, billing |
| Marketing & PR | 20k–60k | Launch, sponsorship promotion |
| Contingency (10%) | 14k–30k | Risk buffer |

Scale Triggers and Hiring Guardrails (EARS)
- WHEN weekly expert output exceeds 8 long-form pieces for 4 consecutive weeks, THE pol-econ-board service SHALL hire or contract editorial capacity within 30 days.
- WHEN moderation queues breach SLA for 2 consecutive weeks, THE pol-econ-board service SHALL add moderator shifts or capacity within 14 days.
- WHERE institutional report backlog exceeds 3 signed requests, THE pol-econ-board service SHALL allocate additional analyst capacity within 30 days.

Operational Requirements (EARS)
- THE pol-econ-board service SHALL enforce sponsorship labeling on all sponsored units without exception.
- THE pol-econ-board service SHALL provide exportable booking confirmations and insertion orders in human-readable formats.
- WHEN a moderation report is categorized as severe harm, THE pol-econ-board service SHALL route it to priority handling with a target response within 60 minutes during coverage hours.
- WHERE a campaign includes performance guarantees, THE pol-econ-board service SHALL provide delivery and pacing dashboards to business stakeholders.

## Regulatory & Policy Risks and Response Principles
Risk Categories (Business-Level)
- Political Advertising Compliance: restrictions on campaign/advocacy ads; jurisdictional differences, especially during election windows.
- Privacy & Data Protection: PIPA (Korea), GDPR-like regimes governing consent, minimization, and data subject rights.
- Defamation/Misinformation/Harmful Content: liability exposure from user claims; source labeling and editorial standards required.
- Copyright & Fair Use: excerpts, charts, external media usage.
- Market Integrity: sensitive financial claims and investment advice; require disclaimers and expert verification.

Mitigation Principles
- Prohibited categories and required disclosures explicitly listed and enforced.
- Documented moderation with appeal and transparency.
- Data minimization for monetization; aggregate-only insights for external reporting.
- Election-period special policies with heightened review and cooling-off rules.

Compliance Requirements (EARS)
- THE pol-econ-board service SHALL maintain a publicly accessible policy page describing sponsorship disclosure and prohibited categories.
- WHEN an election-period policy is active, THE pol-econ-board service SHALL apply additional review steps to content tagged as political campaign-related before amplification.
- IF a data subject requests access, THEN THE pol-econ-board service SHALL provide a human-readable summary of stored personal data and processing purposes within 30 days, aligned with applicable law.
- WHERE a Data Report is generated, THE pol-econ-board service SHALL ensure outputs meet aggregation thresholds that prevent re-identification (e.g., minimum cohort size of 100).
- IF a copyright complaint is received with required particulars, THEN THE pol-econ-board service SHALL de-list the content pending review and notify the uploader and complainant.
- WHERE regional political advertising is restricted, THE pol-econ-board service SHALL block such bookings and provide rationale to requesters.

## Success Metrics & Monitoring
Financial KPIs
- Revenue Mix: Ads 25–40%, Sponsorships 25–35%, Premium 20–35%, Data Reports 10–20% by month 18.
- MRR: USD 150k+ by month 18; growth 8–12% MoM during months 6–12, 5–8% thereafter.
- ARPU (paid): USD 8–12 monthly; Churn (paid): < 4% monthly; Refund rate < 2% of monthly billings.

User & Growth KPIs
- MAU: 250k by month 18; DAU/MAU: 18–27%.
- Activation: ≥ 35% of new sign-ups reach first follow and first interaction within 7 days.
- D30 Retention: ≥ 25% Members; ≥ 40% Experts.
- Premium Conversion: 2.0–3.5% of active Members by month 12; annual plan share ≥ 35% of paid subs.

Content Quality & Safety KPIs
- Expert Ratio: ≥ 20% of front-page content from Experts.
- Moderation SLA: ≥ 90% of severe reports handled within 60 minutes during coverage hours; ≥ 80% of general reports within 4 hours.
- Transparency: monthly moderation report published 100% of months.
- Takedown Accuracy: appeal uphold rate between 10–25%.

Sponsorship & Ads Performance KPIs
- Sponsorship Fulfillment: ≥ 95% delivery to booked placements; labeled 100% of time.
- Ad UX: average ads per session ≤ 3; complaint rate < 0.05% of sessions; invalid traffic rate < 2% of ad impressions.

Data Report KPIs
- Institutional Accounts: 20–60 by month 18; renewal rate ≥ 75%.
- Report Production SLA: deliver quarterly updates within 10 business days of quarter close; on-time rate ≥ 95%.

KPI Guardrails and Triggers (EARS)
- IF paid churn exceeds 4% for 2 consecutive months, THEN THE pol-econ-board service SHALL initiate a retention review and pause price increases until churn normalizes.
- WHEN ad complaint rate exceeds 0.05% of sessions in a week, THE pol-econ-board service SHALL reduce ad load by 20% the following week and assess placements.
- WHERE expert content share drops below 15% for a month, THE pol-econ-board service SHALL allocate additional expert commissioning budget the next month.
- IF invalid traffic on ads exceeds 2% for a week, THEN THE pol-econ-board service SHALL enable stricter delivery filters and inform sponsors/advertisers.

Monitoring & Cadence
- Weekly dashboards for growth and engagement; monthly financial close; quarterly planning reviews.
- Named owners: Growth PMM (acquisition), Lead Editor (content quality), Lead Moderator (safety), Partnerships Lead (sponsorship), Analyst (reports), Finance (revenue/margin).

KPI Table (Illustrative Targets)
| KPI | Phase 1 (0–6 mo) | Phase 2 (6–12 mo) | Phase 3 (12–18 mo) |
|-----|-------------------|-------------------|--------------------|
| MAU | 50k | 150k | 250k |
| DAU/MAU | 15–20% | 18–25% | 20–27% |
| Paid Conversion | 0.8–1.5% | 1.5–2.5% | 2.0–3.5% |
| MRR | 20–40k | 60–110k | 150k+ |
| Expert Content Share | 10% | 15% | 20% |
| Severe Report SLA | 80% | 85% | 90% |

## Business Requirements (EARS) Summary
Monetization
- THE pol-econ-board service SHALL limit default ad load to ad-light parameters and enforce frequency capping as defined.
- WHEN a user upgrades to Premium, THE pol-econ-board service SHALL apply entitlements immediately and persist for the subscription term.
- WHERE sponsorship units are booked, THE pol-econ-board service SHALL guarantee visible disclosure at unit start and in listings.
- WHEN a refund is approved, THE pol-econ-board service SHALL revoke premium entitlements and adjust access within 1 hour.

Growth & Content
- THE pol-econ-board service SHALL maintain a weekly editorial cadence with at least 2 expert long-form pieces and 1 digest.
- WHEN a user follows a topic, THE pol-econ-board service SHALL include it in digests and notifications per preferences.

Safety & Compliance
- THE pol-econ-board service SHALL maintain public policy documentation and update transparency logs monthly.
- IF content is flagged as high risk during election periods, THEN THE pol-econ-board service SHALL require elevated review before promotion.

Data & Reporting
- WHERE Data Reports are offered, THE pol-econ-board service SHALL use aggregation thresholds that prevent re-identification and exclude personal data.
- WHEN an institutional subscription lapses, THE pol-econ-board service SHALL revoke access to new report releases while preserving prior entitlements per contract terms.

Operational
- THE pol-econ-board service SHALL publish monthly sponsorship and moderation disclosure summaries accessible to users.
- WHEN moderation or sponsorship complaints are validated, THE pol-econ-board service SHALL implement corrective actions within 5 business days.

## Scope of This Document
Business requirements only. Technical implementation decisions (architecture, APIs, database design, encryption, infrastructure) are at the discretion of the development team; the content specifies measurable policies, SLAs, and KPIs.

References
- For overall vision and scope, see the [Service Overview for pol-econ-board](./01-pol-econ-board-service-overview.md).
- For governance and moderation standards, see the [Community Governance and Moderation Requirements](./07-pol-econ-board-community-governance-and-moderation.md).
- For security and compliance principles, see the [Security and Compliance Requirements](./09-pol-econ-board-security-and-compliance.md).

# 03-pol-econ-board-user-roles-and-authentication

## Scope and Intent
Defines business requirements for authentication, authorization, and role-based access control of the service prefix "pol-econ-board". Describes WHAT must happen in business terms; technical implementation decisions (architecture, APIs, database design, libraries, infrastructure) remain with the development team.

## Authentication Requirements Overview
- THE system SHALL support the full account lifecycle: registration, email verification, login, logout, password change, password reset, and session/device management.
- THE system SHALL enforce role-based authorization for roles: guest (unauthenticated), member, expert, moderator, editor, admin.
- THE system SHALL use JWT for access control with short-lived access tokens and longer-lived refresh tokens.
- THE system SHALL record key authentication and authorization events for audit and security monitoring.
- THE system SHALL operate default business time references in Asia/Seoul (KST) while respecting user-preferred locales for communications.

## Account Lifecycle: Registration, Email Verification, Login, Logout, Password Reset/Change

### Registration
- WHEN a user attempts to register with email and password, THE system SHALL validate inputs against password policy and email format rules.
- WHEN registration succeeds, THE system SHALL place the account in "pending_verification" state and require email ownership confirmation before enabling content interactions.
- WHERE invitation-based or role elevation flows are used (e.g., expert candidates), THE system SHALL create the account as member and perform elevation post-verification and review.

Input validation (business rules)
- THE system SHALL require email in valid format containing a single "@", domain with at least one dot, and a TLD of 2–24 letters.
- THE system SHALL reject disposable or blocked domains per policy-maintained lists.
- THE system SHALL require password length ≥ 10 and at least 2 of the following classes: uppercase, lowercase, number, symbol; alternatively, passphrases ≥ 16 characters MAY include spaces with no additional class requirements.
- THE system SHALL reject passwords present in the common-passwords list and those derived from the user’s personal identifiers (email local part, display name) with trivial mutations.

### Email Verification
- WHEN a registration is submitted, THE system SHALL send a verification message containing a single-use token.
- THE system SHALL set verification tokens to expire in 30 minutes and be one-time use.
- WHILE an account is unverified, THE system SHALL permit read-only public access and profile completion while blocking posting, commenting, voting, reporting, following, and reporting.
- IF a verification token is expired or invalid, THEN THE system SHALL present a clear error and SHALL allow requesting a new token up to 3 times per 24 hours.
- WHEN an email address is changed on an existing account, THE system SHALL re-verify ownership of the new address and restrict sensitive actions until verification completes.

### Login
- WHEN a user submits email and password, THE system SHALL validate credentials and respond within 2 seconds at P95 under normal load.
- IF credentials are valid and the account is in good standing, THEN THE system SHALL create a session and issue access and refresh tokens embedding role and permissions.
- IF the account is suspended, THEN THE system SHALL deny login and present the suspension reason and remaining duration where policy allows disclosure.
- WHERE multi-factor authentication (MFA) is enabled by policy or user preference, THE system SHALL require a second factor (e.g., code or approved action) before issuing tokens.
- WHEN a user opts for "remember this device" within policy, THE system SHALL mark the device session as trusted and reduce MFA prompts for 30 days unless risk signals require step-up authentication.

### Logout
- WHEN a user initiates logout, THE system SHALL invalidate the active access token and detach it from the corresponding refresh token chain for that device within 60 seconds.
- WHEN the user selects "log out from all devices", THE system SHALL revoke all active sessions and refresh tokens associated with the account within 60 seconds.

### Password Reset and Change
- WHEN a user requests password reset, THE system SHALL send a one-time reset token that expires in 30 minutes and is invalidated upon use.
- WHEN a user completes password reset, THE system SHALL invalidate all existing sessions and refresh tokens and require login with the new password.
- WHEN a user changes password from a logged-in state, THE system SHALL prompt for current password re-authentication and SHALL invalidate all refresh tokens while allowing the current access token to expire on schedule unless policy requires immediate revocation.
- WHERE password reset attempts exceed policy thresholds, THE system SHALL apply rate limits and communicate the next eligible time.

## Account States and Transitions
States: pending_verification, active, suspended_temporary, suspended_permanent, disabled_security, deleted_pending, deleted_final.

- THE system SHALL maintain a canonical account state and update it atomically.
- WHEN email verification completes successfully, THE system SHALL transition state from pending_verification to active immediately.
- WHEN a temporary suspension is applied, THE system SHALL set state to suspended_temporary with an end timestamp and block new sessions until expiry or lift.
- WHEN a permanent suspension is applied, THE system SHALL set state to suspended_permanent and block all sessions indefinitely unless reversed by admin.
- WHEN a security incident necessitates protection, THE system SHALL set state to disabled_security and require remediation (e.g., password reset, step-up verification) prior to reactivation.
- WHEN an account deletion request is confirmed after cooling-off, THE system SHALL transition to deleted_final and block authentication permanently.
- IF a suspension period expires, THEN THE system SHALL switch the account back to active and restore login capability.
- WHILE an appeal is pending under governance policy, THE system SHALL preserve the current enforcement state until the appeal outcome.

## Session and Token Management (JWT) Principles
- THE system SHALL issue JWT access tokens with a lifetime of 20 minutes and refresh tokens with a lifetime of 14 days.
- THE system SHALL rotate refresh tokens on every use and SHALL invalidate the previous token immediately after rotation.
- THE system SHALL detect refresh token reuse and SHALL revoke the entire refresh token family upon detection, requiring re-authentication.
- THE system SHALL embed in JWT payload at minimum: userId, role, a permissions array, issued-at time, expiration time; optional claims MAY include trust level, verified status, and badges when relevant to business logic.
- WHERE audience, issuer, and token purpose distinctions are required for business control, THE system SHALL include business-identifying claims sufficient for environment isolation and contract-level enforcement.
- IF a user’s role or permissions change, THEN THE system SHALL invalidate all active refresh tokens within 60 seconds and require token re-issuance under the new role.
- WHERE device-level session tracking is enabled, THE system SHALL allow users to view active device sessions (device label, approximate location, last activity) and revoke individual sessions.
- IF suspicious activity is detected on a session (impossible travel, abnormal IP/device velocity per policy), THEN THE system SHALL flag the session and require step-up verification prior to continued access.
- WHERE client storage policy applies, THE system SHALL support secure storage of tokens with preference for httpOnly cookies; localStorage MAY be used where acceptable by policy. Developers retain discretion on exact mechanism.
- THE system SHALL maintain a business-level key rotation policy for the JWT signing keys, including dual-publish windows, scheduled rotations at least every 180 days, and emergency rotation capability within 24 hours of incident declaration.
- WHERE session concurrency policy applies, THE system SHALL limit simultaneous active device sessions per user to 10 by default (admin-configurable) and SHALL deny creation of additional sessions beyond the limit with guidance to revoke existing sessions.

## Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) Policy (Business Level)
- WHERE MFA is mandated by policy or user opt-in, THE system SHALL support at least one possession factor and SHALL allow recovery paths that balance security and usability.
- WHEN a sensitive action occurs (password change, email change, role elevation, global sign-out), THE system SHALL require step-up verification if MFA is enabled or risk signals are present.
- IF repeated high-risk signals are detected within 24 hours (e.g., 3+ impossible-travel detections), THEN THE system SHALL enforce MFA on next login even for trusted devices.

## Role Definitions and Permission Descriptions
JWT payloads MUST include role and a permissions array reflecting granted actions. Permissions are expressed in business terms and enforced per matrix below.

### Guest (Unauthenticated)
- Read-only access to public content and search public posts.
- Cannot create content, vote, react, report, or follow.

### Member
- Registered participant (real name or alias). May create/edit/delete own posts and comments, report content, bookmark, follow topics/users, vote/react, and manage notifications. Subject to governance enforcement.
- Typical permissions: ["post:create", "post:edit:own", "post:delete:own", "comment:create", "comment:edit:own", "comment:delete:own", "report:create", "bookmark:create", "follow:create", "vote:create", "notify:manage", "profile:edit"]

### Expert
- Verified political/economic domain expert. Inherits member permissions; may display expert badge, propose expert-only topics, publish deep-dive research/insight posts, and participate in expert Q&A.
- Additional permissions: ["topic:propose:expert", "post:create:insight", "qa:expert:participate", "badge:expert"]

### Moderator
- Community operations. Access report queue, temporarily hide/delete content, request user sanctions (warning/suspension), mediate disputes, manage transparency logs.
- Additional permissions: ["report:queue:read", "content:hide", "content:delete", "sanction:request", "dispute:mediate", "transparency:manage"]

### Editor
- Content quality and curation. Edit tags/topics, manage announcements/pinned posts, operate featured selections. Collaborates with moderators on violations.
- Additional permissions: ["topic:edit", "curation:feature", "announcement:manage", "pin:manage"]

### Admin
- Organization-wide operations. Full access to all resources, role management, policy/settings changes, legal request workflow, service health/metrics oversight, audit review.
- Additional permissions: ["role:manage", "policy:manage", "sanction:execute", "audit:read", "system:metrics:read", "legal:request:manage", "session:revoke:any"]

## Permission Matrix (Role × Action)

|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| View public content | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| Search public posts | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| Create standard post | ❌ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| Create deep-dive insight post | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| Edit own post (within policy window) | ❌ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| Delete own post | ❌ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| Create comment | ❌ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| Edit own comment | ❌ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| Delete own comment | ❌ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| Vote/React on content | ❌ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| Report content | ❌ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| Bookmark content | ❌ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| Follow topic/user | ❌ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| Propose expert-only topic | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| Edit topics/tags | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ | ✅ |
| Curate featured collections | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ | ✅ |

| Temporarily hide content | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ | ❌ | ✅ |
| Delete content (moderation remove) | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ | ❌ | ✅ |
| Issue user warning (execute) | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ |
| Request user suspension | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ | ❌ | ✅ |
| Execute user suspension | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ |

| Manage roles | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ |
| Change policies/settings | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ |
| Access audit logs | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ |
| View service health metrics | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ |

| View own sessions | ❌ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |

Notes:
- Moderators request account-level sanctions; admins execute irreversible sanctions.
- Experts add publishing and proposal capabilities beyond members; no moderation powers.

## Policies: Password Rules, Login Attempt Limits, Account Suspension/Unlock, Device Logout, MFA

### Password Rules
- THE system SHALL enforce minimum password length of 10 and the defined complexity rules.
- THE system SHALL permit passphrases ≥ 16 characters without additional complexity requirements.
- IF a password is found in a banned list or derived from personal identifiers, THEN THE system SHALL reject it with guidance to choose a stronger password.
- WHEN a password is changed or reset, THE system SHALL require re-authentication for sensitive actions for the next 5 minutes.

### Login Attempt Limits and Abuse Prevention
- THE system SHALL allow up to 5 failed login attempts per account per rolling 15 minutes before temporary lockout.
- IF the threshold is exceeded, THEN THE system SHALL lock the account for 15 minutes and SHALL send an advisory notice to the account email.
- WHERE suspicious velocity or credential stuffing is detected, THE system SHALL apply adaptive throttling and MAY require additional verification.
- THE system SHALL reset failure counters upon successful login.

### Account Suspension and Unlock
- WHEN a moderator submits a suspension request with reason codes and proposed duration, THE system SHALL route it for admin execution and log the decision.
- WHEN an admin executes a suspension, THE system SHALL immediately revoke all sessions and block new sessions until the suspension ends or is lifted.
- IF the suspension period expires, THEN THE system SHALL automatically restore login capability and flag the account for post-suspension review where policy requires.
- WHERE an appeal is in progress per governance policy, THE system SHALL maintain the current enforcement state until the appeal outcome.

### Device Logout and Session Visibility
- THE system SHALL provide users a list of active sessions including device label, approximate location (city/country), and last activity timestamp.
- WHEN a user revokes a specific session, THE system SHALL invalidate the corresponding refresh token and any derived access tokens within 60 seconds.
- WHEN a user selects "log out from all devices", THE system SHALL revoke all active sessions and refresh tokens within 60 seconds and confirm completion.

### MFA Application Rules
- THE system SHALL provide MFA enrollment and backup/recovery options (e.g., backup codes) with rate-limited retrieval.
- WHEN MFA is enabled, THE system SHALL require step-up verification for high-risk actions (password/email change, role elevation, global sign-out, viewing audit logs where role permits).

## Error Handling and Recovery (Auth-Specific)
- IF login fails due to invalid credentials, THEN THE system SHALL present a generic failure message without disclosing whether the email exists.
- IF login fails due to unverified email, THEN THE system SHALL allow immediate resend of verification up to the daily resend limit.
- IF login is blocked due to account suspension, THEN THE system SHALL present suspension status and policy-based guidance.
- IF a password reset token is invalid or expired, THEN THE system SHALL explain the issue and allow requesting a new token subject to rate limits.
- IF token refresh fails due to reuse or rotation violation, THEN THE system SHALL revoke the refresh token family and require re-authentication.
- WHEN system-side anomalies affect authentication, THE system SHALL provide status messaging and reference codes for support without exposing internals.

## Performance and Rate-Limiting Expectations
- THE system SHALL complete credential validation and token issuance within 2 seconds at P95 under normal load.
- THE system SHALL deliver verification and reset emails within 60 seconds at P95 under normal load.
- THE system SHALL support at least 10 token refreshes per user per hour without degradation, subject to normal rate-limits.
- WHERE global traffic protection is necessary, THE system SHALL enforce per-IP and per-account rate limits for registration, login, verification, and reset actions per policy thresholds.

## Audit and Security Considerations (Business Perspective)
- THE system SHALL maintain audit records for registration, verification, login success/failure, logout, token refresh, token revocation, password change/reset, role/permission change, suspension requests and executions, MFA enrollment/usage, and device trust changes.
- THE system SHALL ensure audit records include: actor (userId or system), action, timestamp, business context (e.g., device label, approximate location), and outcome (success/failure).
- THE system SHALL align event retention with the data lifecycle policy and ensure data minimization and pseudonymization where feasible.
- THE system SHALL enable authorized reviewers (admin; limited moderator scope) to access relevant audit views while honoring least privilege.
- IF anomalous authentication patterns are detected, THEN THE system SHALL generate security alerts for review and MAY trigger protective measures (step-up authentication, temporary locks).
- THE system SHALL support JWT signing key rotation according to policy with auditable activation timestamps and approver roles.

## Mermaid Diagram: Authentication and Token Flow
```mermaid
graph LR
  subgraph "User Authentication Flow"
    A["Start(Login)"] --> B["Validate Input"]
    B --> C{"Credentials Valid?"}
    C -->|"Yes"| D["Check Account State"]
    C -->|"No"| E["Show Generic Failure"]
    D --> F{"MFA Required?"}
    F -->|"Yes"| G["Perform Second Factor"]
    F -->|"No"| H["Issue Tokens"]
    G --> I{"Success?"}
    I -->|"Yes"| H
    I -->|"No"| E
  end

  subgraph "Token Management"
    H --> J["Access Token(20m)"]
    H --> K["Refresh Token(14d)"]
    K --> L["Rotate On Use"]
    L --> M{"Rotation Valid?"}
    M -->|"Yes"| N["Issue New Pair"]
    M -->|"No"| O["Revoke Family & Re-auth"]
  end

  subgraph "Security Responses"
    D --> P{"Suspended?"}
    P -->|"Yes"| Q["Deny Login & Notify"]
    P -->|"No"| F
    K -.-> R["Revoke All Sessions"]
  end
```

## Mermaid Diagram: Role Elevation and Sanction Workflow (Business Level)
```mermaid
graph LR
  subgraph "Role Elevation"
    A1["Member Submits Expert Verification"] --> A2["Collect Evidence & Validate"]
    A2 --> A3{"Meets Criteria?"}
    A3 -->|"Yes"| A4["Admin Assigns Expert Role"]
    A3 -->|"No"| A5["Reject with Rationale"]
    A4 --> A6["Revoke Refresh Tokens"]
    A6 --> A7["Require Re-Authentication"]
  end

  subgraph "Sanction Flow"
    B1["Moderator Submits Sanction Request"] --> B2["Admin Reviews"]
    B2 --> B3{"Approve?"}
    B3 -->|"Yes"| B4["Execute Suspension"]
    B3 -->|"No"| B5["Return with Guidance"]
    B4 --> B6["Revoke All Sessions"]
    B4 --> B7["Notify User & Log"]
  end
```

## EARS-Formatted Detailed Requirements

### Ubiquitous Requirements
- THE authentication service SHALL require email verification before enabling content creation or interaction actions.
- THE authorization service SHALL enforce role-based permissions as defined in the Permission Matrix.
- THE token service SHALL issue access tokens with 20-minute lifetime and refresh tokens with 14-day lifetime.
- THE security service SHALL maintain audit logs for all authentication and authorization events listed in this file.
- THE risk service SHALL evaluate session signals and require step-up verification under suspicious conditions.

### Event-Driven Requirements
- WHEN a user registers, THE system SHALL send a verification message containing a single-use token that expires in 30 minutes.
- WHEN a user logs in successfully, THE system SHALL bind the session to a device identifier and record last activity time.
- WHEN a user logs out, THE system SHALL invalidate the active session within 60 seconds.
- WHEN a refresh token is presented, THE system SHALL rotate it and invalidate the prior token.
- WHEN a role is elevated (e.g., member → expert), THE system SHALL revoke existing refresh tokens and require re-authentication.
- WHEN a moderator submits a sanction request, THE system SHALL route it for admin decision and log the outcome.
- WHEN a user changes email address, THE system SHALL require verification of the new address before enabling sensitive actions.
- WHEN a user enables MFA, THE system SHALL prompt for a second factor during login and sensitive actions.

### State-Driven Requirements
- WHILE an account remains unverified, THE system SHALL restrict the account to read-only public access and profile completion.
- WHILE an account is under active suspension, THE system SHALL block login and token issuance.
- WHILE an appeal is pending per governance policy, THE system SHALL preserve the current enforcement state.
- WHILE a device session is marked trusted, THE system SHALL suppress MFA prompts unless risk signals are present.

### Unwanted Behavior Requirements
- IF a login attempt fails, THEN THE system SHALL present a generic error without confirming account existence.
- IF failed login attempts exceed 5 within 15 minutes, THEN THE system SHALL lock the account for 15 minutes and log the event.
- IF a refresh token reuse is detected, THEN THE system SHALL revoke the entire token family and require re-authentication.
- IF impossible travel or anomalous activity is detected, THEN THE system SHALL require step-up verification before issuing tokens.
- IF a password reset token is expired or invalid, THEN THE system SHALL deny the reset and allow a new request within policy limits.
- IF session concurrency exceeds the allowed limit, THEN THE system SHALL deny additional session creation and advise revocation of older sessions.

### Optional Features Requirements
- WHERE multi-factor authentication is enabled, THE system SHALL require a second factor during login and sensitive actions.
- WHERE device session visibility is enabled, THE system SHALL display active sessions and allow revocation by the user.
- WHERE organization policy mandates httpOnly cookies, THE system SHALL store tokens in secure cookies rather than other storage options.
- WHERE trusted device preference is enabled, THE system SHALL reduce MFA prompts for trusted sessions for up to 30 days.

## Business Rules and Validation Details
- Email format: must include "@" and a domain containing at least one dot; TLD length 2–24; reject blocked domains.
- Password: minimum length 10; at least 2 character classes unless passphrase ≥ 16; reject common and personal-info-based passwords.
- Display names: prohibited from impersonating public figures or organizations per governance policy.
- Verification/resets: tokens are single-use, expire in 30 minutes, and are rate-limited to 3 sends per 24 hours per account.
- Sensitive changes (email, password): require re-authentication within the past 5 minutes.

## Success Criteria and KPIs (Auth Scope)
- Email verification completion rate ≥ 90% within 24 hours of registration under normal operations.
- Login response time ≤ 2 seconds at P95 under normal load.
- Password reset email delivery ≤ 60 seconds at P95.
- Security alert false-positive rate ≤ 5% after tuning.
- Token reuse detection time ≤ 5 seconds from event to enforcement.

## Dependencies and References
- Community sanctions, appeals, and transparency align with the [Community Governance and Moderation Requirements](./07-pol-econ-board-community-governance-and-moderation.md).
- Privacy, data rights, and legal compliance align with the [Security and Compliance Requirements](./09-pol-econ-board-security-and-compliance.md).
- Functional behaviors that invoke auth decisions align with the [Functional Requirements Specification](./04-pol-econ-board-functional-requirements.md).

## Implementation Autonomy Statement
Business requirements only. All technical implementation decisions, including architecture, API design, database structure, cryptography choices, and infrastructure, are owned by the development team; the content defines WHAT must occur, not HOW to implement it.
