# pol-econ-board Functional Requirements

Complete, business-level functional requirements for the pol-econ-board service written in EARS where applicable. Content focuses on WHAT the system must do and excludes architecture, API shapes, database schemas, and infrastructure details. Developers retain full autonomy over technical implementation.

Align authentication, authorization, and roles with the [User Roles and Authentication Requirements](./03-pol-econ-board-user-roles-and-authentication.md). Refer to flows in the [User Flows and Process Diagrams](./06-pol-econ-board-user-flows.md). Apply governance and sanctions from the [Community Governance and Moderation Requirements](./07-pol-econ-board-community-governance-and-moderation.md). Connect business events to delivery rules in the [Notifications and Communications Requirements](./11-pol-econ-board-notifications-and-communications.md).

## 1) Purpose and Scope
- Define the full set of functional capabilities required for a moderated, expertise-forward political and economic discussion platform.
- Establish business rules, input validation, processing logic, outputs, performance expectations, error handling, and role-based constraints.
- Cover member-generated content, expert contributions, editorial curation, moderation workflows, personalization, search, subscriptions, and notification triggers.

## 2) Terminology and Global Conventions
- Timezone: Business time windows and SLAs use Asia/Seoul (KST). User-facing times SHALL respect the user’s configured local timezone where preferences exist.
- Counting windows: Unless stated otherwise, rate limits use rolling 60-minute windows for per-hour metrics and rolling 24-hour windows for daily metrics.
- Content policy baseline: Content behaviors defer to the [Community Governance and Moderation Requirements](./07-pol-econ-board-community-governance-and-moderation.md).
- Performance baseline: Unless specified, simple actions (create/edit/delete/like/bookmark/follow) SHALL complete within 2 seconds for the user; discovery actions (search/filter/sort) SHALL respond within 1 second for common queries and within 3 seconds for complex queries under typical load.
- Content states: Draft (private to author and reviewers where applicable); Published (visible per visibility rules); Hidden (system- or moderator-suppressed); Soft-Hidden (limited visibility, e.g., author and direct participants only); Archived (excluded from default feeds but still accessible as defined herein).
- Versioning: Each published edit creates an immutable version that can be viewed in comparisons.
- Visibility levels (business): Public; Limited (followers or invited audiences where configured); Staff-only (moderators/editors/admins).

## 3) Role Context (Business Perspective)
- member: Create and manage own posts and comments; react, follow, bookmark, report, and block; subject to rate limits and policy.
- expert: All member privileges plus expert badge, expert-only topic proposals, long-form research/insight posts, expert Q&A participation, expert recommendation signals.
- moderator: Review reports, hide/delete content per policy, request sanctions, manage disputes, maintain transparency logs.
- editor: Curate categories and tags, manage featured content, announcements, and pins; collaborate with moderators on policy issues.
- admin: Oversight of roles, policies, legal requests, and service health.

Role-based constraints per feature are embedded in the sections below. The full role model and JWT principles reside in the [User Roles and Authentication Requirements](./03-pol-econ-board-user-roles-and-authentication.md).

---

## 4) Functional Requirements (EARS)

### 4.1) Post Management (Create/Edit/Delete/Version)
Business fields (business-level, not schema):
- Title (4–120 characters)
- Body (≥ 20 characters for published posts; drafts may be shorter but must be non-empty)
- Attachments (0–10 files; each ≤ 25 MB; types: image, PDF, CSV; videos only when explicitly enabled)
- Category (exactly one controlled value)
- Tags (0–5; profanity/ban list filtered; each 1–30 characters)
- Visibility (public/limited/staff-only)
- Source links (0–10; valid URLs)
- Content warnings (0–3 from predefined list)
- Estimated reading time (auto-calculated)
- Language (e.g., Korean, English)

Validation and creation
- WHEN a user submits a new post as draft, THE system SHALL validate title length 4–120 characters, body length ≥ 1 character for drafts and ≥ 20 characters for publication, and allowed attachment count/size/types.
- WHEN a user saves a draft, THE system SHALL persist within 2 seconds and return the draft identifier and last-saved timestamp.
- WHEN a user attempts to publish, THE system SHALL require Category and enforce at least one source link for “analysis/research” post types.
- WHERE the user role is member, THE system SHALL allow publishing up to 10 posts per 24 hours.
- WHERE the user role is expert, THE system SHALL allow publishing up to 20 posts per 24 hours and permit “long-form” flag up to 20,000 characters body.
- WHERE the user role is moderator or editor, THE system SHALL allow staff-only posts without public visibility for operational notices.

Editing and versioning
- WHEN an author edits a published post, THE system SHALL create a new immutable version and retain prior versions for comparison.
- WHERE edits occur within 10 minutes of publication, THE system SHALL allow “silent update” without feed bump; after 10 minutes, feed bump SHALL occur unless staff marks “no-bump”.
- WHILE a post is draft, THE system SHALL allow unlimited edits and autosave at least every 30 seconds of active typing.

Deletion and restoration
- WHEN an author deletes own post, THE system SHALL soft-delete and hide from public while retaining for 30 days for potential restoration.
- IF a soft-deleted post is restored within 30 days, THEN THE system SHALL reinstate its visibility and maintain version history continuity.
- IF a post is under active investigation (flagged), THEN THE system SHALL prevent author deletion until moderation completes or staff override is recorded.

Integrity and policy checks
- WHEN a post contains more than 3 external links, THE system SHALL flag it for automated spam review without blocking publication unless thresholds are exceeded (see §4.7).
- WHERE content includes media attachments, THE system SHALL require a text alternative (caption/alt-text) per accessibility requirements (§4.13).
- IF a post violates rate limits or is under sanction, THEN THE system SHALL deny publishing with a clear reason and next eligible time.

Outputs
- THE system SHALL return identifiers, timestamps (created/updated/published), current visibility, version number, moderation status, and derived signals (e.g., estimated reading time) upon create/edit/publish.

Performance
- THE post save or publish operation SHALL complete within 2 seconds under nominal load for text-only posts; within 5 seconds when up to 10 attachments are included.

Edge constraints
- WHERE mentions in the post body exceed 20 unique users, THE system SHALL block publication and instruct the author to reduce mass-mentions per anti-abuse policy.
- WHERE tags include banned terms, THE system SHALL reject publication with a policy-aligned reason code.

### 4.2) Comments, Replies, Mentions
Scope
- Comments support one level of replies (reply-to-comment). Mentions use “@handle” of users with public mentionability.

Validation and creation
- WHEN a user submits a comment, THE system SHALL validate length 1–5,000 characters and disallow empty or media-only comments.
- WHERE the role is member or expert, THE system SHALL allow up to 60 comments per 24 hours.
- WHEN a reply is created, THE system SHALL associate it with the parent comment and the post thread.
- WHEN a user mentions another user, THE system SHALL validate mention permissions and block interactions with users who are blocked by or have blocked the author.
- WHERE a single comment attempts to mention more than 10 distinct users, THE system SHALL block submission and return a mass-mention limit message.

Editing and deletion
- WHERE the author is the comment owner, THE system SHALL allow edits for 15 minutes with an edit marker displayed thereafter.
- WHEN the author deletes a comment, THE system SHALL soft-delete and replace with a placeholder indicating removal.

Abuse and policy
- IF a comment triggers prohibited content rules, THEN THE system SHALL route it to moderation queues and may auto-hide according to §4.7 thresholds.

Notifications
- WHEN a user is mentioned, THE system SHALL enqueue a mention notification per preferences (§4.11).

Outputs and performance
- THE system SHALL return identifiers, parent linkage, timestamps, mention list, and moderation status for created comments.
- THE comment create/edit/delete operation SHALL complete within 1 second for text-only content.

### 4.3) Categories, Tags, Topic Follow
Categories and tags
- WHEN a post is published, THE system SHALL require exactly one Category from the controlled list managed by editors.
- WHERE tags are provided, THE system SHALL allow up to 5 free-form tags validated against profanity/ban lists and length 1–30 characters.
- WHEN editors modify category definitions, THE system SHALL preserve historical category labels on existing posts while applying new taxonomy prospectively.

Topic follow
- WHEN a user follows a topic (category/tag or editor-curated topic), THE system SHALL add it to the user’s subscription list.
- WHERE a user follows a topic, THE system SHALL prioritize that topic in personalized feeds (§4.10).
- IF a followed topic is deprecated, THEN THE system SHALL notify followers and suggest alternatives; migrations SHALL preserve user preferences with user-confirmable mapping.

### 4.4) Votes, Reactions, Recommendations
Vote and reaction types
- Votes support “Agree” and “Disagree”. Reactions support “Insightful”, “Question”, “Source requested”, and “Appreciation”.

Constraints
- WHERE a user is authenticated, THE system SHALL allow one vote per post per user with ability to change the choice; reactions are one per type per user per post.
- WHERE the actor is expert, THE system SHALL allow an “Expert Recommend” marker distinct from general reactions.
- IF a post is archived or hidden, THEN THE system SHALL block new votes/reactions while preserving counts.

Outputs and display rules (business)
- WHEN counts are requested for display, THE system SHALL provide totals and expert-specific counts to enable separate labeling.
- WHILE reaction/vote updates propagate, THE system SHALL maintain eventual consistency with staleness ≤ 3 seconds under normal load.

Performance
- THE system SHALL record a vote or reaction within 1 second and reflect updated counts within 2 seconds in dependent views.

Anti-abuse
- WHERE a single account submits >10 reactions within 10 seconds, THE system SHALL delay further reactions for 30 seconds (§4.12).

### 4.5) Bookmarks, Read State, Saved Items
- WHEN a user bookmarks a post, THE system SHALL store it in the user’s bookmarks and allow foldering into up to 20 named collections (collection name 1–40 characters, profanity filtered).
- WHILE a user scrolls through a post, THE system SHALL track read progress and mark as “read” when ≥ 80% of body is viewed or ≥ 10 seconds of engaged reading elapse, whichever comes later.
- WHEN a user saves a post for offline reading (business concept), THE system SHALL store a snapshot of the text and metadata for later retrieval; media may be excluded depending on rights.
- WHERE the user requests export of saved items, THE system SHALL prepare an export within 10 seconds for up to 100 items and provide a durable link or retrieval reference.
- IF a bookmarked item is deleted or becomes private, THEN THE system SHALL retain a placeholder with permissible metadata and indicate unavailability.

### 4.6) Search, Sort, Filter
Inputs and validation
- WHEN a user searches, THE system SHALL accept queries up to 200 characters, with logical operators AND/OR and quoted phrases.
- WHERE filters are applied, THE system SHALL support Category, Tags, Author, Role (expert only), Date range, Content type (post/comment), Minimum reaction score, and Moderation status (staff roles only).
- WHERE sorting is applied, THE system SHALL support Newest, Oldest, Most reacted, and Most agreed.

Processing and outputs
- WHEN a search is executed, THE system SHALL return results with total matches and page data in pages of 20 items for posts and 50 items for comments, including key metadata (title/excerpt/author/category/timestamps/reaction summaries/visibility state as appropriate).

Performance
- THE system SHALL return common query results within 1 second and complex multi-filter queries within 3 seconds under typical load.

Safety and integrity
- IF a query triggers sensitive or election-period rules, THEN THE system SHALL elevate checks per governance policy and annotate affected results with compliance labels where applicable.

### 4.7) Reporting, Blocking, and Automation Rules
Reporting
- WHEN a user reports content, THE system SHALL require a reason category (e.g., Misinformation, Harassment, Hate, Spam, Off-topic, Illegal) and an optional note up to 500 characters.
- WHERE a single content item receives ≥ 5 reports within 1 hour, THE system SHALL flag it for expedited review.

Auto-hide thresholds
- WHERE reports ≥ 20 from distinct users within 3 hours OR a weighted score threshold is exceeded (expert reports count as 2), THE system SHALL auto-hide the content pending review.
- IF auto-hide is triggered, THEN THE system SHALL notify the author and provide an appeal link to the dispute workflow.

Blocking
- WHEN a user blocks another user, THE system SHALL hide the blocker’s view of the blockee’s content and prevent mentions and direct interactions between them.
- WHILE a block is active, THE system SHALL suppress notifications originating from the blocked user to the blocker.

Staff workflows
- WHEN content is auto-hidden or reported beyond thresholds, THE system SHALL place it into the moderation queue with metadata: report counts by category, timestamps, involved users, and preliminary risk assessment.

Rate-limits on reporting
- WHERE the user files reports, THE system SHALL limit to 30 reports per 24 hours.

### 4.8) Draft, Review, Publish Workflow
States
- Draft → Submitted for Review (optional) → Published → Updated (versioned) → Archived/Hidden.

Rules
- WHERE the author is expert and the post is marked as “long-form research”, THE system SHALL require either editor review or source completeness check before publication.
- WHERE the post includes a “content warning”, THE system SHALL display a preface and require user confirmation before viewing full content.
- WHEN an editor rejects a submission, THE system SHALL return reasons and allow resubmission after corrections.
- WHEN a post is archived, THE system SHALL remove it from feeds while retaining searchability for staff and author.

SLA
- WHERE review is required, THE system SHALL complete first review within 24 hours under normal operations.

### 4.9) Announcements, Pinned Posts, Special Curation
- WHERE the actor is editor or admin, THE system SHALL allow creating “Announcement” posts visible to all users.
- WHEN a post is pinned in a section by an editor, THE system SHALL keep it at the top of that section for a configurable duration (1–14 days).
- WHERE a post is featured in a curated collection, THE system SHALL annotate it with the collection label and ensure it appears in that collection’s feed.
- IF a pinned item expires, THEN THE system SHALL unpin it automatically and record the unpin event in audit logs.
- WHERE editorial quality requires temporary visibility reduction, THE system SHALL allow editors to apply non-policy-based soft-hiding with rationale visible to staff.

### 4.10) Feeds, Timelines, Subscriptions
Personalization
- WHERE a user follows topics or authors, THE system SHALL prioritize their content in the user’s home feed while ensuring at least 30% diversity from non-followed but relevant topics.
- WHERE the actor is unauthenticated, THE system SHALL show a general feed based on overall quality and recency.

Ordering and freshness
- WHEN building feeds, THE system SHALL prefer recency within the past 72 hours and decay older items unless they are featured or actively discussed.
- WHERE duplicate appearances would occur within the same feed page, THE system SHALL deduplicate items.

Integrity
- IF a post is hidden or under sanction, THEN THE system SHALL exclude it from public feeds while staff views remain available.
- WHERE a block or mute exists, THE system SHALL exclude blocked or muted sources from the viewer’s feed composition.

Pagination
- THE system SHALL deliver feeds in pages of 20 posts, supporting infinite continuation from the user perspective.

Performance
- THE system SHALL generate the first page of a personalized feed within 1.5 seconds under typical load.

### 4.11) Notification Triggers Linkage (Business Events)
- WHEN a user is mentioned in a post or comment, THE system SHALL trigger a “mention” notification per user preference.
- WHEN a followed author publishes, THE system SHALL trigger a “new post by followed author” notification subject to frequency limits (max 3 per author per day).
- WHEN a followed topic has new curated content, THE system SHALL trigger a “topic update” notification; batched in digests where configured.
- WHEN a user’s post is reported and auto-hidden, THE system SHALL send an “action required” notification with appeal information.
- WHEN an editor pins or features a user’s post, THE system SHALL notify the author of the feature placement.
- WHERE DND or snooze preferences are set, THE system SHALL defer non-transactional notifications accordingly.

Delivery channels and templates must follow the [Notifications and Communications Requirements](./11-pol-econ-board-notifications-and-communications.md).

### 4.12) Rate-Limiting and Usage Restrictions
Per-user limits (default)
- WHERE the role is member, THE system SHALL enforce: up to 10 posts/day; 60 comments/day; 300 reactions/day; 30 reports/day.
- WHERE the role is expert, THE system SHALL enforce: up to 20 posts/day; 100 comments/day; 500 reactions/day; 50 reports/day.
- WHERE the role is newly registered (< 7 days), THE system SHALL halve the above limits.

Burst control
- WHEN a user performs more than 10 reactions within 10 seconds, THE system SHALL delay further reactions for 30 seconds.
- WHEN a user attempts more than 5 post publications within 10 minutes, THE system SHALL delay further publications for 15 minutes and provide the next eligible time.

Abuse escalations
- IF repeated rate-limit violations occur 3 times within 24 hours, THEN THE system SHALL place the account under temporary restriction for 24 hours on posting and commenting.
- WHERE automated signals indicate bot-like behavior, THE system SHALL require an interactive challenge before allowing further actions.

### 4.13) Accessibility and Multilingual (Business)
Accessibility
- WHERE content includes images, THE system SHALL require descriptive alt-text 20–250 characters.
- WHERE content includes audio/video, THE system SHALL require a transcript or captions before publication unless an editor grants an exception for breaking news with a 48-hour remediation window.
- WHEN presenting color-coded badges or signals in business logic, THE system SHALL include textual equivalents.
- WHERE links are provided, THE system SHALL use meaningful descriptive link text rather than raw URLs.

Language
- WHERE a post is created, THE system SHALL store its language and allow filtering by language in search and feeds.
- WHERE multilingual content is supported, THE system SHALL link translations of the same post and allow users to prefer languages in feed preferences.
- IF a preferred language version is unavailable, THEN THE system SHALL present the default language with a notice of available languages.

Sensitive periods
- WHERE election or other sensitive political periods are in effect, THE system SHALL apply stricter review rules per the governance document and annotate affected posts with compliance tags.

---

## 5) Process Diagrams (Business Flows)

Draft → Review → Publish
```mermaid
graph LR
  subgraph "Authoring"
    A["Start Draft"] --> B["Write Content"]
    B --> C["Save Draft"]
    C --> D{"Requires Review?"}
  end
  subgraph "Review"
    E["Submit For Review"] --> F["Editor Checks Sources"]
    F --> G{"Approve?"}
  end
  subgraph "Publication"
    H["Publish"] --> I["Create Version Record"]
    I --> J["Distribute To Feeds"]
  end
  D -->|"Yes"| E
  D -->|"No"| H
  G -->|"Yes"| H
  G -->|"No"| K["Reject With Reasons"]
  K --> C
```

Report → Moderation
```mermaid
graph LR
  A["User Reports Content"] --> B["Collect Reasons"]
  B --> C{"Threshold Met?"}
  C -->|"No"| D["Queue Standard Review"]
  C -->|"Yes"| E["Auto-Hide Content"]
  E --> F["Notify Author"]
  D --> G["Moderator Review"]
  F --> G
  G --> H{"Policy Violation?"}
  H -->|"Yes"| I["Apply Sanction"]
  H -->|"No"| J["Restore Content"]
  I --> K["Transparency Log"]
  J --> K
```

---

## 6) Acceptance Criteria & Exceptions
General
- THE system SHALL persist drafts, posts, comments, and reactions with correct ownership and timestamps, visible in subsequent retrievals within expected performance windows.
- THE system SHALL prevent actions that exceed limits and provide user-facing reasons and next eligible times.
- THE system SHALL create audit entries for staff-driven visibility changes (pin, feature, hide, unhide) including actor role, reason, and timestamp.

Posts
- WHEN publishing valid content, THE system SHALL return published status, version number, and visibility; WHEN invalid, errors SHALL identify the violated business rule (length, attachments, policy triggers) in natural language.
- WHEN editing published posts, THE system SHALL create a new version and maintain access to prior versions.
- IF a post is auto-hidden due to thresholds, THEN THE system SHALL notify the author with reason category and appeal link.

Comments
- WHEN submitting valid comments, THE system SHALL append to the thread, increment counts, and notify mentioned users according to preferences.
- IF a comment violates mass-mention limits or block rules, THEN THE system SHALL reject with a clear reason.

Search and feeds
- WHEN executing typical searches and feed builds, THE system SHALL meet performance targets and return correct ordering, filtering, and deduplication.

Reporting and moderation
- WHEN report thresholds are crossed, THE system SHALL auto-hide content, notify the author, and enqueue for review with required metadata.

Notifications
- WHEN eligible events occur, THE system SHALL enqueue the corresponding notification respecting opt-in status, DND/snooze, and frequency limits.

Exceptions and overrides
- WHERE legal hold or compliance requires preservation, THE system SHALL prevent deletion and annotate the hold.
- WHERE staff override is documented, THE system SHALL record the actor, reason, and timestamp in audit logs.
- WHERE service-wide incidents necessitate temporary relaxation of limits (e.g., breaking elections news), THE system SHALL allow configured exceptions for a defined window and record the change.

Business requirements only. All technical implementation decisions, including architecture, APIs, and database design, belong to the development team. Describes WHAT the pol-econ-board system must do from a business perspective and does not prescribe HOW to build it.

files.content:
# pol-econ-board User Stories and Acceptance Criteria

User stories define complete, testable behaviors for pol-econ-board in business terms using EARS. All statements specify WHAT the system must do; all technical implementation decisions (architecture, APIs, database design) remain at the discretion of the development team.

## Personas

| Persona | Description | Primary Goals | Key Constraints | Anti-Goals |
|--------|-------------|---------------|-----------------|-----------|
| Member | Registered participant (real name or alias). Can create/manage own posts and comments, bookmark, follow topics/authors, vote/react, report, configure notifications. | Express opinions, discover credible content, manage personal library, receive relevant updates. | Must follow community rules; subject to rate limits and moderation; new-account restrictions. | Cannot moderate other users; cannot bypass policy checks; cannot view staff-only content. |
| Expert | Verified political/economic domain expert; inherits Member capabilities with expert features (badge, expert topics, in-depth insights, expert Q&A). | Publish authoritative analysis, lead expert topics, answer community questions, build reputation. | Verification required; disclosure of affiliations when relevant; higher quality bar. | Cannot override policy enforcement; cannot edit others’ content without policy-based role. |
| Moderator | Community operator enforcing rules. Triage reports, hide/remove content, request sanctions, manage disputes, maintain transparency logs. | Keep community safe and compliant; meet moderation SLAs; ensure due process. | Must follow sanction ladder and audit requirements; limited to permitted actions. | Cannot execute permanent bans without admin approval; cannot alter editorial curation. |
| Editor | Content quality curator. Manage taxonomy (categories/tags), featured collections, announcements, pinned items; collaborate with moderators for policy violations. | Elevate high-signal content, maintain taxonomy hygiene, run curated programs. | Subject to pin/feature quotas; cannot issue user sanctions alone. | Cannot remove content for policy reasons without moderation; cannot change roles. |
| Admin | System-wide operator. Manage roles/policies/settings, legal requests, transparency/audit oversight, system health indicators. | Govern operations, ensure compliance, publish transparency. | Separation of duties; sensitive actions require verification; audit logging for all admin actions. | Cannot skip transparency/audit requirements; cannot disable appeals process without policy basis. |

## Core Scenarios (Happy Paths)

### Member Core Scenarios

1) Registration and Email Verification
- User Story: As a Member, register and verify email to participate.
- Acceptance Criteria (EARS):
  - WHEN valid registration details are submitted, THE pol-econ-board SHALL create a pending account and send a verification message within 5 minutes.
  - WHEN verification is completed within 24 hours, THE pol-econ-board SHALL activate the account and allow login immediately.
  - IF the verification window expires, THEN THE pol-econ-board SHALL require a new verification before enabling login.

2) Login, Session Continuity, and Device Awareness
- User Story: As a Member, log in securely and maintain session without frequent interruptions.
- Acceptance Criteria (EARS):
  - WHEN valid credentials are submitted, THE pol-econ-board SHALL grant access and establish a session within 2 seconds under normal load.
  - WHILE the session remains within policy limits, THE pol-econ-board SHALL preserve state and support silent token renewal.
  - WHERE device session visibility is enabled, THE pol-econ-board SHALL list active sessions with device label, approximate location, and last activity.
  - WHEN a user chooses log out from all devices, THE pol-econ-board SHALL revoke all active sessions within 60 seconds and confirm completion.

3) Topic and Author Following with Personalized Feed
- User Story: As a Member, follow topics and authors to personalize discovery.
- Acceptance Criteria (EARS):
  - WHEN a topic or author is followed, THE pol-econ-board SHALL update the subscription list and adjust feed composition on the next refresh.
  - WHILE followed items exist, THE pol-econ-board SHALL present at least 20 items per page prioritized by recency and relevance.
  - IF a topic or author is unfollowed, THEN THE pol-econ-board SHALL remove it from the subscription list and reflect the change on next feed build.

4) Post Drafting, Editing Window, and Publication
- User Story: As a Member, draft, edit, and publish posts.
- Acceptance Criteria (EARS):
  - WHEN a draft with valid required fields is saved, THE pol-econ-board SHALL persist it and return a stable identifier within 2 seconds.
  - WHEN a valid draft is submitted for publication, THE pol-econ-board SHALL publish it and include it in feeds and search within 10 seconds subject to policy checks.
  - WHERE a post is edited within 10 minutes of publication, THE pol-econ-board SHALL apply a silent update without feed bump; otherwise apply normal bump.
  - IF content exceeds policy limits (length, restricted tags, missing required sources), THEN THE pol-econ-board SHALL block publication and enumerate the violated rules in user language.

5) Commenting and Mentions
- User Story: As a Member, comment and @mention others for discussion.
- Acceptance Criteria (EARS):
  - WHEN a comment meets validation rules, THE pol-econ-board SHALL post it within 2 seconds and notify recipients per preferences.
  - WHERE a mention is included and the target permits mentions, THE pol-econ-board SHALL tag the mention and trigger a notification.
  - IF the target content is removed or locked, THEN THE pol-econ-board SHALL prevent new comments and provide a policy-aligned reason.

6) Reactions and Voting
- User Story: As a Member, react or vote to signal evaluation.
- Acceptance Criteria (EARS):
  - WHEN a valid reaction or vote is submitted, THE pol-econ-board SHALL record it once per user per item and update aggregate counts within 1 second.
  - WHERE reactions are disabled or the item is archived, THE pol-econ-board SHALL prevent new reactions and indicate the state.
  - IF a conflicting vote is attempted, THEN THE pol-econ-board SHALL keep the most recent valid state without double counting.

7) Bookmarks and Reading History
- User Story: As a Member, bookmark and track reading to revisit items.
- Acceptance Criteria (EARS):
  - WHEN a bookmark request is submitted, THE pol-econ-board SHALL create it and confirm within 1 second.
  - WHILE a post is read for ≥ 10 seconds or ≥ 80% of length, THE pol-econ-board SHALL mark it as read.
  - IF a bookmarked item is deleted or made private, THEN THE pol-econ-board SHALL retain a placeholder with permitted metadata.

8) Reporting Content and Blocking Users
- User Story: As a Member, report problematic content and block users for safety.
- Acceptance Criteria (EARS):
  - WHEN a report with valid category and context is submitted, THE pol-econ-board SHALL enqueue it with timestamp and return acknowledgment within 2 seconds.
  - WHEN a user is blocked, THE pol-econ-board SHALL immediately prevent delivery of their content and notifications to the blocker.
  - IF interaction with blocked users or content is attempted, THEN THE pol-econ-board SHALL prevent the action and state the block rule.

9) Notification Preferences and Quiet Hours
- User Story: As a Member, configure notifications to limit noise.
- Acceptance Criteria (EARS):
  - WHEN notification preferences are updated, THE pol-econ-board SHALL apply changes to future notifications within 1 minute.
  - WHERE digest mode is selected, THE pol-econ-board SHALL aggregate eligible events and deliver per configured schedule.
  - IF a channel is disabled, THEN THE pol-econ-board SHALL suppress non-mandatory notifications to that channel and confirm suppression.
  - WHERE quiet hours are enabled, THE pol-econ-board SHALL defer non-critical notifications until quiet hours end.

10) Search, Sort, and Filter
- User Story: As a Member, find relevant content efficiently.
- Acceptance Criteria (EARS):
  - WHEN a search query up to 200 characters is submitted with optional filters (category, tag, author, role=expert, date range, min reaction), THE pol-econ-board SHALL return a results page within 1 second for common queries and within 3 seconds for complex filters.
  - WHERE sorting is applied, THE pol-econ-board SHALL support Newest, Oldest, Most reacted, and Most agreed orderings.
  - IF filters are invalid (e.g., inverted date range), THEN THE pol-econ-board SHALL reject the request and present corrective guidance.

11) Edit and Delete Own Content
- User Story: As a Member, manage posts and comments responsibly.
- Acceptance Criteria (EARS):
  - WHEN a published post is edited, THE pol-econ-board SHALL create a new version and maintain prior versions in history accessible to authorized roles.
  - WHEN own post is deleted, THE pol-econ-board SHALL soft-delete immediately and preserve a 30-day restoration window.
  - WHEN own comment is deleted, THE pol-econ-board SHALL soft-delete and preserve a 14-day restoration window, leaving a placeholder.

12) Account Security: Password Reset and Email Change
- User Story: As a Member, recover access and maintain up-to-date contact.
- Acceptance Criteria (EARS):
  - WHEN a password reset is requested, THE pol-econ-board SHALL send a single-use token and accept a new password within 30 minutes.
  - WHEN email change is initiated, THE pol-econ-board SHALL require re-authentication and verification of the new email before updating contact.

### Expert Core Scenarios

1) Expert Verification Lifecycle
- User Story: As an Expert candidate, submit credentials to gain expert capabilities.
- Acceptance Criteria (EARS):
  - WHEN required verification data is submitted, THE pol-econ-board SHALL record the application and notify reviewers within 5 minutes.
  - WHILE under review, THE pol-econ-board SHALL expose status and allow supplemental evidence.
  - IF approved, THEN THE pol-econ-board SHALL assign the expert role and display the badge on new and existing content within 10 minutes.

2) Conflict of Interest (COI) Disclosure
- User Story: As an Expert, disclose affiliations to maintain trust.
- Acceptance Criteria (EARS):
  - WHEN a post discusses entities with potential COI, THE pol-econ-board SHALL require affiliation disclosure before publication.
  - IF disclosure is missing for flagged contexts, THEN THE pol-econ-board SHALL hold publication and request disclosure.

3) Expert Topic Proposal and Leadership
- User Story: As an Expert, propose specialized topics and lead content.
- Acceptance Criteria (EARS):
  - WHEN a topic proposal with required metadata is submitted, THE pol-econ-board SHALL route it for editorial review and return a tracking ID.
  - IF approved, THEN THE pol-econ-board SHALL create the topic, assign the proposer as lead contributor, and publish guidelines.
  - WHERE rejected, THE pol-econ-board SHALL record rationale visible to the proposer.

4) In-depth Insight Publication and Versioning
- User Story: As an Expert, publish in-depth insights with expert labeling.
- Acceptance Criteria (EARS):
  - WHEN a compliant expert post is submitted, THE pol-econ-board SHALL publish it with expert labeling and include it in expert feeds.
  - WHERE curation flags the post, THE pol-econ-board SHALL hold publication pending review and notify within 10 minutes.
  - IF updated after publication, THEN THE pol-econ-board SHALL version the content and expose version history to authorized roles.

5) Expert Q&A Participation
- User Story: As an Expert, answer tagged questions effectively.
- Acceptance Criteria (EARS):
  - WHEN posting an answer to a tagged question, THE pol-econ-board SHALL mark it expert-answered and notify the asker.
  - WHERE multiple experts answer, THE pol-econ-board SHALL order by freshness and relevance and allow reactions/votes.
  - IF the question is closed by policy, THEN THE pol-econ-board SHALL prevent new answers and indicate closure reason.

### Moderator Core Scenarios

1) Report Intake and Triage
- User Story: As a Moderator, triage incoming reports to act within SLA.
- Acceptance Criteria (EARS):
  - WHEN a new report arrives, THE pol-econ-board SHALL place it in the triage queue with severity and category metadata immediately.
  - WHILE a moderator handles a report, THE pol-econ-board SHALL lock it to that moderator to prevent conflicting actions.
  - IF the report lacks sufficient context, THEN THE pol-econ-board SHALL request more information from the reporter.

2) Provisional Hide, Removal, and Restoration
- User Story: As a Moderator, hide or remove violating content and restore if appropriate.
- Acceptance Criteria (EARS):
  - WHEN a provisional hide is applied under rules, THE pol-econ-board SHALL hide the content within 1 minute and log the action.
  - WHERE removal is warranted, THE pol-econ-board SHALL remove content, preserve audit evidence, and notify involved parties.
  - IF an action is reversed after review, THEN THE pol-econ-board SHALL restore visibility and update transparency logs.

3) Sanction Requests and Enforcement
- User Story: As a Moderator, request sanctions to deter violations.
- Acceptance Criteria (EARS):
  - WHEN a sanction request meets thresholds, THE pol-econ-board SHALL route it for approval and start SLA timers.
  - WHERE a sanction is approved, THE pol-econ-board SHALL apply it and restrict affected actions immediately.
  - IF the sanction period elapses, THEN THE pol-econ-board SHALL lift restrictions automatically and log completion.

4) Appeals Handling
- User Story: As a Moderator, process appeals to ensure fairness.
- Acceptance Criteria (EARS):
  - WHEN an appeal is submitted within the window, THE pol-econ-board SHALL acknowledge receipt and place it in an appeals queue.
  - WHILE an appeal is pending, THE pol-econ-board SHALL pause further escalations where policy allows.
  - IF the appeal is upheld, THEN THE pol-econ-board SHALL reverse actions and notify parties; ELSE THE pol-econ-board SHALL provide rationale and next steps.

5) Election-Period Triage
- User Story: As a Moderator, apply heightened standards during election periods.
- Acceptance Criteria (EARS):
  - WHERE the system is in election-period state, THE pol-econ-board SHALL prioritize flagged items and shorten internal review timers according to policy.
  - WHEN content about elections lacks required sourcing, THE pol-econ-board SHALL hold publication pending verification.

### Editor Core Scenarios

1) Taxonomy Management and Deprecation
- User Story: As an Editor, manage categories, tags, and deprecations.
- Acceptance Criteria (EARS):
  - WHEN a category/tag update is submitted, THE pol-econ-board SHALL validate uniqueness and policy compliance and apply changes within 2 minutes.
  - WHERE a category is deprecated, THE pol-econ-board SHALL migrate attached content to a designated alternative and log mappings.
  - IF a change would break references, THEN THE pol-econ-board SHALL block it and propose safe alternatives.

2) Featured Collections, Pinning, and Rotation
- User Story: As an Editor, curate featured sets and manage pins.
- Acceptance Criteria (EARS):
  - WHEN a featured collection with valid items is created, THE pol-econ-board SHALL publish it and expose it to eligible feeds.
  - WHERE pinning limits are reached, THE pol-econ-board SHALL reject new pins and indicate current allocations.
  - IF a pinned item expires or is removed, THEN THE pol-econ-board SHALL unpin it and update dependent placements.

3) Scheduled Publishing and Announcements
- User Story: As an Editor, schedule posts and publish announcements.
- Acceptance Criteria (EARS):
  - WHEN a scheduled publish time in Asia/Seoul is set, THE pol-econ-board SHALL publish within the scheduled minute barring policy holds.
  - WHERE an announcement is created by authorized roles, THE pol-econ-board SHALL display it to all users and log publish/unpublish events.

### Admin Core Scenarios

1) Role and Permission Management
- User Story: As an Admin, assign roles and manage permissions appropriately.
- Acceptance Criteria (EARS):
  - WHEN a role is assigned or revoked, THE pol-econ-board SHALL reflect the change in authorization decisions within 1 minute.
  - WHERE conflicting role changes occur, THE pol-econ-board SHALL apply deterministic precedence per policy and log resolution.
  - IF assignment checks fail, THEN THE pol-econ-board SHALL reject the change with a policy-aligned reason.

2) Legal Request and Transparency Reporting
- User Story: As an Admin, process legal requests and publish transparency data.
- Acceptance Criteria (EARS):
  - WHEN a lawful request is recorded with required metadata, THE pol-econ-board SHALL freeze affected data changes and start fulfillment timers.
  - WHERE disclosure is authorized, THE pol-econ-board SHALL produce required artifacts and update status.
  - IF the request is withdrawn or expires, THEN THE pol-econ-board SHALL lift holds and record closure.
  - WHEN the monthly transparency report is due, THE pol-econ-board SHALL publish aggregated moderation metrics by the policy deadline.

---

## Secondary and Edge Scenarios

1) Draft Autosave and Recovery
- Acceptance Criteria (EARS):
  - WHILE editing and changes are detected, THE pol-econ-board SHALL autosave at least every 30 seconds or on significant edits.
  - IF a session ends unexpectedly, THEN THE pol-econ-board SHALL offer the most recent autosaved draft upon return.

2) Version Conflicts on Edit
- Acceptance Criteria (EARS):
  - WHEN an edit conflicts with a newer server version, THE pol-econ-board SHALL detect the conflict and require confirmation to merge or overwrite.
  - IF the user cancels, THEN THE pol-econ-board SHALL preserve the server version and local changes as a new draft.

3) Comment Thread Locking
- Acceptance Criteria (EARS):
  - WHEN a thread is locked, THE pol-econ-board SHALL prevent new comments and reactions and display the locked state to authorized viewers.
  - IF the lock is lifted, THEN THE pol-econ-board SHALL restore normal interaction immediately.

4) Rate Limits and Cooldowns
- Acceptance Criteria (EARS):
  - WHEN defined action limits are exceeded, THE pol-econ-board SHALL block further attempts for the cooldown period and indicate remaining wait time.
  - WHERE elevated abuse risk is detected, THE pol-econ-board SHALL apply stricter temporary limits consistent with policy.

5) Soft-Deleted Content References
- Acceptance Criteria (EARS):
  - WHEN content is soft-deleted, THE pol-econ-board SHALL maintain a placeholder with non-sensitive metadata where policy allows.
  - IF hard deletion is required by policy, THEN THE pol-econ-board SHALL remove references and indicate unavailability.

6) Appeal Window Boundary
- Acceptance Criteria (EARS):
  - WHEN an action triggers an appealable decision, THE pol-econ-board SHALL show the appeal window and accept appeals until the exact cutoff.
  - IF an appeal arrives after the deadline, THEN THE pol-econ-board SHALL reject it and provide information about next permitted steps.

7) Notification Delivery Guarantees and Quiet Hours
- Acceptance Criteria (EARS):
  - WHEN a triggering event occurs, THE pol-econ-board SHALL enqueue notification delivery within 1 minute and attempt delivery according to preferences.
  - IF delivery fails, THEN THE pol-econ-board SHALL retry per policy and record the outcome for user-visible status.
  - WHERE quiet hours apply, THE pol-econ-board SHALL defer non-critical deliveries until quiet hours end.

8) Expert Status Revocation
- Acceptance Criteria (EARS):
  - WHEN expert status is revoked, THE pol-econ-board SHALL remove the badge from new and existing public views and update permissions immediately.
  - WHERE prior content references expert status, THE pol-econ-board SHALL preserve historical accuracy in audit contexts while removing public-facing badges.

9) Duplicate Submission Protection and Idempotency
- Acceptance Criteria (EARS):
  - WHEN the same action is detected as a retry within 30 seconds, THE pol-econ-board SHALL return the prior success identifier without duplicating side effects.
  - IF a duplicate post is detected by similarity within 5 minutes, THEN THE pol-econ-board SHALL block publication and offer options to edit, merge, or discard.

10) Offline and Intermittent Connectivity
- Acceptance Criteria (EARS):
  - WHEN connectivity is lost during draft editing, THE pol-econ-board SHALL preserve the last confirmed version and surface a reconciliation prompt on restore.
  - WHEN connectivity resumes, THE pol-econ-board SHALL synchronize pending actions in submission order with idempotency.

---

## Abuse and Misuse Prevention Scenarios

1) Spam Posting and Mass Mentions
- Acceptance Criteria (EARS):
  - WHEN posting frequency or content patterns match spam heuristics, THE pol-econ-board SHALL throttle or block submission and require additional verification.
  - WHERE mass mentions exceed policy thresholds, THE pol-econ-board SHALL block the operation and indicate limits.

2) Coordinated Brigading and Vote Manipulation
- Acceptance Criteria (EARS):
  - WHEN correlated abnormal voting is detected, THE pol-econ-board SHALL flag tallies for review and temporarily exclude suspicious signals from public counts.
  - IF accounts are confirmed abusive, THEN THE pol-econ-board SHALL invalidate related interactions and apply sanctions per policy.

3) Harassment and Doxxing Prevention
- Acceptance Criteria (EARS):
  - WHEN content includes prohibited personal information or targeted harassment patterns, THE pol-econ-board SHALL block or remove the content and escalate to moderation.
  - WHERE repeated harassment originates from an account, THE pol-econ-board SHALL escalate sanctions per severity ladder.

4) False Reporting Abuse
- Acceptance Criteria (EARS):
  - WHEN reporting patterns from an account are repeatedly invalid, THE pol-econ-board SHALL limit reporting privileges temporarily and inform the user.
  - IF a subsequent report is validated within a defined period, THEN THE pol-econ-board SHALL restore normal privileges.

5) Election-Period Safeguards
- Acceptance Criteria (EARS):
  - WHERE the system is in election-period state, THE pol-econ-board SHALL apply heightened content checks and shorter moderation SLAs for flagged items.
  - WHEN election-related content lacks required sourcing, THE pol-econ-board SHALL hold publication pending verification.

6) Sockpuppeting and Evasion
- Acceptance Criteria (EARS):
  - WHEN evasion of sanctions via new accounts is detected, THE pol-econ-board SHALL link related accounts for enforcement and apply escalated sanctions per policy.

---

## Definition of Done (DoD) and Cross-Cutting Acceptance Criteria

- DoD per story
  - THE pol-econ-board SHALL satisfy all EARS acceptance criteria defined for the story.
  - THE pol-econ-board SHALL implement input validation rules, clear error states, and reversible outcomes where policy allows.
  - THE pol-econ-board SHALL log business events necessary for audit and transparency with durable identifiers.
  - THE pol-econ-board SHALL meet performance expectations (e.g., common actions within 1–2 seconds P95; publication/indexing within stated windows).
  - THE pol-econ-board SHALL present policy-aligned user messages without revealing sensitive internals.

- Cross-cutting criteria
  - WHEN an operation succeeds, THE pol-econ-board SHALL return a durable identifier referencing the resulting entity.
  - IF an operation fails, THEN THE pol-econ-board SHALL provide a reason code and a recoverable next step where applicable.
  - WHILE permissions are being changed, THE pol-econ-board SHALL keep authorization decisions consistent and atomic from the user perspective.
  - WHERE data retention or legal holds apply, THE pol-econ-board SHALL respect retention windows and display availability states.
  - WHERE localization applies, THE pol-econ-board SHALL provide messages in the user’s preferred language with consistent terminology.
  - WHERE accessibility applies, THE pol-econ-board SHALL include textual equivalents for non-text signals in user-facing messages.

---

## Visual Flows (Representative)

### Post Creation, Review, and Publication (Member → Editor/Moderator)
```mermaid
graph LR
  subgraph "Authoring"
    A["Start Draft"] --> B["Autosave Draft"]
    B --> C["Submit For Publication"]
  end
  subgraph "Editorial/Policy Checks"
    D["Policy Validation"] --> E{"Compliant?"}
  end
  subgraph "Outcomes"
    F["Publish Post"]
    G["Hold For Review"]
    H["Reject With Guidance"]
  end
  C --> D
  E -->|"Yes"| F
  E -->|"Needs Review"| G
  E -->|"No"| H
```

### Report Intake and Moderation Action
```mermaid
graph LR
  subgraph "Report Intake"
    R1["Member Submits Report"] --> R2["Categorize & Timestamp"]
    R2 --> R3["Queue For Triage"]
  end
  subgraph "Triage"
    T1["Assign To Moderator"] --> T2{"Sufficient Context?"}
  end
  subgraph "Action"
    A1["Provisional Hide"]
    A2["Remove & Preserve Evidence"]
    A3["No Action"]
  end
  R3 --> T1
  T2 -->|"Yes"| A1
  T2 -->|"Yes"| A2
  T2 -->|"No"| A3
```

### Expert Verification and COI Disclosure
```mermaid
graph LR
  subgraph "Application"
    V1["Submit Verification Data"] --> V2["Record & Notify Reviewers"]
  end
  subgraph "Review"
    V3["Review Credentials"] --> V4{"Approve?"}
  end
  subgraph "Outcomes"
    V5["Assign Expert Role"]
    V6["Request More Evidence"]
    V7["Reject With Rationale"]
  end
  V2 --> V3
  V4 -->|"Yes"| V5
  V4 -->|"No"| V7
  V3 --> V6
```

### Notification Preferences and Quiet Hours
```mermaid
graph LR
  subgraph "Preference Management"
    P1["Open Preferences"] --> P2["Set Categories & Channels"]
    P2 --> P3["Enable Quiet Hours"]
    P2 --> P4["Select Digest Frequency"]
  end
  subgraph "Evaluation"
    E1["Event Triggered"] --> E2["Check Preferences"]
    E2 --> E3{"Suppress?"}
  end
  subgraph "Delivery"
    D1["Queue In-App"]
    D2["Queue Email"]
  end
  E3 -->|"Yes"| E4["Defer or Suppress"]
  E3 -->|"No"| D1
  E3 -->|"No"| D2
```

# pol-econ-board User Flows

## Scope and Principles
- Business workflows covering account creation and authentication, content authoring and publishing, reporting and moderation with appeal, and notifications configuration and delivery.
- Roles in scope: member, expert, moderator, editor, admin.
- Out of scope: frontend UI/UX layouts, API endpoints, database schemas, infrastructure design.
- Implementation ownership: defines WHAT happens; all technical implementation decisions (architecture, APIs, database design, encryption, infrastructure) belong to developers.
- Consistency rules: EARS requirements throughout; Mermaid diagrams use left-to-right orientation; all labels in double quotes; no spaces between brackets/braces and quotes; correct arrow syntax.
- Time references: user-perceived performance and any SLAs are expressed in business terms; default business timezone Asia/Seoul (KST).

## User Journey Overview
The service supports trustworthy political/economic discourse. Users discover content, register, verify, and sign in; create and publish posts; engage via comments and reactions; and escalate issues through reporting. Experts produce in-depth analyses; moderators and editors ensure compliance and quality; admins manage global policies and escalations.

Key journey highlights:
- Onboarding: registration, email verification, sign-in, session maintenance, secure sign-out across devices.
- Creation: draft → edit → version tracking → publish; optional pre-publish review based on policies and role capabilities.
- Governance: report → triage → action (hide/delete/sanction) → transparency log → appeal → review → resolution.
- Notifications: real-time and batch/digest messages that respect user preferences, quiet hours, and rate limits.

### High-Level Journey Diagram
```mermaid
graph LR
  A["Discover Content"] --> B["Register/Sign In"]
  B --> C["Create Draft/Post"]
  C --> D{"Publish?"}
  D -->|"Yes"| E["Visible Per Policy"]
  D -->|"No"| F["Save as Draft"]
  E --> G["Engage(Comments/Reactions)"]
  G --> H{"Policy Violation Report?"}
  H -->|"No"| I["Continue Engagement"]
  H -->|"Yes"| J["Moderation Workflow"]
  J --> K{"Action Required?"}
  K -->|"Yes"| L["Apply Action(Sanction/Hide/Delete)"]
  K -->|"No"| M["Close with No Action"]
  E --> N["Notifications"]
```

## Account Creation and Authentication Flow
Covers registration, email verification, sign-in, session maintenance, sign-out, password reset, and cross-device revocation. Token usage adheres to JWT-based principles defined in the authentication requirements.

### Narrative Flow
- Registration: A user submits registration data; inputs are validated; a pending-verification account is created; verification instructions are sent; account activates upon successful verification.
- Sign-in: A user submits credentials; the system validates and establishes a session with short-lived access and longer-lived refresh tokens. Failed attempts increase a counter that can trigger temporary lockout.
- Password reset: A user initiates a reset; a one-time, time-bound reset process is issued; after success, prior sessions are invalidated per policy.
- Sign-out and device revocation: A user signs out on the current device and may revoke all sessions across all devices.

### Role Notes
- All roles use the same authentication and session flow; role assignment influences authorization decisions after sign-in.

### EARS Requirements (Authentication)
- THE authentication service SHALL accept registration with email and password and create an account in a pending-verification state.
- WHEN a user completes email verification within the valid window, THE authentication service SHALL activate the account for sign-in.
- IF email verification is attempted after expiration, THEN THE authentication service SHALL deny activation and allow requesting a new verification process.
- WHEN a user submits valid credentials, THE authentication service SHALL establish a session and issue tokens with defined expirations.
- IF a login attempt uses invalid credentials, THEN THE authentication service SHALL reject the login, increment a failure counter, and present a non-revealing error message.
- WHERE the failure counter exceeds the lockout threshold within a window, THE authentication service SHALL apply a temporary login delay and provide guidance for password reset.
- WHEN a user requests password reset, THE authentication service SHALL issue a one-time reset process bound to time and single-use constraints.
- WHEN a password reset is completed, THE authentication service SHALL invalidate prior sessions according to security policy.
- WHEN a user signs out, THE authentication service SHALL terminate the current session immediately.
- WHEN a user requests device-wide sign-out, THE authentication service SHALL revoke all active sessions associated with the account.
- WHILE a session is active, THE authentication service SHALL refresh access according to token refresh policy and deny refresh after refresh expiration.
- THE authentication service SHALL respond to sign-in attempts within 2 seconds under normal load.

### Account Creation & Authentication Diagram
```mermaid
graph LR
  subgraph "Registration"
    A["Start Registration"] --> B["Validate Inputs"]
    B --> C{"Valid?"}
    C -->|"Yes"| D["Create Pending Account"]
    C -->|"No"| E["Reject and Explain"]
    D --> F["Send Verification"]
  end

  subgraph "Verification"
    F --> G["User Follows Link"]
    G --> H{"Within Valid Window?"}
    H -->|"Yes"| I["Activate Account"]
    H -->|"No"| J["Offer New Verification"]
  end

  subgraph "Sign-In & Session"
    K["Submit Credentials"] --> L["Validate Credentials"]
    L --> M{"Valid?"}
    M -->|"Yes"| N["Issue Tokens"]
    M -->|"No"| O["Reject and Increment Counter"]
    N --> P["Access Protected Resources"]
    P --> Q{"Refresh Needed?"}
    Q -->|"Yes"| R["Refresh Within Policy"]
    Q -->|"No"| S["Continue"]
  end

  subgraph "Sign-Out & Revocation"
    T["User Sign-Out"] --> U["Terminate Current Session"]
    V["Revoke All Devices"] --> W["Invalidate All Sessions"]
  end
```

## Post Create, Edit, Publish Flow
Covers drafting, editing, versioning, and publishing with policy checks and role-based nuances.

### Narrative Flow
- Drafting: Any authenticated member or expert creates drafts with autosave. Editors and admins typically do not author on behalf of others unless policy allows; editors manage curation and featured placement via separate processes.
- Editing: Authors freely edit drafts; edits to published posts create versions with change logs. Members update their own content; experts publish “insight” or “research” posts under the same versioning rules.
- Pre-publish checks: Policy validations run (e.g., restricted topics during sensitive periods, required sources for factual claims). Signals or rules may route posts for moderator review.
- Publishing: If checks pass and no mandatory review applies, the post becomes visible per visibility policy (public or restricted). If review is required, visibility remains limited until approval.

### Role Notes
- member: drafts, edits, publishes own content; subject to automated checks and potential moderation review.
- expert: same as member with expert labeling; does not bypass policy enforcement.
- editor: features and pins posts; manages topics/labels; cannot unilaterally override policy enforcement.
- moderator: may hold, hide, or request actions per governance policy.
- admin: oversees legal/policy compliance and system-level settings.

### EARS Requirements (Authoring & Publishing)
- WHEN an authenticated user creates a draft, THE content service SHALL save the draft and maintain an immutable version history upon each significant save.
- WHILE a post remains in draft, THE content service SHALL restrict visibility to the author and authorized reviewers where applicable.
- WHEN an author attempts to publish, THE content service SHALL execute policy checks including restricted periods, mandatory citations, and prohibited content categories.
- IF any mandatory check fails, THEN THE content service SHALL block publishing, present failure reasons, and preserve the draft state.
- WHERE a post is flagged by automated heuristics or configured rules, THE content service SHALL route the post to a moderation queue and defer public visibility until decision.
- WHEN a post passes all checks without mandatory review, THE content service SHALL publish the post and set visibility per policy immediately.
- WHEN an author edits a published post, THE content service SHALL create a new version, preserve prior versions, and update the live version upon successful checks.
- IF an author attempts to edit content under active investigation, THEN THE content service SHALL restrict edits to draft-copy only and prevent live changes until the investigation concludes.
- THE content service SHALL record publication timestamps and version identifiers for transparency.
- THE content service SHALL complete pre-publish validation within 3 seconds for standard-length posts under normal load.

### Authoring & Publishing Diagram
```mermaid
graph LR
  subgraph "Drafting"
    A["Start Draft"] --> B["Autosave Draft"]
    B --> C["Edit Content"]
  end

  subgraph "Pre-Publish Checks"
    C --> D["Run Policy Checks"]
    D --> E{"Checks Pass?"}
    E -->|"No"| F["Block Publish and Explain"]
    E -->|"Yes"| G{"Flagged for Review?"}
    G -->|"Yes"| H["Route to Moderation Queue"]
    G -->|"No"| I["Publish Immediately"]
  end

  subgraph "Post-Publish"
    I --> J["Visible per Policy"]
    H --> K{"Moderator Decision"}
    K -->|"Approve"| L["Publish"]
    K -->|"Reject"| M["Return to Draft with Reasons"]
    K -->|"Request Changes"| N["Author Revises Draft"]
    N -.-> D
  end

  subgraph "Editing Published Content"
    O["Edit Published Post"] --> P["Create New Version"]
    P --> D
  end
```

## Report Intake → Moderation → Appeal Flow
Defines how users report content, how moderators triage and act, and how authors can appeal decisions. Time expectations are stated in business terms.

### Narrative Flow
- Reporting: Any authenticated user reports content under specified categories (e.g., misinformation, hate, spam). The system validates report completeness and enters it into the moderation queue.
- Triage: Moderators review by severity and context, consult guidelines, and record transparent decisions, including temporary hiding where warranted.
- Actions: Outcomes include no action, warning, temporary suspension, edit request, hide, or delete. Sanctioning follows the governance policy and transparency logging.
- Appeal: Affected users file appeals within a defined window. Appeals are reviewed by a different moderator or a designated reviewer. Decisions are logged and communicated.

### Role Notes
- member/expert: submit reports; appeal actions affecting their content or account.
- moderator: triage reports; apply content actions; propose or apply sanctions within remit.
- editor: collaborates on quality; does not override moderation outcomes unilaterally.
- admin: handles escalations, legal requests, and final adjudication when policy demands.

### EARS Requirements (Moderation)
- WHEN a user submits a report with a valid category and target, THE governance service SHALL create a case and place it in the moderation queue.
- IF the report lacks required details, THEN THE governance service SHALL reject the submission and instruct the reporter to provide missing fields.
- WHERE content presents imminent harm indicators, THE governance service SHALL apply temporary hiding pending expedited review.
- WHEN a moderator reviews a case, THE governance service SHALL require a decision record including category, rationale, and action.
- WHEN a case is resolved with action, THE governance service SHALL notify the reporter and affected parties with outcome and rationale.
- WHERE a sanction affects account capabilities, THE governance service SHALL enforce restrictions immediately upon decision.
- WHEN an appeal is received within the allowed window, THE governance service SHALL assign it to an eligible reviewer distinct from the original decision maker.
- IF an appeal is upheld, THEN THE governance service SHALL restore the content or reverse sanctions and update the transparency record.
- IF an appeal is denied, THEN THE governance service SHALL maintain the action and record the rationale.
- THE governance service SHALL target initial triage within 24 hours for standard cases and within 2 hours for imminent harm indicators.

### Moderation & Appeal Diagram
```mermaid
graph LR
  subgraph "Report Intake"
    A["Submit Report"] --> B["Validate Fields"]
    B --> C{"Complete?"}
    C -->|"No"| D["Reject and Guide"]
    C -->|"Yes"| E["Create Case"]
  end

  subgraph "Triage & Review"
    E --> F{"Imminent Harm?"}
    F -->|"Yes"| G["Temporarily Hide Content"]
    F -->|"No"| H["Queue by Priority"]
    G --> I["Expedited Review"]
    H --> I
    I --> J{"Decision"}
  end

  subgraph "Actions"
    J -->|"No Action"| K["Close Case"]
    J -->|"Warn/Suspend"| L["Apply Sanction"]
    J -->|"Hide/Delete"| M["Apply Content Action"]
    J -->|"Edit Request"| N["Request Changes from Author"]
  end

  subgraph "Appeal"
    O["File Appeal"] --> P["Assign Different Reviewer"]
    P --> Q{"Appeal Outcome"}
    Q -->|"Upheld"| R["Reverse Action and Restore"]
    Q -->|"Denied"| S["Maintain Action"]
  end

  K --> T["Notify Parties"]
  L --> T
  M --> T
  N --> T
  R --> T
  S --> T
```

## Notification Settings and Receipt Flow
Defines how users configure preferences and how notifications are delivered in real time or digest, respecting rate limits and user control.

### Narrative Flow
- Preference management: Users opt in/out per channel (in-app, email) and per category (mentions, replies, follows, moderation updates, policy events). Users may select digest frequency for summaries.
- Triggering: Events such as mentions, comments, follows, publication outcomes, and moderation decisions trigger notifications. The system evaluates user preferences, quiet hours, and rate limits before sending.
- Delivery: Real-time where required; batched aggregation for digest per chosen interval. Failures are retried per policy. Users can view notification history.

### Role Notes
- All roles receive notifications appropriate to their actions and responsibilities. Moderators also receive queue assignments; admins receive policy/legal event notifications.

### EARS Requirements (Notifications)
- WHEN a trigger event occurs, THE notification service SHALL evaluate the recipient's preferences and channel availability before queuing delivery.
- WHERE a user has enabled digest for a category, THE notification service SHALL aggregate events and deliver at the configured interval.
- IF a user has opted out for a channel or category, THEN THE notification service SHALL suppress delivery for that scope.
- WHEN a delivery attempt fails transiently, THE notification service SHALL retry according to backoff policy and record failure if exhausted.
- WHEN a notification pertains to moderation outcomes, THE notification service SHALL include outcome, rationale summary, and available next steps.
- THE notification service SHALL respect configured rate limits and quiet hours for non-critical categories.
- WHERE an event is critical (security or policy), THE notification service SHALL bypass quiet hours for the minimum necessary alerting.

### Notification Flow Diagram
```mermaid
graph LR
  subgraph "Preference Management"
    A["Open Preferences"] --> B["Set Channels"]
    B --> C["Set Categories"]
    C --> D["Set Digest Frequency"]
  end

  subgraph "Trigger & Evaluation"
    E["Event Triggered"] --> F["Load Recipient Preferences"]
    F --> G{"Opted Out?"}
    G -->|"Yes"| H["Suppress"]
    G -->|"No"| I{"Digest Category?"}
    I -->|"Yes"| J["Aggregate for Digest"]
    I -->|"No"| K["Queue for Real-Time Delivery"]
  end

  subgraph "Delivery"
    K --> L["Attempt Delivery"]
    L --> M{"Success?"}
    M -->|"Yes"| N["Record Sent"]
    M -->|"No"| O["Retry per Policy"]
    O --> P{"Exhausted?"}
    P -->|"Yes"| Q["Record Failure"]
    P -->|"No"| L
    J --> R["Send Digest at Interval"]
  end
```

## Role-Based Approval and Gating Points
Authorization gates differ by role for certain actions. Business rules are expressed in EARS to remove ambiguity.

### EARS Requirements (Role Gates)
- WHERE the actor is member, THE content service SHALL allow publishing own posts subject to policy checks without mandatory staff pre-approval.
- WHERE the actor is expert and marks content as “long-form research”, THE content service SHALL require either source completeness verification or editor review prior to publication.
- WHERE the actor is editor, THE curation service SHALL permit pinning and featuring but SHALL require moderator approval to enforce policy violations.
- WHERE the actor is moderator, THE governance service SHALL allow content hide/remove and SHALL require admin approval for permanent account sanctions.
- WHERE the actor is admin, THE governance service SHALL allow irreversible sanctions and legal-policy overrides with mandatory audit logging.

### Role Gate Diagram
```mermaid
graph LR
  subgraph "Actors"
    A["Member"]
    B["Expert"]
    C["Editor"]
    D["Moderator"]
    E["Admin"]
  end

  subgraph "Gates"
    G1["Publish Without Pre-Approval"]
    G2["Research Pre-Check or Editor Review"]
    G3["Pin/Feature Requires Policy Alignment"]
    G4["Hide/Remove Content"]
    G5["Permanent Sanction Approval"]
  end

  A --> G1
  B --> G2
  C --> G3
  D --> G4
  D --> G5
  E --> G5
```

## Exception Branches and Rollback Flows
Cross-flow exception handling paths and rollback behaviors expressed in EARS with a consolidated diagram.

### EARS Requirements (Exceptions & Rollbacks)
- IF registration input validation fails, THEN THE authentication service SHALL not create an account and SHALL provide actionable guidance without revealing sensitive validation logic.
- IF email verification is attempted with an invalid or expired token, THEN THE authentication service SHALL deny activation and SHALL offer a new verification process.
- IF token refresh is attempted after refresh expiration, THEN THE authentication service SHALL require re-authentication and SHALL deny access until successful sign-in.
- IF an author loses connectivity during draft save, THEN THE content service SHALL retain the last confirmed version and SHALL surface a reconciliation prompt on next restore.
- IF pre-publish checks detect policy violations, THEN THE content service SHALL preserve the draft, SHALL enumerate violations, and SHALL block publication until resolved.
- IF a moderation action is applied in error and later reversed, THEN THE governance service SHALL restore content visibility and SHALL update all related notifications and transparency records.
- IF notification delivery repeatedly fails for a channel, THEN THE notification service SHALL mark the channel as temporarily unavailable for the recipient and SHALL suggest remediation steps via an alternative channel if available.
- WHEN a user requests account-wide sign-out, THE authentication service SHALL revoke all devices within 1 minute and SHALL require fresh authentication for any new access.

### Cross-Flow Rollback Diagram
```mermaid
graph LR
  A["Draft Save Attempt"] --> B{"Network OK?"}
  B -->|"Yes"| C["Save Draft Version"]
  B -->|"No"| D["Keep Last Confirmed Version"]
  D --> E["Prompt Reconcile on Return"]

  F["Publish Attempt"] --> G{"Policy Checks Pass?"}
  G -->|"Yes"| H["Publish Live"]
  G -->|"No"| I["Block and Keep Draft"]

  J["Token Refresh"] --> K{"Refresh Valid?"}
  K -->|"Yes"| L["Issue New Access"]
  K -->|"No"| M["Require Re-Auth"]

  N["Moderation Reversal"] --> O["Restore Content"]
  O --> P["Update Notifications"]
  O --> Q["Update Transparency Record"]
```

## Related Documents
- Refer to the [User Roles and Authentication Requirements](./03-pol-econ-board-user-roles-and-authentication.md) for roles, tokens, and authentication policies.
- Refer to the [Functional Requirements Specification](./04-pol-econ-board-functional-requirements.md) for end-to-end business functionality and validations.
- Refer to the [Community Governance and Moderation Policy](./07-pol-econ-board-community-governance-and-moderation.md) for report categories, sanctions, and appeals.
