# Community Governance and Moderation Requirements (pol-econ-board)

## 1) Scope and Principles
- Purpose: establish unambiguous, enforceable rules and processes for content governance, reporting, moderation actions, sanctions, transparency, and appeals, including special election-period policies aligned to domestic law.
- Scope: applies to all user-generated content (UGC): posts, comments, replies, titles, tags, attachments, profile bios, display names, and any user-visible metadata or labels.
- Principles:
  - Legality: comply with applicable domestic regulations in the primary jurisdiction; prohibit unlawful content and behavior.
  - Truthfulness: encourage evidence-based discourse; mitigate unverified or manipulative content through labels and distribution controls while preserving legitimate opinion.
  - Proportionality: apply progressive sanctions proportional to severity and recurrence, with clear thresholds and windows.
  - Due process: provide reason codes, timelines, and an appeal channel; record audit trails suitable for review.
  - Transparency: publish aggregated moderation statistics, and provide user-facing case histories and outcomes.

EARS (Foundational)
- THE governance subsystem SHALL apply these policies consistently across roles, content types, and workflows.
- THE governance subsystem SHALL maintain a standardized taxonomy for reason codes, decisions, sanctions, and closure statuses.

## 2) Roles and Governance Responsibilities (Business)
- member: may create and report content, block users, and receive sanctions; cannot sanction others.
- expert: inherits member; can propose expert topics, publish in-depth research, participate in expert Q&A; must meet higher disclosure standards for affiliations/conflicts.
- moderator: operates the moderation queue; can hide/remove content; can issue warnings and temporary suspensions up to 30 days; manages disputes; maintains transparency logs.
- editor: curates featured content; manages announcements/pinned posts; edits topics/tags; may hide content for editorial quality but cannot sanction users; must escalate policy violations to moderators.
- admin: full oversight; manages roles/policies; handles legal requests; may impose permanent sanctions; approves election-period configurations and policy updates.

EARS (Roles)
- THE governance subsystem SHALL enforce role-specific authorization boundaries and approval flows for all moderation actions.
- WHERE the actor role is "editor", THE system SHALL restrict enforcement actions to temporary editorial hiding without user sanctions.
- WHERE the actor role is "moderator", THE system SHALL allow warnings and suspensions of 24h/7d/30d and content removal within defined scope only.
- WHERE the actor role is "admin", THE system SHALL allow permanent sanctions, role/policy changes, and election-policy activation.
- WHEN any role performs a moderation-relevant action, THE system SHALL record actor role, action, target, timestamp, reason code, and outcome in an audit log.

## 3) Community Rules: Allowed/Restricted/Prohibited Content
3.1 Allowed with Expectations (Examples)
- Opinion/Analysis framed as subjective perspective, clearly separated from factual assertions.
- Critique of public policy/officials without doxxing or unlawful exposure of personal data.
- Satire/Parody labeled to prevent confusion with factual reporting.

3.2 Restricted (Require Labels/Disclaimers or Distribution Mitigation)
- Unverified claims: require a "Unverified" label until a credible source is provided; visibility may be reduced pending sourcing.
- Polls/Surveys: require methodology disclosure; incomplete disclosures receive "Methodology Incomplete" label.
- Economic/Financial content: require a "Not financial advice" disclaimer.

3.3 Prohibited (Immediate Enforcement)
- Illegal content: threats, incitement to violence, doxxing, non-consensual personal information, targeted harassment, discriminatory hate content, sexual exploitation, unlawful solicitation.
- Harmful misinformation: fabricated facts presented as truth with potential imminent harm (public safety, election procedure manipulation).
- Spam/Manipulation: mass posting, link farming, coordinated inauthentic behavior, undisclosed paid political content, astroturfing.
- Copyright infringement: unauthorized reproduction where rights-holder objection is likely.

EARS (Classification & Mitigation)
- THE governance subsystem SHALL maintain a canonical reason code set (e.g., ILLEGAL_THREAT, HATE_SPEECH, DOXXING, MISINFO_HARM, SPAM, COPYRIGHT, OFF_TOPIC, LOW_QUALITY, HARASSMENT, ELECTION_PROCEDURE_FALSE).
- WHEN content is classified as prohibited, THE system SHALL immediately block public exposure and move it to "Under Review" state.
- WHEN content requires labeling, THE system SHALL attach the specified label(s) and reduce algorithmic amplification until criteria are satisfied.
- IF classification confidence is low, THEN THE system SHALL apply the "Unverified" label and route the item to the review queue without permanent action.

## 4) Political-Sensitive Content Guidelines (Factuality, Source, Tone)
4.1 Factuality
- Assertions of fact must be verifiable via reliable sources (primary records, reputable media, official statistics). Opinions remain permissible if clearly framed.

4.2 Sourcing
- Political claims must include source citations (URL, publication, date). Missing sources trigger mitigation labels and reduced promotion.

4.3 Expression Level
- Robust debate is encouraged; dehumanizing language, slurs, calls for violence, and targeted harassment are prohibited.

EARS (Political-Sensitive)
- WHEN a user publishes content claiming political facts, THE system SHALL provide source fields and apply "Unverified" where absent.
- WHEN a user adds credible sources to previously unverified content, THE system SHALL update the label to "Sourced" and lift exposure limits within 1 hour of submission.
- IF dehumanizing or violent-incitement expressions are detected, THEN THE system SHALL hide the content immediately and route to the high-severity queue.

## 5) Reporting Taxonomy and Processing SLAs
5.1 Report Types (Reason Families)
- Safety: Threat/Violence, Doxxing, Harassment.
- Integrity: Hate Speech, Misinformation, Copyright.
- Quality: Spam, Off-topic, Low-quality/Noise.
- Election Integrity: Undisclosed paid political content, False procedural claims.

5.2 Reporter Credibility Tiers (Business Concept)
- Tier A: report validity ≥ 80% in the last 90 days or verified expert.
- Tier B: 50–79%.
- Tier C: <50% or new reporters.

5.3 Thresholds and SLAs
- High severity (Safety, Election Integrity): auto-hide when ≥ 5 unique reports in 60 minutes including ≥ 2 Tier A; any single admin/moderator may hide immediately.
- Medium severity (Hate, Misinformation, Copyright): soft-hide when ≥ 8 unique reports in 6 hours including ≥ 2 Tier B+.
- Low severity (Spam/Off-topic/Quality): queue-only; apply rate-limit to the author if ≥ 12 valid reports in 24 hours.

EARS (Reporting & SLA)
- WHEN the same content receives ≥ 5 high-severity reports within 60 minutes including ≥ 2 Tier A, THE system SHALL auto-hide the content within 1 minute.
- WHEN the same content receives ≥ 8 medium-severity reports within 6 hours including ≥ 2 Tier B+, THE system SHALL soft-hide the content and mark it "Under Review".
- WHEN the same author accrues ≥ 3 valid spam reports within 24 hours, THE system SHALL apply a 24-hour posting restriction.
- THE governance subsystem SHALL create a unique case ID for every report and record creation time, classification, reporter tier, and affected resource.
- IF a reporter’s invalid-report ratio exceeds 70% over 30 days, THEN THE system SHALL rate-limit further reports to 5/day for 14 days and inform the reporter.

## 6) Moderation Workflow and Automation Rules
6.1 States
- Visible, Labeled, Soft-Hidden (visible to author and direct participants), Hidden (not publicly visible), Removed, Restored, Under Review, Closed.

6.2 Workflow Summary
- Intake → Auto-triage (severity and thresholds) → Queue assignment (priority, specialization) → Decision (label/hide/remove/sanction) → Notify parties → Transparency logging → Appeal (if any) → Closure.

6.3 Closure Statuses
- No Action (policy compliant), Action Applied (specify), Reversed on Appeal, Withdrawn (insufficient evidence), Duplicate, Abandoned (reporter non-response where required).

EARS (Workflow)
- WHEN a report is received, THE system SHALL auto-classify, assess severity, and route to the appropriate queue within 30 seconds.
- WHILE content is "Under Review", THE system SHALL restrict public exposure per state rules (Soft-Hidden or Hidden).
- WHEN a moderation decision is finalized, THE system SHALL notify the author with reason code(s), action summary, and appeal window within 5 minutes.
- THE governance subsystem SHALL record every state transition in an auditable log with actor, timestamp, and reason.
- WHERE conflict-of-interest is detected (moderator is the author or followed party), THE system SHALL reassign the case to a different moderator automatically.

## 7) Sanction Ladder and Triggers
7.1 Sanction Types
- Warning (no feature restriction), Content Removal, Feature Restriction (posting/commenting/messaging), Temporary Suspension: 24h, 7d, 30d, Permanent Suspension, Shadow-visibility reduction (distribution dampening without user-facing label where policy allows).

7.2 Escalation Rules (General)
- First offense (low/medium): warning + policy education.
- Repeated offense (same code) within 90 days: escalate one level.
- High severity (threats, doxxing, targeted hate): minimum 7-day suspension at first offense; permanent at the third within 365 days.

7.3 Special Cases
- Evasion (sockpuppeting) to bypass sanctions: immediate 30-day suspension; link accounts for enforcement.
- Undisclosed paid political content: content removal + 7-day suspension; repeat → 30-day → permanent.
- Coordinated manipulation (brigading/botting): feature restrictions for 30 days; repeat → suspension.

EARS (Sanctions)
- WHEN the same reason code recurs twice within 90 days, THE system SHALL escalate the sanction by one level.
- IF the reason code is ILLEGAL_THREAT or DOXXING, THEN THE system SHALL apply a minimum 7-day suspension at first offense.
- IF three high-severity offenses accrue within 365 days, THEN THE system SHALL impose a permanent suspension.
- WHERE any sanction is applied, THE system SHALL notify the user with duration, affected features, and expiration date/time.
- WHEN evasion is detected, THE system SHALL link related accounts for consistent enforcement and record linkage rationale.

## 8) Transparency Reporting and Logs
8.1 Public Transparency (Aggregated)
- Monthly summary: total reports, actions by category, reversal rates, appeal outcomes, median time-to-action; no personal data.

8.2 User-Facing Case History
- Authors can view their own moderation history including case IDs, timestamps, reason codes, actions, and appeal status.

8.3 Internal Audit Access
- Authorized roles may review detailed audit trails for compliance and training.

EARS (Transparency)
- THE governance subsystem SHALL publish a monthly transparency report with category counts and median processing times by the 10th of the following month.
- WHEN a user sanction is finalized, THE system SHALL add the case to the user’s history within 1 minute.
- THE governance subsystem SHALL store anonymized sample cases for public education consistent with data retention policy.
- WHERE internal audit access is granted, THE system SHALL limit visibility to least-privilege scopes by role.

## 9) Appeals, Re-review, and Restoration
9.1 Timelines
- Appeal window: 14 days from action notification (48 hours for election-period takedowns).
- Acknowledgment: within 24 hours; decision: within 7 days (3 days during election periods).

9.2 Outcomes
- Uphold, Modify (relabel or reduce sanction), Reverse (restore content/access).

EARS (Appeals)
- WHEN a user submits an appeal within 14 days of notice, THE system SHALL acknowledge receipt within 24 hours.
- WHEN an appeal is accepted for review, THE system SHALL issue a decision within 7 days and communicate result + reason codes.
- IF the outcome is Reverse, THEN THE system SHALL restore content/access and remove exposure limits within 15 minutes.
- WHILE an appeal is active, THE system SHALL maintain current enforcement state and present a status message to the user.
- WHERE the original reviewer has a conflict, THE system SHALL assign a different reviewer for the appeal.

## 10) Election-Period Special Policies (Domestic Law Compliance)
10.1 Activation and Duration
- Election windows defined per domestic regulations; activation is recorded and announced by admins with effective dates and summary of stricter standards.

10.2 Stricter Standards
- New accounts (≤ 7 days since registration): cannot publish political campaign content; may comment under policy-compliant labels.
- Claims about election procedures must include an official source; absent source → immediate soft-hide pending verification.
- Paid political content must include sponsor identity and labeling; undisclosed → immediate removal and sanction per escalation.
- Polling blackout and other jurisdictional rules are enforced as policy text configured by admins.

EARS (Election)
- WHERE an election period is active, THE system SHALL restrict campaign-content publishing for new accounts (≤ 7 days since registration).
- WHEN election-procedure claims lack official sources, THE system SHALL soft-hide immediately and maintain restriction until sources are added and verified.
- WHEN paid political content is detected without sponsor disclosure, THE system SHALL remove it and apply the sanction ladder per policy.
- THE governance subsystem SHALL display an in-product banner linking to the active election policy and user guidance.

## 11) Labels, Disclaimers, and Conflicts of Interest
11.1 Labels Catalog (non-exhaustive)
- "Opinion", "Analysis", "Unverified", "Sourced", "Satire", "Paid Promotion", "Sensitive", "Methodology Incomplete".

11.2 Disclaimers
- Economic/financial content: "Not financial advice".
- Polls/Surveys: disclosure of methodology, sample size, collection dates.
- Expert disclosures: affiliation/conflict-of-interest where material.

11.3 COI (Experts)
- Experts disclose affiliations materially related to discussed entities when posting or answering in their domain.

EARS (Labels & COI)
- WHEN content meets label criteria, THE system SHALL attach applicable labels to content metadata and present them visibly to users.
- WHERE an expert author’s conflict is reasonably anticipated, THE system SHALL require entry of affiliation/sponsorship details before public posting.
- WHEN a required disclaimer is missing, THE system SHALL block publication and prompt for completion.

## 12) Performance and Availability Expectations for Moderation
- Report acknowledgment: under 2 seconds.
- Auto-triage classification: under 30 seconds.
- Auto-hide execution: under 60 seconds from threshold crossing.
- Decision notice to author: within 5 minutes of decision.
- Queue coverage: 24/7 for high severity; business hours for medium/low with clear ETAs.

EARS (Performance)
- WHEN a report is submitted, THE system SHALL return an acknowledgment status within 2 seconds.
- WHEN an auto-action threshold is reached, THE system SHALL complete the action within 60 seconds.
- WHERE a case is high severity, THE system SHALL target initial moderator handling within 60 minutes at any time of day.

## 13) Permission Matrix (Role × Action)

| Action (Business) | member | expert | editor | moderator | admin |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Submit report | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| View report queue | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ | ✅ |
| Auto-triage override | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ (within scope) | ✅ |
| Hide content (policy) | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ | ✅ |
| Hide content (editorial quality) | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ (temporary) | ✅ | ✅ |
| Remove content | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ | ✅ |
| Issue warning | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ | ✅ |
| Suspend 24h/7d/30d | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ | ✅ |
| Permanent suspend | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ |
| Publish transparency report | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ (draft) | ✅ (approve) |
| Approve election policy activation | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ |

EARS (Permission Rules)
- WHEN an editor flags suspected policy violations, THE system SHALL require moderator approval for sanctions.
- WHERE a requested action exceeds moderator limits, THE system SHALL route the request for admin approval.

## 14) Diagrams

14.1 Report Lifecycle
```mermaid
graph LR
  A["Report Submitted"] --> B["Auto-Triage(Classify/Severity)"]
  B --> C{"Auto-Hide Threshold Met?"}
  C -->|"Yes"| D["Auto-Hide Content"]
  C -->|"No"| E["Queue Assignment"]
  D --> E
  E --> F["Moderator Review"]
  F --> G{"Decision"}
  G -->|"Label"| H["Apply Labels"]
  G -->|"Hide/Remove"| I["Enforce Action"]
  G -->|"No Action"| J["Close Case"]
  H --> K["Notify Parties"]
  I --> K
  J --> K
  K --> L["Log & Transparency"]
  L --> M["Appeal Window"]
```

14.2 Appeals Flow
```mermaid
graph LR
  A["Appeal Submitted"] --> B["Acknowledge Receipt"]
  B --> C["Assign Reviewer(Independent)"]
  C --> D["Re-review Evidence"]
  D --> E{"Outcome?"}
  E -->|"Uphold"| F["Maintain Action"]
  E -->|"Modify"| G["Adjust Labels/Sanction"]
  E -->|"Reverse"| H["Restore Content/Access"]
  F --> I["Notify & Log"]
  G --> I
  H --> I
```

14.3 Sanction Escalation (Decision Aid)
```mermaid
graph LR
  A["Confirmed Violation"] --> B{"Severity?"}
  B -->|"Low/Medium"| C["Issue Warning + Education"]
  C --> D{"Repeat Within 90d?"}
  D -->|"Yes"| E["Escalate One Level"]
  D -->|"No"| F["Close Case"]
  B -->|"High"| G["Apply ≥7d Suspension"]
  G --> H{"Third High in 365d?"}
  H -->|"Yes"| I["Permanent Suspension"]
  H -->|"No"| F
```

## 15) Glossary of Reason Codes (Examples)
- ILLEGAL_THREAT: credible threats of violence or harm.
- DOXXING: publishing personal identifiable information without consent.
- HATE_SPEECH: dehumanizing or derogatory content targeting protected classes.
- HARASSMENT: targeted abusive behavior toward an individual or group.
- MISINFO_HARM: fabricated or misleading facts likely to cause public harm.
- ELECTION_PROCEDURE_FALSE: false claims about voting procedures or counting.
- SPAM: unsolicited repetitive or promotional content or link farming.
- OFF_TOPIC: content unrelated to the thread/topic.
- LOW_QUALITY: extremely short/noise/non-substantive posts.
- COPYRIGHT: unauthorized reproduction of copyrighted material.
- ELECTION_UNDISCLOSED: paid political content without sponsor disclosure.

## 16) Data Retention and Security Alignment
- Align moderation logs, transparency data, and user case histories with retention windows and privacy constraints defined in the data lifecycle and security/compliance policies.

EARS (Retention & Privacy)
- THE governance subsystem SHALL retain and dispose of case logs according to the published retention schedule.
- THE governance subsystem SHALL record only the minimum necessary personal data to execute moderation and transparency obligations.
- WHERE third-party personal data appears in evidence, THE system SHALL redact or pseudonymize it in public-facing artifacts.

## 17) Change Management
- Policy updates require admin approval and public changelog entries with effective dates and material change summaries.

EARS (Change Mgmt)
- WHEN a policy is updated, THE system SHALL publish its effective date and a summary of key changes in the user policy area within 24 hours of activation.
- WHERE election-period policies are enabled/disabled, THE system SHALL log the activation/deactivation event with actor and timestamps.

## 18) Related Documents
- For feature-level behaviors and validations, refer to the [Functional Requirements Specification](./04-pol-econ-board-functional-requirements.md).
- For privacy, data rights, and lawful processing, refer to the [Security and Compliance Requirements](./09-pol-econ-board-security-and-compliance.md).

---
This document provides business requirements only. Developers retain full autonomy over technical implementation, including architecture, APIs, and database design.

# pol-econ-board Non-Functional Requirements

Measurable, testable non-functional requirements for pol-econ-board are defined from a user-perceived perspective across performance, availability, recovery, scalability, observability, privacy-by-design, time windows, and capacity planning. Technical implementation decisions (architecture, APIs, data models, infrastructure) belong to the development team.

## 1. Scope, Principles, and Assumptions

### 1.1 Scope and Intent
- Business-level, verifiable criteria govern quality attributes for pol-econ-board, expressed as user-perceived outcomes and operational expectations.
- Applicable across development, QA, operations, and product to plan, validate, and operate the service.

### 1.2 Related Documents
- Product context and priorities: [Service Overview for Pol-Econ Board](./01-pol-econ-board-service-overview.md).
- Legal, privacy, and security controls: [Security and Compliance Requirements](./09-pol-econ-board-security-and-compliance.md).

### 1.3 Definitions (Business-Level)
- SLO: Service Level Objective, a target performance or availability level measured over a time window.
- Error Budget: The permissible amount of unavailability or SLO violation within the SLO window.
- RTO: Recovery Time Objective (time to restore service after a disruption).
- RPO: Recovery Point Objective (maximum acceptable data loss measured in time).
- P50/P95/P99: Percentile distribution for response times (server-side processing), excluding end-user network and device rendering time.
- KST: Korea Standard Time (Asia/Seoul), the primary business timezone for scheduling.

### 1.4 Service Boundaries and Assumptions
- THE service SHALL operate scheduling windows in KST and primarily target users in Korea.
- WHERE third-party providers are involved (e.g., email), THE service SHALL measure hand-off times independently and treat provider delays separately for SLO calculations.
- THE baseline usage assumptions and capacity planning in this specification SHALL be revisited quarterly and on major product changes.
- WHERE national events (election periods, major policy/news cycles) elevate load, THE service SHALL preserve P0 SLOs using fair-use and prioritization policies.

## 2. Performance Expectations (Response Time, Throughput, Concurrency)

All performance targets are user-perceived server-side processing times measured at the service boundary, unless stated otherwise.

### 2.1 Core Response Time SLOs (Per Request)

| User Journey (Server-Side) | P50 Target | P95 Target | P99 Target | Notes |
|----------------------------|------------|------------|------------|-------|
| Read timeline/feed         | 150 ms     | 500 ms     | 900 ms     | Personalization and filtering included.
| View a post with comments  | 180 ms     | 600 ms     | 1000 ms    | Initial comment page only.
| Create/edit post save      | 200 ms     | 700 ms     | 1200 ms    | Excludes large media uploads; see 2.5.
| Post publish action        | 220 ms     | 750 ms     | 1200 ms    | Moderation hooks may add queueing; see 2.4.
| Add comment/reply          | 150 ms     | 500 ms     | 900 ms     | Idempotent to avoid duplicates.
| Search (keyword/tag)       | 250 ms     | 800 ms     | 1500 ms    | Typo tolerance and sorting included.
| Login (credential verify)  | 200 ms     | 600 ms     | 1000 ms    | Excludes email verification roundtrips.
| Notification fetch (in-app)| 120 ms     | 350 ms     | 700 ms     | Last 50 notifications.
| Moderation queue load      | 200 ms     | 700 ms     | 1200 ms    | Standard filters applied.

#### EARS Requirements: Response Time
- THE service SHALL meet the response time table targets for at least 99% of business hours each calendar month.
- WHEN a user requests the timeline/feed, THE service SHALL return results within 500 ms at P95 measured monthly.
- WHEN a user opens a post with initial comments, THE service SHALL complete server-side processing within 600 ms at P95 measured monthly.
- WHEN a user submits a new post or saves edits, THE service SHALL acknowledge persistence within 700 ms at P95 measured monthly.
- WHEN a user performs a search, THE service SHALL return results within 800 ms at P95 measured monthly.
- WHEN a user logs in with correct credentials, THE service SHALL complete authentication within 600 ms at P95 measured monthly.
- WHILE the service experiences elevated traffic within stated capacity assumptions (Section 8), THE service SHALL still meet P95 targets without degradation.
- IF P95 targets are missed for two consecutive 15-minute intervals, THEN THE service SHALL trigger a performance incident and apply throttling/deferral policies.

### 2.2 Throughput and Concurrency Targets

| Metric | Baseline Target | Peak Target (Burst ≤ 10 min) | Notes |
|-------|------------------|-------------------------------|-------|
| Read requests per second (RPS) | 350 RPS | 900 RPS | Mix of feed, post, and notification fetch.
| Write requests per second (RPS) | 70 RPS  | 200 RPS | Posts, edits, comments, reactions, reports.
| Concurrent authenticated sessions | 6,000 | 15,000 | Active sessions during national events.
| Concurrent content creators | 800 | 2,000 | Members, experts, editors, moderators combined.

#### EARS Requirements: Throughput and Concurrency
- THE service SHALL sustain the baseline throughput and concurrency targets continuously during business hours.
- WHERE burst traffic occurs for up to 10 minutes, THE service SHALL meet the peak targets without violating P95 response SLOs.
- IF concurrency exceeds peak targets for more than 10 minutes, THEN THE service SHALL apply fair-use throttling and present clear user messaging.

### 2.3 Data Consistency Windows
- THE service SHALL provide read-after-write consistency for a user’s own content within 1 second for posts and comments in the same region.
- WHERE global counters, aggregates, and ranking feeds are displayed, THE service SHALL allow eventual consistency with a maximum staleness of 3 seconds under normal conditions and 10 seconds under peak bursts.
- IF a moderation action hides content, THEN THE service SHALL reflect the hidden state across all user-visible endpoints within 5 seconds.

### 2.4 Queueing and Background Work
- THE service SHALL separate user-facing acknowledgement from heavy background processing, ensuring acknowledgements meet response time SLOs while background tasks complete within defined deadlines (Section 7).
- IF background processing exceeds deadlines, THEN THE service SHALL notify operators through alerts and inform impacted users through non-intrusive in-app messages when relevant.

### 2.5 Media Handling (Business-Level)
- WHERE users upload large attachments, THE service SHALL provide progress feedback and SHALL acknowledge the upload request within 1 second, with final processing completed within 2 minutes for files up to 100 MB.
- IF media processing fails, THEN THE service SHALL preserve the draft state and allow retry without data loss.

## 3. Availability, Recovery, and Release Guardrails

### 3.1 Availability SLOs by Business Tier

| Tier | Description | Monthly Availability Target | Error Budget |
|------|-------------|-----------------------------|--------------|
| P0 | Authentication, read feed/post, submit content, moderation hide/unhide | 99.90% | 43.2 minutes downtime/month |
| P1 | Search, notifications fetch, reactions, bookmarks | 99.50% | 3.6 hours downtime/month |
| P2 | Batch digests, analytics exports, editorial curation updates | 99.00% | 7.3 hours downtime/month |

#### EARS Requirements: Availability & Releases
- THE service SHALL meet the monthly availability targets by tier as defined in the table.
- WHEN maintenance is required, THE service SHALL schedule it within the maintenance window (Sundays 02:00–05:00 KST) and SHALL not breach P0 availability.
- IF unplanned downtime occurs, THEN THE service SHALL prioritize restoration of P0 functions before P1 and P2.
- IF the P0 error budget is exhausted within the month, THEN THE service SHALL pause non-urgent feature launches and focus on reliability until budget recovers the following month.
- WHERE heightened risk windows exist (e.g., election days), THE service SHALL enforce a release freeze for P0-impacting changes starting 24 hours before the window and ending after stability is confirmed.

### 3.2 Recovery Objectives

| Tier | RTO (Restore Service) | RPO (Acceptable Data Loss) | Notes |
|------|------------------------|----------------------------|-------|
| P0 | 30 minutes | 5 minutes | Auth, read, submit, moderation state.
| P1 | 60 minutes | 15 minutes | Search indices, notifications, reactions.
| P2 | 180 minutes | 60 minutes | Batch jobs, exports, curation.

#### EARS Requirements: Recovery
- THE service SHALL restore P0 capabilities within 30 minutes of a major incident and limit data loss to 5 minutes.
- WHERE partial restoration is possible, THE service SHALL restore read-only access first if full write capability cannot be immediately recovered.
- IF RTO or RPO targets are at risk, THEN THE service SHALL publish a user-facing status update within 15 minutes of detection and every 30 minutes thereafter until resolved.

## 4. Scalability and Flexibility Expectations

#### EARS Requirements: Scalability and Updates
- THE service SHALL scale to maintain P95 response targets across baseline and peak loads defined in Section 2.2.
- WHERE traffic grows beyond peak targets for two consecutive weeks, THE service SHALL raise capacity planning actions within 5 business days (Section 8).
- THE service SHALL perform updates with zero user-visible downtime for P0 functions; brief degradations for P1/P2 are acceptable within respective error budgets.
- WHERE a gradual rollout is required, THE service SHALL support audience-based enablement by role (member, expert, moderator, editor, admin) and by percentage-based cohorts.
- WHERE capacity expansions occur, THE service SHALL pre-warm capacity such that cold-start effects do not exceed P95 latency targets during the first 10 minutes of traffic ramp.

## 5. Observability Requirements (Business Criteria)

### 5.1 Business Event Logging
- THE service SHALL log key business events: authentication successes/failures, content creation/edits/deletions, moderation actions, policy violations, notification dispatches, and user preference changes.
- WHERE events include personal data, THE service SHALL minimize logged identifiers and apply redaction per compliance policy in the [Security and Compliance Requirements](./09-pol-econ-board-security-and-compliance.md).
- IF logging fails, THEN THE service SHALL not block user actions and SHALL record a compensating audit entry indicating the gap.

### 5.2 Metrics and SLO Monitoring
- THE service SHALL continuously measure request rates, success/error ratios, latency percentiles, queue backlogs, and notification delivery latencies for each tier.
- WHEN P95 latency or availability deviates from targets for 10 minutes, THE service SHALL raise a warning; for 20 minutes, THE service SHALL raise a critical alert.
- WHERE alert noise exceeds 10 false-positive P0 alerts in a month, THE service SHALL trigger a tuning review within 5 business days.

### 5.3 Alerting and Response Expectations

| Severity | Trigger (Examples) | Operator Response Time (KST) | User Communication |
|----------|---------------------|------------------------------|--------------------|
| P0-Critical | P0 unavailability > 5 min; P95 latency breach > 20 min; security incident indicators | Acknowledge ≤ 5 min, Mitigation start ≤ 15 min, 24/7 | Status page update ≤ 15 min; 30-min cadence thereafter |
| P1-High | P1 unavailability > 20 min; repeated retries on notifications | Acknowledge ≤ 15 min, Business hours (07:00–23:00 KST) | Status page update if user impact material |
| P2-Medium | Batch delays > 2 hours; digest backlog | Acknowledge ≤ 4 hours, Business hours | Optional update in release notes |

#### EARS Requirements: Alerting and Response
- THE service SHALL dispatch alerts according to the severity matrix and SHALL meet the operator response times stated.
- IF a P0 incident is declared, THEN THE service SHALL publish a status page update within 15 minutes and maintain updates at least every 30 minutes until resolution.
- WHERE an incident meets criteria for postmortem, THE service SHALL publish an internal post-incident review within 5 business days including contributing factors and follow-up actions.

### 5.4 Incident Management Flow
- THE service SHALL follow a consistent detect → triage → mitigate → recover → review cycle with operator and user communications.

```mermaid
graph LR
  subgraph "Detection"
    A["SLO Monitor(Deviations)"] --> B{"P0/P1/P2?"}
  end
  subgraph "Triage"
    C["Assign Severity"] --> D["Notify On-call"]
  end
  subgraph "Mitigation"
    E["Throttling/Feature Toggle"] --> F["Partial Restore(Read-first)"]
  end
  subgraph "Recovery"
    G["Full Service Restore"] --> H["Backlog Drain"]
  end
  subgraph "Communication"
    I["Status Page Update"] --> J["Postmortem(Within 5 Business Days)"]
  end
  B -->|"P0"| C
  B -->|"P1/P2"| C
  D --> E
  E --> F
  F --> G
  G --> H
  C -.-> I
  G -.-> I
  H -.-> J
```

## 6. Privacy by Design and Data Minimization (Business Link)
- THE service SHALL collect only the minimum personal data necessary to provide features, following the principles defined in the [Security and Compliance Requirements](./09-pol-econ-board-security-and-compliance.md).
- WHERE personal data is processed for analytics or diagnostics, THE service SHALL prefer aggregated or pseudonymized forms aligned to approved business purposes.
- IF a user opts out of certain data processing, THEN THE service SHALL honor preferences within 24 hours across all processing pipelines.
- WHERE data residency requirements apply by policy or law, THE service SHALL keep personal data within approved jurisdictions for primary storage and processing.

## 7. Notification and Batch Time Windows

### 7.1 Real-time Notifications (In-App)
- THE service SHALL deliver in-app notifications within 5 seconds P95 and 15 seconds P99 after the triggering event under normal conditions.
- IF delivery exceeds 60 seconds for more than 1% of notifications in a 15-minute window, THEN THE service SHALL raise a warning and prioritize notification pipelines.

### 7.2 Email/Scheduled Digests
- THE service SHALL send daily digests between 07:00–09:00 KST on user-selected days, and weekly digests between 08:00–10:00 KST on user-selected weekdays.
- WHERE users change preferences, THE service SHALL reflect changes in the next eligible digest cycle.

### 7.3 Batch and Heavy Processing Windows
- THE service SHALL run heavy batch processes (e.g., re-indexing, large exports) primarily between 02:00–05:00 KST.
- WHERE batch tasks risk impacting P0 workloads, THE service SHALL defer or throttle them to preserve P0 SLOs.
- IF a batch deadline is missed, THEN THE service SHALL notify operators and, where user-facing, inform affected users with a revised completion window within 60 minutes.

## 8. Capacity Planning Guide and Growth Assumptions

### 8.1 Baseline Assumptions (Quarter 1–2)

| Metric | Value | Notes |
|--------|-------|-------|
| MAU | 120,000 | General audience during initial adoption.
| DAU | 36,000 | 30% of MAU.
| Peak concurrent sessions | 12,000 | Major news cycles, debates.
| Daily posts | 8,000 | Includes expert insights and editor features.
| Daily comments | 80,000 | High engagement threads.
| Daily reactions/bookmarks | 400,000 | Lightweight interactions.
| Storage growth | 60 GB/day | Posts, comments, logs, and media references.

### 8.2 Scaling Triggers and Actions
- THE service SHALL review capacity monthly and after significant product launches or public events.
- WHEN P95 latency approaches targets within 10% for two consecutive weeks, THE service SHALL initiate capacity increase planning within 5 business days.
- WHERE storage growth exceeds plan by 25% over a month, THE service SHALL adjust retention and archiving policies according to data lifecycle standards.
- WHERE traffic ramp events are announced (elections, debates), THE service SHALL stage pre-event load tests and capacity checks at least 5 business days in advance.

### 8.3 Fair-Use and Backpressure
- THE service SHALL protect overall user experience by applying fair-use limits during bursts, prioritizing P0 traffic, and transparently communicating delays for non-critical actions.
- WHERE backlogs accumulate for non-P0 tasks, THE service SHALL degrade non-critical features before affecting P0 paths.

## 9. Reliability and Rate Limiting Expectations

### 9.1 Idempotency and Duplicate Prevention (Business-Level)
- THE service SHALL treat repeated submissions of the same post/comment within 30 seconds as a single action and avoid duplicates while returning a single confirmation to the user.

### 9.2 Eventual Consistency and User Feedback
- THE service SHALL surface non-blocking indicators when background processing is pending and SHALL ensure final consistency within deadlines (Sections 2.3 and 7.3).

### 9.3 Rate Limiting and User Messaging
- WHERE users exceed fair-use thresholds (e.g., reports, comments, reactions), THE service SHALL return a clear message indicating temporary limits and the expected retry horizon.
- IF limits are applied erroneously, THEN THE service SHALL automatically lift them within 5 minutes after the triggering condition is cleared.
- WHERE rate limiting is applied due to service protection, THE service SHALL avoid consuming quota for refused retries after a RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED response.

## 10. Non-Functional Acceptance Criteria (Testable)

- THE service SHALL achieve P95 and P99 response time targets in Section 2.1 for the defined user journeys during synthetic load tests matching Section 8 assumptions.
- THE service SHALL sustain throughput and concurrency targets in Section 2.2 for at least 8 continuous hours without breaching P95 SLOs.
- THE service SHALL meet monthly availability targets in Section 3.1 and recovery objectives in Section 3.2 across two consecutive months prior to general release.
- THE service SHALL meet notification timeliness in Section 7 with at least 99% of in-app notifications delivered within 15 seconds under normal conditions.
- THE service SHALL satisfy observability requirements including alerting within thresholds (Sections 5.2–5.3) and incident communications timelines.
- THE service SHALL demonstrate adherence to data minimization commitments in Section 6 through audit of sampled events and stored logs.
- THE service SHALL pass a chaos test where termination of non-critical services does not breach P0 SLOs for 30 minutes.

## 11. Constraints and Out-of-Scope
- Business requirements only; technical implementation decisions belong to the development team, including architecture, APIs, and data models.
- UI/UX specifications, screen design, and styling are out of scope.
- Detailed encryption algorithms, provider selections, and infrastructure topology are out of scope.

## 12. Appendix: Glossary
- Availability: The proportion of time a service is usable by users within agreed functionality thresholds.
- Business Hours: 07:00–23:00 KST for operational staffing expectations, unless otherwise noted.
- Consistency Window: The time allowed for data to become visible across all parts of the service after a change.
- Maintenance Window: A reserved time for planned changes with minimized user impact.
- Percentile Latency: A statistical measure where P95 indicates 95% of requests are at or below the specified time.

---

### Consolidated EARS Requirements Index

Performance
- THE service SHALL meet the response time table targets for at least 99% of business hours each calendar month.
- WHEN a user requests the timeline/feed, THE service SHALL return results within 500 ms at P95 measured monthly.
- WHEN a user opens a post with initial comments, THE service SHALL complete server-side processing within 600 ms at P95 measured monthly.
- WHEN a user submits a new post or saves edits, THE service SHALL acknowledge persistence within 700 ms at P95 measured monthly.
- WHEN a user performs a search, THE service SHALL return results within 800 ms at P95 measured monthly.
- WHEN a user logs in with correct credentials, THE service SHALL complete authentication within 600 ms at P95 measured monthly.
- WHILE the service experiences elevated traffic within stated capacity assumptions, THE service SHALL still meet P95 targets without degradation.
- IF P95 targets are missed for two consecutive 15-minute intervals, THEN THE service SHALL trigger a performance incident and apply throttling/deferral policies.

Throughput and Concurrency
- THE service SHALL sustain baseline throughput and concurrency during business hours.
- WHERE burst traffic occurs for up to 10 minutes, THE service SHALL meet peak targets without violating P95 SLOs.
- IF concurrency exceeds peak targets for more than 10 minutes, THEN THE service SHALL apply fair-use throttling with clear messaging.

Consistency and Background Work
- THE service SHALL provide read-after-write consistency for a user’s own content within 1 second.
- WHERE aggregates and rankings are displayed, THE service SHALL limit staleness to 3 seconds (10 seconds at peak).
- IF moderation hides content, THEN THE service SHALL reflect the state across endpoints within 5 seconds.
- THE service SHALL acknowledge user-facing actions quickly and complete heavy work in background within deadlines.

Availability, Recovery, Releases
- THE service SHALL meet monthly availability targets by tier (P0 99.90%, P1 99.50%, P2 99.00%).
- WHEN maintenance is needed, THE service SHALL schedule it Sundays 02:00–05:00 KST without breaching P0.
- IF unplanned downtime occurs, THEN THE service SHALL restore P0 before P1/P2.
- THE service SHALL restore P0 within 30 minutes and limit data loss to 5 minutes; P1 and P2 per table.
- WHERE partial restore is possible, THE service SHALL enable read-only first.
- IF RTO/RPO are at risk, THEN THE service SHALL publish status updates within 15 minutes and every 30 minutes thereafter.
- IF the P0 error budget is exhausted in a month, THEN THE service SHALL pause non-urgent launches until budget recovery.
- WHERE risk windows exist, THE service SHALL apply release freezes for P0-impacting changes.

Scalability and Updates
- THE service SHALL scale to maintain P95 targets at baseline and peak.
- WHERE traffic exceeds peaks for two weeks, THE service SHALL raise capacity planning within 5 business days.
- THE service SHALL perform updates with zero user-visible downtime for P0; controlled degradations for P1/P2 within error budgets.
- WHERE gradual rollout is required, THE service SHALL support audience and cohort-based enablement.
- WHERE capacity expansions occur, THE service SHALL pre-warm to avoid cold-start breaches.

Observability and Alerts
- THE service SHALL log key business events with data minimization.
- WHERE logging fails, THE service SHALL not block actions and SHALL audit the gap.
- THE service SHALL measure core metrics continuously and alert on deviations (10 min warn, 20 min critical).
- THE service SHALL meet operator response times by severity and publish timely user communications for P0.
- WHERE alert noise exceeds thresholds, THE service SHALL initiate tuning reviews.

Privacy and Data Minimization
- THE service SHALL collect the minimum personal data necessary and favor aggregated or pseudonymized forms for secondary purposes.
- IF a user opts out, THEN THE service SHALL honor preferences within 24 hours.
- WHERE data residency applies, THE service SHALL keep personal data within approved jurisdictions.

Notifications and Batch
- THE service SHALL deliver in-app notifications within 5 seconds P95 and 15 seconds P99.
- IF delivery exceeds 60 seconds for >1% in 15 minutes, THEN THE service SHALL raise a warning and prioritize pipelines.
- THE service SHALL schedule digests within the defined morning windows in KST and reflect preference changes in the next cycle.
- THE service SHALL run heavy batches primarily 02:00–05:00 KST and defer/throttle to protect P0.
- IF a batch deadline is missed, THEN THE service SHALL notify operators and inform users with a revised window within 60 minutes.

Capacity Planning and Fair Use
- THE service SHALL review capacity monthly and after major events.
- WHEN P95 latency is within 10% of the target for two weeks, THE service SHALL plan capacity increases within 5 business days.
- WHERE storage growth exceeds plan by 25% in a month, THE service SHALL adjust retention/archiving per data lifecycle standards.
- WHERE major events are anticipated, THE service SHALL pre-stage load testing.
- THE service SHALL apply fair-use limits during bursts and communicate delays for non-critical actions.

Reliability and Limits
- THE service SHALL treat repeated submissions within 30 seconds as a single action to prevent duplicates.
- THE service SHALL surface pending indicators for background processing and ensure final consistency within deadlines.
- IF fair-use limits are applied erroneously, THEN THE service SHALL lift them within 5 minutes of clearing conditions.
- WHERE protective rate limiting is active, THE service SHALL not consume quota for refused retries after notification.

# 09-pol-econ-board Security and Compliance Requirements

## Purpose and Scope
Specifies business-level security, privacy, legal-compliance, abuse prevention, and incident communication requirements for the pol-econ-board service. All statements define WHAT must occur from a compliance perspective in measurable, testable terms using EARS. Technical implementation decisions (architecture, APIs, database schemas, encryption choices, vendor tools) belong to the development team.

Provides business requirements only. All technical implementation decisions are at the discretion of developers. Describes WHAT the system shall do, not HOW to build it.

## Definitions and Scope of Personal Data
- Personal Data: Information relating to an identified or identifiable natural person (e.g., name, email, IP address, device identifiers, account identifiers, and authored content when linkable to a person).
- Sensitive Data: Government-issued IDs, financial account numbers, precise geolocation, political opinions, health data, and other special categories defined by applicable law.
- Processing: Any operation on personal data (collection, storage, use, disclosure, transfer, deletion).
- Controller (Business Role): Service operator (admin role) determining purposes and means of processing.
- Processor (Operational Role): Third parties processing on behalf of the controller.

## Privacy Principles, Legal Bases, and Consent Management
### Core Principles
- Lawfulness, fairness, transparency
- Purpose limitation and data minimization
- Accuracy
- Storage limitation and retention schedules
- Integrity and confidentiality
- Accountability and auditability

### Legal Bases (Business-Level)
- Contract necessity: providing core service functions (e.g., account, content hosting, moderation safety).
- Legal obligation: fulfilling statutory duties (e.g., responding to lawful requests, retention for compliance).
- Legitimate interests: protecting platform integrity, fraud prevention, product analytics using minimized/aggregated signals (balancing test documented).
- Consent: optional communications, marketing, non-essential analytics/trackers, or features that require opt-in.

### Consent and Preference Governance (EARS)
- THE service SHALL present clear privacy notices at each point of personal data collection describing purposes, categories, recipients, and retention periods.
- THE service SHALL collect only the minimum data necessary for stated purposes and legal compliance.
- THE service SHALL maintain a registry of processing activities including purposes, data categories, recipient categories, geographic locations, and retention periods.
- WHEN a user registers, THE service SHALL obtain explicit consent for optional processing (e.g., marketing communications) separate from essential processing.
- WHEN consent is required by law, THE service SHALL record consent with timestamp, user identifier, consent scope, and source context.
- WHEN a user withdraws consent, THE service SHALL cease the corresponding processing within 24 hours and update the consent registry.
- WHEN processing purposes change materially, THE service SHALL notify users prior to changes and request renewed consent where required.
- WHERE cookies or trackers are used for analytics or marketing, THE service SHALL obtain opt-in consent before activation and provide per-category controls.
- WHILE executing essential service features, THE service SHALL permit processing without optional consents strictly limited to essential purposes specified in privacy notices.
- IF a user declines optional tracking, THEN THE service SHALL honor the choice across sessions within the same account and device context.
- THE service SHALL provide granular preference controls for marketing, newsletter digests, and topic-based communications at category×channel level.
- THE service SHALL retain consent and preference change logs for at least 2 years for auditability.
- WHERE Global Privacy Control (GPC) or equivalent browser signals are detected, THE service SHALL treat the signal as an opt-out for non-essential processing for that browser session and associated account context.

## Data Subject Rights (Access, Rectification, Deletion, Portability)
### Process Overview
Data rights requests (DSAR) are accepted via authenticated channels, acknowledged, verified, processed, and recorded within defined SLAs. Actions include access copy, rectification, deletion, portability export, restriction of processing, and objection where applicable.

### Requirements (EARS)
- WHEN a user submits a rights request, THE service SHALL acknowledge receipt within 1 hour via the user’s preferred contact channel.
- THE service SHALL require identity verification for all rights requests before actioning them.
- WHEN identity verification succeeds, THE service SHALL begin processing within 1 business day.
- THE service SHALL fulfill access and portability requests within 14 calendar days, with one 14-day extension for complex cases where permitted by law.
- THE service SHALL fulfill rectification requests within 7 calendar days after verification.
- THE service SHALL fulfill deletion requests within 7 calendar days except where retention is required by law or for dispute resolution per published policies.
- IF legal retention obligations prevent immediate deletion, THEN THE service SHALL restrict processing to storage-only and inform the user of the legal basis and retention duration.
- THE service SHALL provide access copies limited to the requesting user’s data and exclude third-party personal data unless law permits disclosure.
- WHERE portability applies, THE service SHALL provide a structured, commonly used, machine-readable export of the user’s data and metadata relevant to their content and account settings.
- THE service SHALL log each request with request type, timestamps, verification outcome, action taken, and final resolution status for audit purposes.
- IF a request is manifestly unfounded or excessive, THEN THE service SHALL decline with justification and provide an appeal path.
- THE service SHALL provide an appeal path with review by a moderator or admin independent from the initial handler.
- WHEN a deletion request completes, THE service SHALL remove the user’s profile data and pseudonymize authored public content where policy requires content continuity.
- THE service SHALL limit concurrent open DSARs per user to 3 and rate-limit submissions to 1 per 24 hours per request type to prevent abuse.
- IF identity verification fails after 2 attempts, THEN THE service SHALL close the request with status "verification_failed" and provide retry guidance after 7 days.

### DSAR Evidence, Channels, and Status
- THE service SHALL surface DSAR status and processing timestamps in a user-accessible portal with history of the last 12 months of DSAR events.
- THE service SHALL provide downloadable records of completed DSAR responses for 90 days after closure.

## Age/Identity Verification and Sensitive Period Policies
### Context
Political and economic discourse may involve heightened risk periods (elections, regulatory windows). Age and identity verification may be required by law for specific features or content.

### Requirements (EARS)
- WHERE age-based restrictions apply, THE service SHALL require date-of-birth declaration at registration and provide guardian consent workflows for users under 14 years old.
- IF a user is identified as under 14 years old without guardian consent, THEN THE service SHALL suspend data processing beyond essential safety operations and request consent.
- WHERE real-name verification is mandated for specific publishing features by applicable law, THE service SHALL require identity verification before enabling those features.
- WHILE an election-sensitive period is active as defined by policy, THE service SHALL enable heightened review workflows for flagged political content per community governance policies.
- THE service SHALL provide clear notices about additional processing involved in identity or age verification and retain verification evidence only for the minimum period necessary for compliance.

## Legal/Policy Compliance and Official Requests
### Scope
Covers compliance with Korea’s Personal Information Protection Act (PIPA) and other applicable local regulations for the service’s operating jurisdictions, as well as handling of official requests from authorities or litigants.

### Requirements (EARS)
- THE service SHALL maintain up-to-date records of applicable laws, regulatory guidance, and policy interpretations relevant to privacy and platform governance in operating jurisdictions.
- WHEN a lawful request for user information is received, THE service SHALL verify legal validity and scope before disclosure and document the decision process.
- IF a request is overbroad, THEN THE service SHALL seek to narrow scope and refuse disclosure beyond lawful requirements.
- THE service SHALL notify affected users of disclosure requests unless legally prohibited or risk of harm is identified.
- THE service SHALL preserve relevant data upon receipt of a valid preservation notice and limit access to authorized personnel only.
- THE service SHALL publish jurisdiction-specific policies for cross-border transfers and apply appropriate safeguards consistent with law.
- WHEN policies or laws change materially, THE service SHALL update internal procedures and staff training within 30 days.

## Vendor and Processor Management
- THE service SHALL maintain a vendor inventory listing processors, processing purposes, data categories processed, jurisdictions, and retention dependencies.
- THE service SHALL execute data processing agreements (DPAs) with processors before processing begins and review them annually.
- WHEN a new processor is onboarded, THE service SHALL perform a privacy and security assessment and record the outcome in the processing registry.
- IF a processor fails to meet obligations or suffers a relevant incident, THEN THE service SHALL assess risk, implement mitigations, and notify affected users and/or authorities where required.

## Cross-Border Transfer Governance
- WHERE personal data is transferred cross-border, THE service SHALL identify transfer mechanisms compliant with applicable law (e.g., contractual safeguards) and record them in the processing registry.
- THE service SHALL disclose cross-border transfer destinations and safeguards in privacy notices.

## Audit Trail and Transparency Requirements
### Auditability
- THE service SHALL record administrative and moderation actions with actor role, target resource, action type, timestamp, and standardized reason codes.
- THE service SHALL protect audit logs from tampering via controlled access and integrity controls under developer-chosen mechanisms.
- THE service SHALL retain audit logs for 2 years unless law requires longer retention.

### Transparency
- THE service SHALL publish a transparency report at least quarterly summarizing content moderation actions, government requests, privacy incidents, and DSAR statistics.
- THE service SHALL provide category-level metrics without exposing personal data.
- WHEN any admin or moderator performs a content action, THE service SHALL require a reason code from a standardized taxonomy.
- WHEN DSARs are processed, THE service SHALL update the transparency dataset with count and average resolution time within 7 days of closure.
- IF audit logs reach 80% of planned capacity, THEN THE service SHALL trigger capacity review and retention optimization according to published retention rules.

## Abuse/Spam/Bot Prevention and Rate Limiting Principles
### Philosophy
Balance community participation with platform integrity, using measurable thresholds and fair appeal mechanisms. Thresholds apply per role with stricter limits for new or flagged accounts.

### Default Thresholds by Role
| Action | member | expert | moderator | editor | admin |
|--------|--------|--------|-----------|--------|-------|
| Post creations per hour | 5 | 8 | 12 | 8 | 20 |
| Comments per 10 minutes | 30 | 40 | 60 | 40 | 80 |
| Follows per hour | 20 | 30 | 60 | 30 | 80 |
| Reports filed per hour | 10 | 15 | 40 | 40 | 80 |
| DMs/invites per hour (if enabled) | 10 | 15 | 40 | 20 | 80 |

Additional states:
- New accounts (<72 hours since registration) use 50% of the above limits.
- Flagged accounts (policy or security risk) use 25% of the above limits until review.

### Requirements (EARS)
- THE service SHALL enforce the default thresholds by role and state as listed in the table for posting, commenting, following, reporting, and messaging actions.
- WHILE an account is in new state (<72 hours), THE service SHALL apply the "new" thresholds automatically.
- WHILE an account is in flagged state, THE service SHALL apply the "flagged" thresholds and require manual review by a moderator within 72 hours.
- WHEN a rate limit is exceeded, THE service SHALL block the action and display the remaining wait time before the next allowed action.
- IF automated signals indicate bot-like behavior (e.g., actions at constant intervals or high burstiness), THEN THE service SHALL require an interactive challenge before allowing further actions.
- THE service SHALL provide an appeal path for rate-limit or restriction decisions and resolve appeals within 7 calendar days.
- WHERE abuse is detected across IP/device clusters, THE service SHALL apply graduated restrictions at the cluster level while permitting legitimate users to request review.

## Security Event Communication
### Severity Levels (Business)
- Low: No personal data involved; limited functionality impact.
- Medium: Limited personal data exposure or moderate functionality impact.
- High: Confirmed or likely personal data breach affecting a meaningful subset of users or sustained service degradation.
- Critical: Large-scale personal data breach or service-wide impact.

### Requirements (EARS)
- WHEN a personal data breach is confirmed at Medium severity or higher, THE service SHALL notify affected users without undue delay and within 24 hours of confirmation, including incident overview, data types affected, protective steps, and contact details.
- THE service SHALL notify the competent authority in jurisdictions where required within statutory time limits (target within 72 hours for reportable incidents).
- WHEN a High or Critical incident occurs, THE service SHALL publish public status updates at least every 6 hours until containment and provide a post-incident report within 14 days.
- IF incident investigation identifies compromised credentials or sessions, THEN THE service SHALL invalidate the affected sessions and require re-authentication for impacted users.
- THE service SHALL maintain an incident communication playbook specifying roles, approval steps, and message templates consistent with these timeframes.
- THE service SHALL record incident timelines, decisions, and messages in an immutable audit trail for at least 2 years.

## Roles and Responsibilities for Compliance
### Role Capabilities
| Compliance Action | member | expert | moderator | editor | admin |
|-------------------|--------|--------|-----------|--------|-------|
| Submit DSAR | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| View own DSAR status | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| Approve/deny DSAR | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ (review) | ❌ | ✅ (final) |
| View audit logs | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ (limited) | ✅ (content ops) | ✅ (full) |
| Modify retention schedules | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ |
| Apply account restrictions | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ | ❌ | ✅ |
| Publish transparency metrics | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ (content metrics) | ✅ (full) |
| Handle legal requests | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ |

### Requirements (EARS)
- THE service SHALL restrict DSAR approval authority to admin with optional moderator review as a prerequisite.
- WHEN a moderator applies a restriction, THE service SHALL record the reason code and notify the user with appeal instructions.
- THE service SHALL limit audit log visibility for moderators and editors to their operational scope and exclude sensitive personal data fields.
- THE service SHALL require dual control (two-person review) for changes to retention schedules and transparency report publication.

## Performance and Service Level Expectations
### User-Perceived Performance (KST as business reference)
- THE service SHALL provide DSAR portal responses (status retrieval) within 2 seconds under normal load.
- THE service SHALL deliver consent preference changes and reflect them in processing decisions within 5 minutes.
- THE service SHALL deliver incident notification emails or in-app messages within 15 minutes of the communication decision.

### Operational SLAs
- THE service SHALL maintain availability for DSAR submission endpoints 99.9% monthly, excluding planned maintenance announced 48 hours in advance.
- THE service SHALL ensure audit log write operations succeed for 99.99% of eligible actions measured monthly.
- THE service SHALL acknowledge lawful request intake within 1 business day and record action status changes within 1 hour of each transition.

## Training, Awareness, and Governance
- THE service SHALL conduct annual privacy and security training for moderators, editors, and admins, with completion tracking.
- WHEN material policy changes occur, THE service SHALL issue targeted training updates within 30 days.
- THE service SHALL designate a compliance owner for privacy and governance workflows and publish contact details for inquiries.

## Risk Assessments (PIA/DPIA Triggers)
- WHERE processing introduces high risk to individuals (e.g., new large-scale profiling, sensitive political categories, identity verification expansions), THE service SHALL conduct a privacy impact assessment prior to launch and record mitigations.
- WHEN residual risks remain high, THE service SHALL seek legal/compliance consultation before proceeding.

## Cookie and Tracker Governance
- THE service SHALL categorize trackers into essential, analytics, and marketing; essential operates without consent strictly for service provision.
- WHEN a user opts out of analytics/marketing trackers, THE service SHALL honor the choice for at least 6 months unless earlier preference changes are recorded.
- THE service SHALL display per-category controls and an easily accessible consent management interface on every page.
- WHERE applicable signals like GPC are present, THE service SHALL treat them as an opt-out for non-essential categories in that context.

## Data Minimization and Retention Alignment
- THE service SHALL align privacy retention with the business policies defined in the [Data Lifecycle and Retention Policy](./10-pol-econ-board-data-lifecycle-and-retention.md), favoring pseudonymization and aggregation wherever feasible.
- THE service SHALL ensure that deletion or anonymization outcomes propagate to dependent systems and analytics aggregates according to published windows.

## Visual Process Diagrams (Mermaid)
### DSAR Processing Flow
```mermaid
graph LR
  subgraph "User Submission"
    A["Submit DSAR"] --> B["Acknowledge(1h)"]
  end
  subgraph "Verification"
    C["Verify Identity"] --> D{"Verified?"}
  end
  subgraph "Processing"
    E["Assign Handler"] --> F["Process Request"] --> G{"Type?"}
    G -->|"Access/Portability"| H["Assemble Export"]
    G -->|"Rectification"| I["Apply Corrections"]
    G -->|"Deletion"| J["Delete/Restrict"]
  end
  subgraph "Closure"
    K["Quality Review"] --> L["Respond & Close"]
  end
  B --> C
  D -->|"Yes"| E
  D -->|"No"| M["Close: verification_failed"]
  H --> K
  I --> K
  J --> K
  E --> F
  F --> G
  K --> L
```

### Abuse Detection and Rate Limit Flow
```mermaid
graph LR
  A["User Action"] --> B["Check Thresholds"] --> C{"Exceeded?"}
  C -->|"No"| D["Allow Action"]
  C -->|"Yes"| E["Block & Show Wait Time"] --> F{"Bot-like?"}
  F -->|"No"| G["Log Event"]
  F -->|"Yes"| H["Challenge User"] --> I{"Pass?"}
  I -->|"Yes"| D
  I -->|"No"| J["Apply Restriction"] --> K["Queue Review(72h)"]
```

### Incident Communication Flow
```mermaid
graph LR
  subgraph "Detection"
    A["Identify Incident"] --> B["Classify Severity"]
  end
  subgraph "Notification"
    C["Authority Notify(≤72h)"]
    D["User Notify(≤24h)"]
    E["Status Update(6h cadence)"]
  end
  subgraph "Containment & Postmortem"
    F["Contain & Invalidate Sessions"] --> G["Post-Incident Report(≤14d)"]
  end
  B --> C
  B --> D
  D --> E
  C --> F
  E --> F
  F --> G
```

## References to Related Documents
- See the [Community Governance and Moderation Requirements](./07-pol-econ-board-community-governance-and-moderation.md) for content policy definitions, enforcement triggers, and appeal processes.
- See the [Non-Functional Requirements](./08-pol-econ-board-non-functional-requirements.md) for performance, availability, observability, and capacity expectations that underpin compliance operations.
- See the [Data Lifecycle and Retention Policy](./10-pol-econ-board-data-lifecycle-and-retention.md) for lifecycle stages, preservation, and disposal rules.

## Compliance Notes
Interprets laws and policies at a business-requirements level and deliberately omits technical implementation details, APIs, encryption specifics, and vendor selections. Developers retain full autonomy over how to implement these requirements.
