# pol-econ-board Data Lifecycle and Retention Requirements

Business requirements only; all technical implementation decisions (architecture, APIs, database design, storage tiers, job orchestration) belong to the development team. Defines WHAT must happen across the data lifecycle, not HOW to implement it.

## 1. Scope and Intent
- Establish verifiable and auditable business rules for creation, use, preservation, anonymization, and deletion of information across its lifecycle in the pol-econ-board service.
- Clarify responsibilities and constraints by role (member, expert, moderator, editor, admin) over data states.
- Align with the [Security and Compliance Requirements](./09-pol-econ-board-security-and-compliance.md) and the [Community Governance and Moderation Requirements](./07-pol-econ-board-community-governance-and-moderation.md).

## 2. Definitions and Data Classes
- Core data classes (business-level):
  - Account Profile: minimal identity and preferences for member/expert/moderator/editor/admin.
  - Post: authored content including title/body and metadata (topics, tags, visibility, language, content warnings, sources).
  - Comment/Reply: discussion items attached to a post or comment; includes mentions.
  - Reaction/Vote: engagement signals tied to posts or comments.
  - Follow/Subscription/Bookmark: user-interest signals for topics, authors, or items.
  - Report: user-submitted complaint about content or behavior.
  - Moderation Record: decisions, reasons, sanctions, transparency notes.
  - Notification Record: delivery attempts, status, category/channel, preferences snapshot.
  - Audit Log: immutable traces of sensitive actions and lifecycle transitions.
  - Metrics/Analytics Event: granular events and aggregated counters for business analytics (non-identifying beyond policy limits).
  - Backup Artifact: point-in-time preservation of business records for disaster recovery.
  - DSAR Record: data subject access/rectify/delete/portability requests and fulfillment artifacts (business tracking).
  - Legal Hold Record: records of holds with scope, basis, approver, and review history.
  - Taxonomy Change Record: topic/tag/category adjustments with effective dates and mapping notes.

- Role scope (business perspective):
  - Member/Expert: create and manage own content; request deletion; exercise data rights per policy.
  - Moderator: handle reports; hide/remove content; propose or apply sanctions per policy scope; manage evidence and transparency entries.
  - Editor: curate/pin/feature; manage taxonomy; no unilateral access to personal data beyond business need.
  - Admin: oversee policy application; impose legal holds; manage roles/policies; access audit and transparency logs.

## 3. Conceptual Data Flow Overview
```mermaid
graph LR
  subgraph "Creation"
    A1["Create Draft(Post/Comment)"] --> A2["Validate & Classify"]
  end
  subgraph "Usage"
    B1["Publish & Engage"] --> B2["Edit & Version"]
  end
  subgraph "Governance"
    C1["Report Submitted"] --> C2["Moderation Review"] --> C3["Decision/Sanction"]
  end
  subgraph "Preservation"
    D1["Audit Logging"] --> D2["Backups & Metrics"]
  end
  subgraph "Disposition"
    E1["User/Policy Delete Request"] --> E2["Soft Delete/Archive"] --> E3["Permanent Deletion/Anonymize"]
  end
  A2 --> B1
  B2 -.-> D1
  B1 --> D2
  C3 --> D1
  E1 --> D1
```

## 4. Global Lifecycle Concepts
- States (business-level): Draft, Published, Edited (Versioned), Archived, Hidden (policy/moderation), Soft Deleted, Permanently Deleted, Under Hold (legal/moderation), Restored.
- Transitions: Valid transitions are constrained by holds, appeals, and policy gates.

EARS requirements (global):
- WHILE 항목이 "Under Hold" 상태, THE lifecycle policy SHALL prohibit permanent deletion or anonymization for the affected records.
- WHEN 상태 전이가 발생(create, publish, edit, archive, delete, restore, hold apply/release), THE lifecycle policy SHALL record actor role, timestamp, and reason in an immutable audit trail.
- WHERE referential dependencies exist (e.g., comment → post), THE lifecycle policy SHALL preserve discussion continuity using placeholders when parents are removed.

## 5. Post Lifecycle
States: Draft → Published → Edited (Versioned) → Archived (optional) → Deleted (Soft) → Permanently Deleted.

Creation and drafts
- WHEN a user saves a post as draft, THE service SHALL retain the draft for 90 days since last edit.
- IF a draft remains inactive for 90 consecutive days, THEN THE service SHALL mark it for permanent deletion within 7 days.
- THE service SHALL allow authors to self-delete drafts at any time; WHEN a draft is self-deleted, THE service SHALL purge it permanently within 7 days.

Publishing and editing
- WHEN a draft is published, THE service SHALL record a publication timestamp and initial version identifier.
- WHEN an author edits a published post, THE service SHALL preserve the immediately prior version for 30 days for rollback and audit purposes unless a legal/moderation hold requires longer retention.
- IF a published post is edited within 10 minutes of publication, THEN THE service SHALL treat the edit as a minor update not requiring separate archival unless content meaning materially changes per moderation rules.

Archiving (business visibility management)
- WHERE a post is older than 365 days without new engagement (views, comments, reactions), THE service SHALL be eligible to move it to an archived state where it remains readable but excluded from default feeds.
- WHEN a post enters archived state, THE service SHALL maintain all references (comments, reactions) intact.

Deletion
- WHEN an author deletes a published post, THE service SHALL transition it to soft delete immediately, exclude it from public access, and begin a 30-day recovery window for the author.
- WHEN the 30-day recovery window elapses without restoration, THE service SHALL permanently delete post body and attachments while retaining minimal non-content metadata (author pseudonymous identifier, deletion timestamp, content identifier) for 180 days for audit/abuse-prevention, after which THE service SHALL anonymize or delete such metadata unless under legal hold.
- IF a post is under active moderation investigation or legal hold when deletion is requested, THEN THE service SHALL defer permanent deletion until the hold is lifted and SHALL inform the author through standard communication channels.

Cross-References
- WHEN a post is permanently deleted, THE service SHALL remove or anonymize dependent objects per their own policies (e.g., comments by others remain but lose parent pointer visibility and show a "missing parent" placeholder; reactions are removed).

### Visual: Post Lifecycle
```mermaid
graph LR
  A["Draft"] --> B["Published"] --> C["Edited(Versioned)"]
  B --> D["Archived"]
  C --> D
  B --> E["Soft Deleted"]
  E --> F["Permanently Deleted"]
  D --> E
  subgraph "Constraints"
    G["Under Hold"]
  end
  E -.-> G
  F -.-> G
```

## 6. Comment/Reply Lifecycle
States: Draft → Published → Edited → Deleted (Soft) → Permanently Deleted.

Drafts and publishing
- THE service SHALL apply the same draft retention rules as posts (90-day inactivity purge).
- WHEN a comment is published, THE service SHALL record a publication timestamp and link to the parent post/comment.

Editing
- WHERE editing is permitted by policy, THE service SHALL allow comment edits within 24 hours of posting; WHEN edited, THE service SHALL keep a prior version for 7 days for moderation audit.

Deletion
- WHEN a commenter deletes their comment, THE service SHALL soft delete immediately and offer a 14-day recovery window.
- WHEN the 14-day window elapses, THE service SHALL permanently delete comment content while retaining minimal non-content metadata for 90 days for audit unless under legal hold.
- IF the comment has replies, THEN THE service SHALL display a "comment removed" placeholder at the business content layer and preserve reply visibility.

## 7. Reactions and Votes
- WHEN a user adds or removes a reaction or vote, THE service SHALL apply the change immediately and record an event in audit logs where required.
- WHEN a user account is deleted, THE service SHALL delete or aggregate reactions and votes such that individual attribution is removed within 7 days.
- THE service SHALL retain reaction events for 90 days for abuse detection, after which THE service SHALL aggregate or purge individual events, keeping only aggregate counts.

## 8. Follows, Subscriptions, and Bookmarks
- WHEN a user follows a topic or author, THE service SHALL store the preference until the user unfollows or the account is deleted.
- WHEN a user removes a bookmark, THE service SHALL delete the bookmark record immediately and exclude it from backups after the standard retention window.
- WHERE an account is deleted, THE service SHALL purge follows/subscriptions/bookmarks within 7 days.

## 9. Account Profile and Preferences
- WHEN an account is created, THE service SHALL store only minimal required profile fields and preferences per data minimization principle.
- WHEN a user updates profile fields or preferences, THE service SHALL overwrite prior values and retain a change-audit entry for 180 days.
- WHEN a user requests account deletion, THE service SHALL begin a 14-day cooling-off period during which sign-in cancels the deletion if the user explicitly revokes the request; after the period, THE service SHALL permanently delete or anonymize personal data except data needed for legal obligations or transparency logs.

### Visual: Account Deletion Flow (Cooling-Off → Final Disposition)
```mermaid
graph LR
  A["Account Deletion Request"] --> B["Acknowledge(≤24h)"] --> C["Cooling-Off(14d)"]
  C --> D{"Revoked?"}
  D -->|"Yes"| E["Cancel Deletion"]
  D -->|"No"| F["Delete/Anonymize(≤15d)"]
  F --> G{"Legal/Moderation Hold?"}
  G -->|"Yes"| H["Defer Until Hold Lifted"]
  G -->|"No"| I["Confirm Completion"]
```

## 10. Report/Moderation Lifecycle and Evidence Retention
States: Reported → Triaged → Under Review → Decision → Sanction (if any) → Appeal → Finalized.

Report intake
- WHEN a report is submitted, THE service SHALL timestamp, classify, and place it into the moderation queue.
- THE service SHALL preserve report details and a referenced content snapshot at time of report for evidence.

Review and decision
- WHEN a moderator opens a report, THE service SHALL record reviewer role, actions taken, and timing for transparency.
- WHEN a decision is issued, THE service SHALL store decision, rationale, and policy references.

Evidence retention
- THE service SHALL retain report records, content snapshots used as evidence, and moderation decisions for 2 years from finalization unless stricter statutory requirements apply.
- IF a sanction includes account suspension or permanent ban, THEN THE service SHALL retain minimal identifiers necessary to enforce sanctions for the sanction duration plus 2 years.

Appeals and interactions
- WHEN an appeal is filed within the allowed window, THE service SHALL lock evidence from deletion until appeal closure.
- WHEN an appeal concludes, THE service SHALL reset the retention start to the appeal closure date.
- IF the reported content’s author requests deletion, THEN THE service SHALL keep evidence under hold until the case is finalized, then apply standard deletion rules.

Reference: [Community Governance and Moderation Requirements](./07-pol-econ-board-community-governance-and-moderation.md).

## 11. Logs, Metrics, DSARs, and Backups: Retention and Disposal
Audit and security logs
- THE service SHALL retain authentication, authorization, and sensitive action audit logs for 180 days at minimum and up to 1 year where required by internal policy.
- WHERE logs contain personal identifiers, THE service SHALL pseudonymize identifiers within 30 days unless strict identity is required for ongoing investigations.

Transparency logs
- THE service SHALL retain public-facing transparency records of moderation actions for 2 years, with personal data minimized and pseudonymized where possible.

Operational metrics and analytics
- THE service SHALL retain granular metrics and event samples for 90 days; after 90 days THE service SHALL keep only aggregated, non-identifying statistics for longitudinal analysis.

Notification delivery logs
- THE service SHALL retain notification delivery attempts and outcomes for 90 days to support troubleshooting and opt-in/opt-out proof.

DSAR records
- THE service SHALL retain DSAR request logs and responses for 2 years for audit and compliance, with personal data minimized.

Backups (business-level principles)
- THE service SHALL maintain daily recovery points sufficient to restore to a business-acceptable point-in-time; WHERE monthly full retention applies, THE service SHALL retain monthly recovery points for 3 months and daily recovery points for 30 days.
- IF a user exercises deletion rights, THEN THE service SHALL ensure deleted personal data ages out of backup media within 35 days after deletion completion, acknowledging backup immutability windows.
- THE service SHALL document and publish effective backup retention windows for audit.

Disposal
- WHEN retention expires and no legal or moderation hold exists, THE service SHALL dispose of logs, metrics, DSAR records, and backups in an irreversible manner and record disposal in audit entries.

## 12. Anonymization and Pseudonymization Requirements
Pseudonymization
- WHEN storing data for audit or transparency, THE service SHALL replace direct personal identifiers with stable pseudonymous identifiers sufficient for role-based review but insufficient for public re-identification.
- WHERE cross-record correlation is necessary for abuse detection, THE service SHALL use rotating pseudonymous identifiers that change at most every 90 days while maintaining internal linkage.

Anonymization
- WHEN permanent deletion is required but analytics value remains, THE service SHALL anonymize records by removing or irreversibly altering personal identifiers and quasi-identifiers so re-identification is not reasonably possible.
- IF anonymization cannot guarantee non-reidentifiability for a dataset, THEN THE service SHALL opt for full deletion.

Re-identification prohibition and documentation
- THE service SHALL prohibit attempts to reverse pseudonymization/anonymization and SHALL record violations as security incidents.
- THE service SHALL maintain a business-level data dictionary mapping data classes to anonymization/pseudonymization strategies.

## 13. User-Requested Deletion and Recovery
Content deletion by author
- WHEN an author deletes own content (posts or comments), THE service SHALL begin the applicable recovery window (30 days for posts, 14 days for comments) and provide a self-service restoration option during that window.
- WHEN content is restored during the window, THE service SHALL reinstate visible links and engagement counts except those already purged by separate user actions.

Account deletion
- WHEN a verified user submits an account deletion request, THE service SHALL acknowledge within 24 hours, start a 14-day cooling-off period, and communicate the scheduled deletion date.
- WHEN the cooling-off period ends without revocation, THE service SHALL delete/anonymize personal data within 15 additional days and notify the user of completion if channels remain valid.
- WHERE legal obligations require retention (e.g., moderation transparency, fraud prevention), THE service SHALL retain only minimal necessary data and SHALL document the legal basis.

Exceptions and holds
- IF an active moderation case, payment dispute, or legal hold exists, THEN THE service SHALL defer deletion until closure and SHALL inform the user of deferral reason and next steps.

Recovery portal
- THE service SHALL provide a history of user-initiated deletions within the active recovery window and SHALL allow one-click restoration by the owner.
- WHERE recovery would violate a moderation decision, THE service SHALL block restoration and display the applicable policy reference in user-facing communications.

## 14. Legal Hold and Exceptions
- WHEN an Admin establishes a legal hold for specific subjects or data classes, THE service SHALL freeze deletion and anonymization actions for affected records until the hold is explicitly lifted.
- THE service SHALL record the hold’s scope, reason (business reference), start/end timestamps, and approver role in the audit log and SHALL review active holds every 90 days.

## 15. Retention Matrix (Business Summary)

| Data Category | State/Trigger | Retention Policy | Deletion Type | Recovery Window | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Draft Posts/Comments | Last edit inactive | Delete after 90 days inactivity; purge within 7 days | Permanent | N/A | User can self-delete anytime |
| Published Post Versions | Edit event | Prior version kept 30 days | Auto purge 30 days | N/A | Longer if under hold |
| Posts (Author-deleted) | Soft deleted | Recovery 30 days; then delete content; metadata 180 days | Permanent (content); anonymize metadata | 30 days | Defer if under hold |
| Comments (Author-deleted) | Soft deleted | Recovery 14 days; then delete content; metadata 90 days | Permanent (content); anonymize metadata | 14 days | Placeholder remains |
| Reactions/Votes | Event created | Keep raw 90 days; keep aggregates indefinitely | Aggregate only | N/A | Remove attribution on account deletion (7 days) |
| Follows/Bookmarks | Preference removed | Immediate deletion | Permanent | N/A | Purge within 7 days on account deletion |
| Account Profiles | Deletion requested | 14-day cooling; delete/anonymize within +15 days | Permanent/Anonymize | N/A | Minimal retention if required by law |
| Reports & Evidence | Finalization/Appeal close | 2 years | N/A | N/A | Extend under legal requirements |
| Audit/Security Logs | Log creation | 180 days up to 1 year | Permanent | N/A | Pseudonymize in 30 days unless needed |
| Transparency Logs | Action published | 2 years | N/A | N/A | Personal data minimized |
| Metrics/Analytics | Event creation | Granular 90 days; aggregates thereafter | Aggregate | N/A | Non-identifying aggregates |
| Notification Logs | Event creation | 90 days | Permanent | N/A | Proof of consent history |
| DSAR Records | Request closure | 2 years | Permanent | N/A | Minimized content |
| Backups | Recovery point creation | Daily 30 days; Monthly 3 months | Secure destruction | N/A | Deleted data ages out ≤35 days |
| Taxonomy Change Records | Change applied | 1 year | Permanent | N/A | For curation audit |
| Legal Hold Records | Hold creation | Duration of hold + 2 years | N/A | N/A | Scope/review trail retained |

## 16. Error Handling and Edge Cases (Business)
Conflicts and holds
- IF a user requests deletion while a legal or moderation hold exists, THEN THE service SHALL process the request to the extent possible and queue the remainder until the hold is lifted, with user notification per communications policy.

Referential integrity
- WHEN a parent post is permanently deleted, THE service SHALL ensure that child comments remain visible if policy allows, with a clear placeholder and without broken navigation.

Partial failures
- IF a deletion workflow partially completes, THEN THE service SHALL mark the item as "deletion pending" and retry within 24 hours until completion or hold.

Race conditions
- WHEN simultaneous restore and delete actions occur within a recovery window, THE service SHALL prioritize the most recent, explicitly confirmed user action and record the decision in the audit log.

Attachments and embedded media
- WHEN content is deleted, THE service SHALL apply the same retention schedule to associated attachments and embedded media unless under hold.

Data residency and localization (business-level)
- WHERE data residency constraints apply, THE service SHALL ensure residency-compliant storage locations for preserved data classes and SHALL document residency scope in audit.

## 17. Auditability and Policy Governance
Lifecycle event logging
- THE service SHALL record lifecycle transitions (create, publish, edit, archive, delete, restore, hold apply/release) with actor role, timestamp, and reason in an immutable audit trail accessible to Admins for compliance review.

Policy versioning
- THE service SHALL maintain a versioned registry of lifecycle and retention rules; WHEN rules change, THE service SHALL apply new rules prospectively and SHALL not retroactively shorten required legal retention unless permitted by law.

Reviews and certification
- THE service SHALL review lifecycle and retention practices at least annually and after major regulatory updates, certifying compliance status at the business level.

Minimization and purpose limitation
- THE service SHALL collect and retain only data necessary for the stated purpose and duration, as detailed in the [Security and Compliance Requirements](./09-pol-econ-board-security-and-compliance.md).

## 18. Performance and Success Criteria
Verifiability
- WHEN auditors review samples, THE service SHALL demonstrate adherence to stated retention timelines within ±2 days for date-specific windows where no holds existed.

User experience timing
- WHEN users delete content, THE service SHALL remove content from user-facing views within 1 minute and complete background cleanup according to this policy.

Backup aging
- WHEN users exercise deletion rights, THE service SHALL verify that personal data no longer appears in restore points older than 35 days after deletion completion.

Transparency
- THE service SHALL produce a quarterly summary of deletions, holds, appeals, and restoration events without exposing personal data.

Processing deadlines
- WHERE anonymization is selected instead of deletion, THE service SHALL complete anonymization within the same deadlines as deletion for the relevant data class.

---
Business requirements only; developers retain full autonomy over architecture, APIs, database design, and infrastructure choices while ensuring consistency with related policy documents.

# Notifications and Communications Requirements — pol-econ-board

## 1) Scope and Principles
- Coverage: In-app notifications, email communications, and batch/digest messages related to user activity, content interactions, moderation/governance, editorial operations, and account/security events.
- Exclusions: Frontend UI layouts, transport/infrastructure specifics, vendor/protocol details, code or API definitions.
- Goals: Timely, relevant, controllable, and compliant communications that respect user consent and minimize noise.
- Timezone: THE notifications program SHALL operate on user-local timezone; WHERE user timezone is unknown, the default SHALL be Asia/Seoul (KST).

EARS Principles
- THE communications policy for pol-econ-board SHALL prioritize user control (opt-in/opt-out, preferences), relevance, timeliness, and minimal intrusiveness.
- THE communications policy SHALL distinguish transactional messages (account/security/obligatory) and non-transactional messages (community growth/marketing/editorial digests).
- THE communications service SHALL support user-local scheduling for batch and digest deliveries with Asia/Seoul as default.
- THE communications service SHALL maintain compliance with privacy and consent boundaries for all channels and categories.

## 2) Notification Taxonomy and Trigger Events

Categories (business-level)
- Account & Security (transactional): sign-up verification, password reset, password changed, email change confirmation, device/session revocation confirmation, role change.
- Engagement (community interactions): mention, direct reply to a user’s post/comment, new post by followed author, new post in followed topic, expert Q&A invitation or assignment, content featured notification, new follower.
- Moderation & Governance: content reported about user, auto-hide applied, decision issued (warning/suspension), appeal received, appeal outcome, report assigned to moderator, SLA reminder for open reports.
- Editorial Operations: draft submitted for review, review decision, scheduled publish reminder, featured/curated selection, special topic program updates.
- Digests & Summaries: daily/weekly topic digest, author digest, personalized activity summary, moderator/editor ops digests (role-scoped).

Event-driven Requirements (representative and testable)
- WHEN a user is mentioned in a post or comment, THE notification service SHALL create a mention notification for the mentioned user.
- WHEN a new reply is posted to a user’s comment, THE notification service SHALL prepare and deliver a reply notification to the original commenter per preferences.
- WHEN a followed topic publishes a new post, THE notification service SHALL consult the recipient’s category/channel preferences and applicable limits before delivery.
- WHEN a followed author publishes multiple posts within 10 minutes, THE notification service SHALL coalesce the events into a single notification for that window.
- WHEN an expert Q&A answer request is assigned to an expert, THE notification service SHALL generate a high-priority real-time notification to the expert.
- WHEN a user’s content is reported and moderation begins, THE notification service SHALL notify the author that review has started while minimizing sensitive identifiers.
- WHEN a new report is assigned to a moderator, THE notification service SHALL dispatch a priority notification to the assigned moderator.
- WHEN a draft is submitted to the review queue, THE notification service SHALL notify the responsible editor of the review request.
- WHEN a review decision is recorded as approved or changes requested, THE notification service SHALL notify the author of the outcome with reason summary.
- WHEN a security-sensitive account event occurs (password reset request, email change confirmation), THE notification service SHALL dispatch transactional notifications without delay.
- WHEN the scheduled weekly digest window arrives, THE notification service SHALL aggregate the user’s followed sources and compile a summary.
- WHEN a user gains a new follower, THE notification service SHALL create an engagement notification per the recipient’s preferences and rate limits.
- WHEN a user’s post is featured by editors, THE notification service SHALL inform the author with the feature context.

Ubiquitous Rules (classification and envelope)
- THE notification service SHALL apply a category tag (account/security, engagement, moderation, editorial, digest) to every notification.
- THE notification service SHALL include a unique identifier, creation timestamp (with user timezone reference), category, priority, and related resource reference in every notification.

## 3) Channels, Frequency, and Rate Limits

Channels
- In-app: notification center entries and badges (user-visible counters).
- Email: transactional and digest communications.

Channel Assignment (policy)
- WHERE the event is transactional (account/security), THE notification service SHALL use In-app + Email as default channels.
- WHERE the event is engagement (mentions/replies), THE notification service SHALL use In-app by default and use Email only if the user has enabled Email for that category.
- WHERE the event is digest, THE notification service SHALL use Email for the digest and provide an In-app summary card.
- WHERE the event targets moderators/editors/admins for operational duties, THE notification service SHALL support both In-app and Email according to their role preferences.

Frequency and Rate Limits (per user unless specified)
- THE notification service SHALL enforce a global per-user cap of up to 200 In-app notifications/day and up to 20 Emails/day.
- WHERE engagement events relate to the same post/thread, THE notification service SHALL coalesce events into a single notification within a 10-minute window.
- WHERE followed-author events occur within 10 minutes, THE notification service SHALL roll up into one notification.
- WHERE digest delivery is enabled, THE notification service SHALL limit frequency to Daily or Weekly, and SHALL not allow both simultaneously per digest type.
- WHILE a user has DND (Do Not Disturb) hours configured, THE notification service SHALL defer real-time non-transactional notifications until DND ends; transactional alerts may bypass DND.

Performance Expectations (aligned with Non-Functional Requirements)
- THE notification service SHALL make In-app notifications available within 5 seconds at P95 and within 15 seconds at P99 under normal conditions.
- THE notification service SHALL enqueue transactional Emails within 2 minutes at P95 and digests within 10 minutes at P95 from their scheduled time.

Burst and Abuse Protections
- WHERE event volume exceeds 50 notifications/hour for a single recipient outside digests, THE notification service SHALL throttle non-critical engagement notifications to protect experience and suggest digest mode.
- IF a recipient reaches the daily Email cap, THEN THE notification service SHALL defer non-critical Email notifications to the next digest or the next day per user preference.

## 4) Subscription, Follow, and Digest Policies

Follow Defaults
- WHEN a user follows a topic or author, THE notification service SHALL set the default alert level to “In-app real-time” for that source.
- WHERE a user unfollows a source, THE notification service SHALL cease future notifications from that source immediately across all channels.

Digest Composition and Scheduling
- THE notification service SHALL include up to 10 highlight items per digest, prioritizing engagement and followed-source relevance.
- WHERE the Daily Digest is enabled, THE notification service SHALL deliver between 07:00 and 09:00 user-local time using a randomized slot within the window.
- WHERE the Weekly Digest is enabled, THE notification service SHALL deliver on Mondays between 08:00 and 10:00 user-local time.
- THE notification service SHALL exclude items already consumed In-app during the digest period to avoid redundancy.

Coalescing and Deduplication
- THE notification service SHALL present a single roll-up notification when more than one event of the same type occurs within a 10-minute window, incrementing a count.
- IF duplicate creation conditions are detected for the same recipient and resource, THEN THE notification service SHALL suppress subsequent duplicates.

## 5) Consent Management and Preference Settings

Consent Boundaries
- THE notification service SHALL treat transactional messages as permitted under the service contract and essential operations.
- THE notification service SHALL send non-transactional (marketing/community growth/editorial) messages only with explicit opt-in for the relevant categories.

Preference Model
- THE notification service SHALL provide category × channel toggles for: account/security, engagement, follows (authors/topics), moderation, editorial, digest; channels: In-app, Email.
- WHERE no explicit user setting exists, THE notification service SHALL apply rational defaults: engagement In-app=ON, Email=OFF; follows In-app=ON, Email=OFF; digest Email=Weekly ON; account/security Email=ON.
- THE notification service SHALL support DND windows (e.g., 22:00–08:00 user-local) and Snooze durations (e.g., 2h/8h/24h).
- THE notification service SHALL support Mute at author/post/topic granularity to block notifications from specific sources.

User Control Actions
- WHEN a user uses the unsubscribe link in an Email, THE notification service SHALL immediately stop Email delivery for that message category for the user.
- WHEN a user opts out of all marketing/community messages, THE notification service SHALL prohibit delivery of such messages across all channels.
- WHEN a user changes preferences, THE notification service SHALL apply the changes to subsequent events immediately.

Proof and Audit of Consent
- THE notification service SHALL record the timestamp, scope, and channel for opt-ins and opt-outs to support audit and compliance inquiries.

## 6) Message Composition and Tone Guidelines

Message Structure and Limits
- THE notification service SHALL provide a title (max 80 characters), a summary (max 140 characters), and a core sentence in the body copy for clarity.
- THE notification service SHALL avoid including sensitive personal data (full email addresses, phone numbers, exact locations) in notification bodies.
- THE notification service SHALL use descriptive link text in messages (avoid “click here”).

Tone and Content
- THE notification service SHALL maintain a factual, neutral, and non-inflammatory tone appropriate to political/economic topics.
- THE notification service SHALL include minimal sufficient context (e.g., post title) and a direct link to the relevant resource.

Localization and Accessibility
- THE notification service SHALL localize message content to the user’s preferred language; the baseline default is en-US.
- THE notification service SHALL provide accessible copy suitable for assistive technologies and avoid color-only or icon-only significance.

Brand Safety and Safety Checks
- IF prohibited terms, excessive claims, or misleading constructs are detected by policy checks, THEN THE notification service SHALL hold the message for review and mark it as requiring attention.

Examples (business copy patterns)
- Mention: “You were mentioned in ‘Title’ by Author.”
- Reply: “New reply to your comment in ‘Title’.”
- Moderation: “Your post was temporarily hidden pending review.”
- Digest: “Your weekly highlights in topics you follow.”

## 7) Delivery Performance, Retry, and Fallback

Delivery Targets
- THE notification service SHALL create notification records within 1 second of event ingestion and make In-app notifications available within 5 seconds at P95 and 15 seconds at P99 under normal conditions.
- THE notification service SHALL enqueue transactional Email within 2 minutes at P95 and digest Email within 10 minutes at P95.

Retry and Fallback (Email and In-app)
- IF an Email delivery attempt fails, THEN THE notification service SHALL retry at 5, 30, and 120 minutes for a maximum of 3 attempts.
- IF all Email retries fail, THEN THE notification service SHALL maintain In-app delivery only and record the failure for audit.
- IF In-app presentation is deferred due to DND, THEN THE notification service SHALL present immediately upon DND expiration.

Bounce and Complaint Handling
- WHEN hard bounces or repeated complaints are detected for Email, THE notification service SHALL disable Email channel for the affected address and prompt the user to update preferences.
- WHEN soft bounces persist across all three retries, THE notification service SHALL mark the attempt as failed and retain In-app delivery only.

Aggregation Windows
- THE notification service SHALL use a default coalescing window of 10 minutes and SHALL allow policy-defined adjustments by event type.

## 8) Role-specific Rules and Governance Alignment

Member
- THE notification service SHALL provide mentions/replies/follow-based content alerts via In-app by default.
- WHERE sanctions or policy actions affect the user, THE notification service SHALL deliver In-app + Email notices with reason summaries.

Expert
- THE notification service SHALL provide expert Q&A assignments, feature placements, and significant follower growth summaries.

Moderator
- THE notification service SHALL display report assignments, SLA threshold breaches, and appeal arrivals with high priority.
- THE notification service SHALL cap moderator Emails at 40/day per moderator and distribute non-urgent notifications in cohorts to avoid overload.

Editor
- THE notification service SHALL provide alerts for drafts awaiting review, scheduled publish reminders, and featured queue updates.

Admin
- THE notification service SHALL provide role change approval requests, policy update announcements, and transparency report preparation notifications.

Governance Alignment
- THE notification service SHALL include a concise reference to relevant community rules in moderation-related notices.

## 9) Error Handling and User Recovery (communications context)

Common Error Scenarios (business handling)
- IF a send request targets a category that the user has opted out of, THEN THE notification service SHALL refuse delivery and honor user preferences.
- IF the referenced resource is deleted or private, THEN THE notification service SHALL not create the notification.
- IF the user has muted the source (author/post/topic), THEN THE notification service SHALL not create the notification for that source.
- IF rate-limit conditions are exceeded, THEN THE notification service SHALL suppress additional notifications and consider digest deferral.

User Recovery
- THE notification service SHALL provide mark-as-read, delete, mark-all-as-read, and source mute controls in the In-app notification center.
- THE notification service SHALL include category-level subscription management links at the bottom of Emails.

## 10) Data Retention and Auditability (communications context)

Retention Windows
- THE notification service SHALL retain In-app notifications for 180 days.
- THE notification service SHALL retain digest creation records for 365 days.
- THE notification service SHALL retain notification delivery attempt logs for 90 days to support troubleshooting and consent proof.

Auditability and Privacy
- THE notification service SHALL record for each delivery attempt: recipient reference, category, channel, result state, and timestamp.
- THE notification service SHALL provide a downloadable user-facing history of notifications for the last 90 days upon request.
- THE notification service SHALL adhere to data minimization and exclude sensitive personal data from notification payloads and logs.

## 11) Mermaid Flow Diagram (end-to-end)
```mermaid
graph LR
  subgraph "Event Sources"
    E1["User Interaction(Event)"] --> E2["Content Lifecycle(Event)"]
    E3["Moderation(Event)"] --> E4["Editorial(Event)"]
  end

  subgraph "Policy & Preferences"
    P1["Classify Category"] --> P2["Check Consent & Preferences"]
    P2 --> P3{"Within Rate Limits?"}
    P3 -->|"Yes"| P4["Apply Coalescing(10m)"]
    P3 -->|"No"| P5["Suppress or Defer"]
  end

  subgraph "Delivery Orchestration"
    D1{"Select Channels"} --> D2["Create Notification Record"]
    D2 --> D3["Queue In-App"]
    D2 --> D4["Queue Email"]
    D4 --> D5{"Email Success?"}
    D5 -->|"Yes"| D6["Mark Delivered"]
    D5 -->|"No"| D7["Retry(5m,30m,120m)"]
    D7 --> D8{"Succeeded?"}
    D8 -->|"Yes"| D6
    D8 -->|"No"| D9["Fallback In-app Only"]
  end

  subgraph "User Experience"
    U1["Notification Center"] --> U2["Email Inbox"]
    U3["Manage Preferences"] --> U4["Snooze/Mute/DND"]
  end

  subgraph "Observability"
    O1["Log Attempt"] --> O2["Metrics & KPIs"]
  end

  E1 --> P1
  E2 --> P1
  E3 --> P1
  E4 --> P1
  P4 --> D1
  P5 -.-> D1
  D3 --> U1
  D4 --> U2
  U3 -.-> P2
  O1 -.-> O2
```

## 12) Success Criteria and KPIs (business-level)
- THE notification service SHALL target monthly complaint rate (spam markings/unsubscribes) under 0.5% per user.
- THE notification service SHALL maintain first-attempt transactional Email success ≥ 98% and 24-hour final success ≥ 99.5%.
- THE notification service SHALL target digest open rate ≥ 20% and mention notification In-app view rate ≥ 70%.
- THE notification service SHALL meet In-app timeliness targets (P95 ≤ 5s, P99 ≤ 15s) for ≥ 99% of business hours.

## 13) Related Documents and Business-only Scope
- See the [Functional Requirements for pol-econ-board](./04-pol-econ-board-functional-requirements.md) for end-to-end feature behaviors and event triggers.
- Refer to the [Non-Functional Requirements for pol-econ-board](./08-pol-econ-board-non-functional-requirements.md) for performance, availability, and observability expectations.

Business-only scope statement: Defines WHAT the system should do in business terms. All technical implementation decisions (architecture, APIs, database design) belong to the development team, which retains full autonomy over HOW to implement these requirements.

# pol-econ-board Exception Handling and Error Scenarios

Business requirements for handling exceptions and user-visible error scenarios, including recovery procedures and consistency rules. Business requirements only; all technical implementation decisions (architecture, APIs, database design, libraries) are owned by the development team. Describes WHAT must happen, not HOW to build it.

## 1. Purpose and Scope
- Standardize error taxonomy, user-facing messaging, recovery flows, and cross-cutting policies across authentication, authorization, content operations, moderation, external integrations, rate limiting/spam control, notification delivery, system incidents, and data integrity.
- Ensure consistent, actionable responses with measurable performance targets and user recovery guidance.
- Define testable, unambiguous requirements using EARS syntax.

## 2. Related Documents
- User and role definitions with authentication policies: [User Roles and Authentication Requirements](./03-pol-econ-board-user-roles-and-authentication.md).
- End-to-end feature behaviors and validations: [Functional Requirements for pol-econ-board](./04-pol-econ-board-functional-requirements.md).
- Visual user journeys and decision branches: [User Flow Diagrams and Journeys](./06-pol-econ-board-user-flows.md).

## 3. Common Error Taxonomy and User Message Principles

### 3.1 Error Categories and Codes
- Categories (business-level): AUTH, PERM, ACCOUNT, SESSION, CONTENT, UPLOAD, CONFLICT, MODERATION, REPORT, INTEGRATION, RATE_LIMIT, SPAM, DATA, VALIDATION, NOTIFICATION, SYSTEM.
- Error code format: CATEGORY_SUBJECT_REASON (UPPERCASE with underscores). Examples: AUTH_INVALID_CREDENTIALS, CONTENT_VERSION_CONFLICT, RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED, INTEGRATION_PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE, DATA_DUPLICATE_SUBMISSION, SYSTEM_MAINTENANCE_ACTIVE.
- Severity levels (business impact): INFO (no user action required), WARNING (user action suggested), ERROR (user action required), CRITICAL (widespread impact; some features degraded or unavailable).

### 3.2 Standard Error Payload (Business-Level Content)
Business information the response must convey to users and audit (not an API schema):
- errorCode (follows format above)
- title (short human-readable summary)
- message (actionable description with next steps and context bounds)
- userAction (specific recommended user step)
- supportId (opaque identifier for support/audit; unique per incident)
- category (one from §3.1)
- severity (INFO/WARNING/ERROR/CRITICAL)
- retryAfter (optional; seconds or timestamp for earliest retry)

### 3.3 User Message Principles
- Clarity: plain language; no jargon, stack traces, or internal error dumps.
- Actionability: include what the user can do now and when to try again.
- Non-disclosure: hide sensitive internals (validation heuristics, internal IDs, provider secrets, exact anti-abuse thresholds).
- Consistency: uniform tone, structure, and placement across modules; predictable codes.
- Localization: messages localized to the user’s language; placeholders substituted correctly; sensitive content neutral.
- Accessibility: concise text alternatives; avoid color-only signals; no emoji-only indicators.

### 3.4 Performance Expectations for Error Responses
- Detection-to-display latency: ≤ 1.0 second for synchronous actions; ≤ 5.0 seconds for asynchronous confirmations.
- Retryability hints: provided in the same response when applicable.
- supportId: present for all ERROR and CRITICAL severities.

## 4. Global Cross-Cutting Requirements (EARS)
- THE pol-econ-board service SHALL classify every error into exactly one category from AUTH, PERM, ACCOUNT, SESSION, CONTENT, UPLOAD, CONFLICT, MODERATION, REPORT, INTEGRATION, RATE_LIMIT, SPAM, DATA, VALIDATION, NOTIFICATION, SYSTEM.
- THE pol-econ-board service SHALL produce a localized user-facing payload with errorCode, title, message, userAction, category, severity, and supportId for errors of severity ERROR or CRITICAL.
- THE pol-econ-board service SHALL include retryAfter where a bounded retry is appropriate.
- THE pol-econ-board service SHALL avoid exposing internal identifiers, stack traces, SQL details, or provider-specific secrets in user-facing messages.
- THE pol-econ-board service SHALL generate a unique supportId for each user-visible error and persist an audit log correlated by that identifier.
- THE pol-econ-board service SHALL display a user-visible error within 1 second for synchronous failures.
- THE pol-econ-board service SHALL record severity on error creation using the defined scale.
- THE pol-econ-board service SHALL attach remediation guidance in userAction for all actionable errors.
- THE pol-econ-board service SHALL suppress duplicate error messages for the same root cause within a single user action.
- THE pol-econ-board service SHALL provide idempotent handling for user-triggered actions retried due to transient failures.
- WHERE rate limiting applies, THE pol-econ-board service SHALL communicate the next eligible retry time using retryAfter.
- WHERE the user role is moderator or admin and the context involves a policy outcome, THE pol-econ-board service SHALL include standardized reason codes and policy references without exposing personal data beyond business necessity.

## 5. Authentication and Authorization Error Handling

### 5.1 Scenarios
- Invalid credentials at login.
- Email not verified.
- Account locked or suspended per policy.
- Access token expired or invalid.
- Refresh token invalid, expired, revoked, or reused.
- Permission denied due to role/permission mismatch.
- Forced logout due to device revocation or global sign-out.
- Multi-factor step-up required by policy or risk.

### 5.2 EARS Requirements
- WHEN invalid login credentials are submitted, THE pol-econ-board service SHALL return AUTH_INVALID_CREDENTIALS with guidance to check email/password and a link to reset, without indicating which field is wrong.
- WHEN the account email is unverified during login, THE pol-econ-board service SHALL return ACCOUNT_EMAIL_UNVERIFIED with an option to resend verification and indicate expected arrival time within 5 minutes.
- WHEN the account is locked due to policy violation, THE pol-econ-board service SHALL return ACCOUNT_LOCKED with lock duration or appeal instructions according to governance policy.
- WHEN the access token has expired, THE pol-econ-board service SHALL attempt silent renewal using a valid refresh context and, upon failure, present SESSION_EXPIRED requiring re-authentication.
- IF the refresh token is expired, revoked, or reused, THEN THE pol-econ-board service SHALL clear session context and present AUTH_REAUTHENTICATION_REQUIRED with userAction "Sign in again".
- WHEN a user with insufficient permissions attempts a restricted action, THE pol-econ-board service SHALL return PERM_FORBIDDEN with a message indicating that the action is not permitted for the user’s role.
- WHEN an admin performs sign-out from all devices, THE pol-econ-board service SHALL present SESSION_REVOKED and require re-authentication before any protected action.
- WHERE multi-factor authentication is required by policy for the action, THE pol-econ-board service SHALL present AUTH_STEP_UP_REQUIRED with guidance to complete additional checks.
- THE pol-econ-board service SHALL limit login attempts to prevent enumeration and return AUTH_ATTEMPT_LIMIT with a cooldown window not exceeding 15 minutes.

### 5.3 Token Refresh and Failure Flow (Mermaid)
```mermaid
graph LR
  subgraph "Session Lifecycle"
    A["Protected Action"] --> B["Access Token Validation"]
    B --> C{"Valid?"}
    C -->|"Yes"| D["Proceed Action"]
    C -->|"No"| E["Attempt Silent Refresh"]
    E --> F{"Refresh Succeeds?"}
    F -->|"Yes"| D
    F -->|"No"| G["Present SESSION_EXPIRED"]
  end
  G --> H["User Re-authenticates"]
  H --> D
```

## 6. Content Operation Errors (Upload/Save/Conflict)

### 6.1 Scenarios
- Draft autosave failure.
- Publish validation errors (missing required fields, policy constraints).
- Attachment upload failures (size/type/timeout/corrupted file).
- Version conflicts due to concurrent edits.
- Storage quota exceeded for attachments or saved items.
- Network interruption during save/publish.

### 6.2 EARS Requirements
- WHEN draft autosave fails, THE pol-econ-board service SHALL display CONTENT_AUTOSAVE_FAILED within 1 second and queue a background retry up to 3 attempts within 2 minutes.
- WHEN a publish request fails mandatory business rule validation, THE pol-econ-board service SHALL return VALIDATION_FAILED with a list of violated business rules in user language and preserve the user’s data.
- WHEN an attachment upload exceeds allowed size or type, THE pol-econ-board service SHALL return UPLOAD_POLICY_REJECTED specifying allowed limits without exposing internal anti-abuse thresholds beyond published policy.
- WHEN an upload fails due to a transient network error, THE pol-econ-board service SHALL return UPLOAD_TRANSIENT_FAILURE with userAction to retry and SHALL allow up to 3 retries with exponential backoff not exceeding 60 seconds total.
- WHEN a version conflict is detected due to concurrent edits, THE pol-econ-board service SHALL return CONTENT_VERSION_CONFLICT and provide options to reload latest, keep local copy, or create a new revision.
- WHEN the connection is interrupted during save or publish, THE pol-econ-board service SHALL guarantee idempotent processing so that repeated submission does not create duplicates.
- WHERE user storage quota policies apply, THE pol-econ-board service SHALL return UPLOAD_QUOTA_EXCEEDED with guidance on freeing space or upgrading if applicable.

### 6.3 Save Conflict Resolution Flow (Mermaid)
```mermaid
graph LR
  subgraph "Edit and Save"
    A["User Edits Content"] --> B["Submit Save"]
    B --> C["Validate Business Rules"]
    C --> D["Check Latest Version"]
    D --> E{"Conflict?"}
    E -->|"No"| F["Persist Changes"]
    E -->|"Yes"| G["Return CONTENT_VERSION_CONFLICT"]
  end
  G --> H["Offer Options"]
  H --> I["Reload Latest"]
  H --> J["Keep Local Copy"]
  H --> K["Create New Revision"]
  I --> F
  J -.-> F
  K --> F
```

## 7. Report/Moderation Failures and Reprocessing

### 7.1 Scenarios
- Report submission transient failure.
- Moderation queue backlog causing SLA risk.
- Temporary moderation action later reversed.
- Appeal submission validation failure.

### 7.2 EARS Requirements
- WHEN report submission fails transiently, THE pol-econ-board service SHALL return REPORT_SUBMISSION_FAILED with userAction to retry and SHALL preserve the report details locally for 24 hours.
- WHILE the moderation queue backlog threatens SLA, THE pol-econ-board service SHALL surface MODERATION_DELAY_NOTICE to reporters with an updated expected resolution window.
- IF conditions for reversing a moderation outcome are met on re-review, THEN THE pol-econ-board service SHALL issue MODERATION_ACTION_REVERSED notices to impacted users and restore content state where applicable.
- WHEN an appeal submission fails validation, THE pol-econ-board service SHALL return VALIDATION_FAILED with missing or invalid elements summarized in user language.
- THE pol-econ-board service SHALL maintain a transparency log entry for moderation errors with supportId correlation.

## 8. External Integration Failures

### 8.1 Scenarios
- Third-party login provider unavailable or timeout.
- Email delivery provider error or rate limit.
- Webhook or partner feed delays.

### 8.2 EARS Requirements
- WHEN an external login provider is unavailable or returns errors, THE pol-econ-board service SHALL return INTEGRATION_PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE with userAction to try an alternative method or try again later and SHALL not block native email login.
- WHEN sending an email verification or password reset message fails, THE pol-econ-board service SHALL return NOTIFICATION_DELIVERY_FAILED with an option to resend and guidance to check spam folders.
- WHEN partner integration data is delayed, THE pol-econ-board service SHALL present INTEGRATION_DELAY_NOTICE with an estimated refresh time window not exceeding 60 minutes.
- IF external integration errors persist, THEN THE pol-econ-board service SHALL degrade gracefully by disabling dependent optional features and informing users via a banner-level message.

## 9. Rate Limit and Spam Blocking Notifications

### 9.1 Scenarios
- Short-term throttling due to bursts.
- Behavioral spam patterns detected.
- Automated challenge required to continue.

### 9.2 EARS Requirements
- WHEN short-term request bursts exceed thresholds, THE pol-econ-board service SHALL return RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED with retryAfter indicating the earliest retry time and SHALL not consume quota on refused retries after notification.
- WHEN spam-suspect patterns are detected, THE pol-econ-board service SHALL return SPAM_SUSPECTED and limit posting or messaging features for a cooldown period while offering appeal instructions.
- WHERE an automated challenge is permitted by policy, THE pol-econ-board service SHALL present CHALLENGE_REQUIRED and restore normal limits upon challenge success.
- THE pol-econ-board service SHALL avoid permanent blocks on a first offense absent clear abuse signals and SHALL provide a path to remediation or appeal.

## 10. Data Integrity, Duplicate Detection, and Correction

### 10.1 Scenarios
- Double submissions due to retries/back button.
- Duplicate posts/comments within a short interval.
- Orphan references to deleted content; broken parent links.

### 10.2 EARS Requirements
- WHEN the same user action is submitted repeatedly within a short window, THE pol-econ-board service SHALL enforce idempotent processing and return DATA_DUPLICATE_SUBMISSION referencing the original successful action via a user-safe reference.
- WHEN duplicate post content is detected within a policy time window (e.g., 5 minutes), THE pol-econ-board service SHALL return CONTENT_DUPLICATE_DETECTED and offer userAction to edit, merge, or discard.
- IF a referential integrity violation is detected, THEN THE pol-econ-board service SHALL return DATA_INTEGRITY_ERROR and guide the user to refresh or navigate to valid resources while recording the condition for backend reconciliation.
- THE pol-econ-board service SHALL prevent publishing content that violates referential integrity rules and SHALL present a corrective checklist.

## 11. User Recovery Procedures and Guidance

### 11.1 Recovery Center (Business-Level)
Centralized, role-aware recovery page that consolidates recent failed actions with status, diagnostics, and next steps (no UI spec implied).

### 11.2 EARS Requirements
- THE pol-econ-board service SHALL provide a recovery center summarizing the last 20 failed actions per user with timestamps, errorCodes, supportIds, and userAction.
- THE pol-econ-board service SHALL allow resubmission of eligible failed actions from the recovery center where safe and idempotent.
- WHERE a recovery requires specific permissions, THE pol-econ-board service SHALL verify authorization and present PERM_FORBIDDEN if insufficient.
- IF the same failure repeats 3 times consecutively, THEN THE pol-econ-board service SHALL prompt the user with alternative actions or support contact guidance.
- THE pol-econ-board service SHALL include a copyable diagnostics summary (non-sensitive) and the supportId in the recovery center for each failure.

## 12. Notification Delivery Errors and Fallbacks

### 12.1 Scenarios
- In-app notification creation succeeds but display is delayed by quiet hours or client state.
- Email delivery failures due to provider rate limits, bounces, or authentication issues.
- Digest generation backlogs.

### 12.2 EARS Requirements
- WHEN a non-critical notification is suppressed by user quiet hours, THE pol-econ-board service SHALL defer in-app display until quiet hours end and annotate the deferral state.
- WHEN email sending fails transiently, THE pol-econ-board service SHALL retry within policy limits and record outcomes; IF retries are exhausted, THEN THE pol-econ-board service SHALL keep the item in in-app notifications and mark email delivery as failed for user visibility.
- WHERE digest generation backlogs occur, THE pol-econ-board service SHALL prioritize transactional notifications and present a DIGEST_DELAY_NOTICE with the next expected send window.

## 13. System, Maintenance, and Degradation Errors

### 13.1 Scenarios
- Planned maintenance.
- Partial outage or feature degradation.
- Global incident affecting core operations.

### 13.2 EARS Requirements
- WHEN planned maintenance is active, THE pol-econ-board service SHALL present SYSTEM_MAINTENANCE_ACTIVE with a maintenance window and a link to the status page; essential read-only access SHALL be preserved when possible.
- IF a partial outage occurs, THEN THE pol-econ-board service SHALL present SYSTEM_PARTIAL_DEGRADATION and disable dependent optional features while preserving core read capabilities when feasible.
- WHEN a global incident is declared, THE pol-econ-board service SHALL surface SYSTEM_INCIDENT_NOTICE across affected areas with scope, impact summary, and expected next update time.
- WHERE user actions are deferred due to degradation, THE pol-econ-board service SHALL queue the action safely and present the queued state with a later auto-retry policy; idempotency SHALL be maintained.

## 14. Composite Operations and Partial Failures

### 14.1 Scenarios
- Post publish with multiple attachments where some attachments fail processing.
- Multi-step moderation workflow actions where one step succeeds and a subsequent step fails.
- Follow and notify chain where follow succeeds but notification creation fails.

### 14.2 EARS Requirements
- WHEN composite operations include independently retryable sub-steps, THE pol-econ-board service SHALL commit successful sub-steps and present a PARTIAL_COMPLETION notice with specific next steps to resolve failed sub-steps without data loss.
- IF a sub-step is non-compensable and fails, THEN THE pol-econ-board service SHALL roll back the composite action to a consistent prior state and present a clear message describing what was undone.
- WHERE partial completion is user-acceptable (e.g., publish without failed optional attachments), THE pol-econ-board service SHALL offer a choice to proceed without the failed parts and to retry them later.

## 15. Error Code to Message Examples

Representative examples of business content; developers retain autonomy over formatting and transport.

| Category | Example Code | Title | Example User Message | Primary User Action |
|----------|--------------|-------|----------------------|---------------------|
| AUTH | AUTH_INVALID_CREDENTIALS | Sign-in failed | Unable to sign you in. Check your email and password, then try again. | Reset password or try again |
| ACCOUNT | ACCOUNT_EMAIL_UNVERIFIED | Email not verified | Your email is not verified. A new verification message was sent. | Open email and verify |
| SESSION | SESSION_EXPIRED | Session expired | Your session ended. Sign in again to continue. | Sign in again |
| PERM | PERM_FORBIDDEN | Action not permitted | Your account does not have permission to perform this action. | Review permissions |
| CONTENT | CONTENT_VERSION_CONFLICT | Edit conflict detected | Another edit was saved while you were editing. Review the latest version. | Review and resolve |
| UPLOAD | UPLOAD_TRANSIENT_FAILURE | Upload interrupted | The upload was interrupted. You can retry safely. | Retry upload |
| VALIDATION | VALIDATION_FAILED | Needs correction | Some required fields are missing or invalid. Review the highlighted issues. | Fix and resubmit |
| RATE_LIMIT | RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED | Too many requests | You’ve reached the limit. Try again later. | Try again after retryAfter |
| SPAM | SPAM_SUSPECTED | Posting temporarily limited | Unusual activity detected. Posting is limited for a short time. | Follow instructions or appeal |
| INTEGRATION | INTEGRATION_PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE | Provider unavailable | A login provider is temporarily unavailable. Try another method. | Try another method |
| NOTIFICATION | NOTIFICATION_DELIVERY_FAILED | Email not sent | We could not send a verification email. Try again or check spam. | Resend email |
| SYSTEM | SYSTEM_MAINTENANCE_ACTIVE | Maintenance in progress | Some features are unavailable during scheduled maintenance. | Try again after window |
| DATA | DATA_DUPLICATE_SUBMISSION | Duplicate submission | It looks like this was already submitted. | View previous result |

## 16. Success Criteria and Monitoring (Business-Level)
- THE pol-econ-board service SHALL achieve ≥ 99% of synchronous error displays within 1 second, measured at the client boundary.
- THE pol-econ-board service SHALL include supportId in 100% of ERROR/CRITICAL cases and maintain auditable logs.
- THE pol-econ-board service SHALL ensure that 95% of transient upload failures succeed within 3 total retries.
- THE pol-econ-board service SHALL provide retryAfter for 100% of rate limit responses and for planned maintenance windows.
- THE pol-econ-board service SHALL publish monthly summaries for moderation reversals in transparency logs.

## 17. Glossary (Business Terms)
- supportId: User-visible opaque identifier used to correlate an incident with audit logs.
- retryAfter: User-understandable indicator for when a retry is allowed or expected.
- Idempotent processing: Repeating the same user action does not create additional side effects.
- Severity: Business impact classification guiding priority and user communications.
- Partial completion: A result where some sub-steps succeed and others are deferred or failed, communicated clearly to the user.

## 18. Additional EARS Requirements by Area (Comprehensive)

### 18.1 Messaging and Localization
- THE pol-econ-board service SHALL ensure messages are written at a reading level accessible to the general public and avoid legal jargon except where mandated.
- WHERE localization is available for a language, THE pol-econ-board service SHALL deliver messages in that language with placeholders correctly substituted.
- IF message rendering fails, THEN THE pol-econ-board service SHALL fall back to a default language and preserve the supportId.

### 18.2 Logging and Privacy
- THE pol-econ-board service SHALL log sufficient context to diagnose user-visible errors while redacting personal data that is not necessary for diagnosis.
- WHERE privacy regulations require minimization, THE pol-econ-board service SHALL avoid logging content bodies for private messages and log only metadata sufficient for audit.

### 18.3 Retries and Backoff (Business Policy)
- THE pol-econ-board service SHALL cap automated retries to prevent cascading failures and user confusion, not exceeding 3 attempts within 2 minutes for content saves and uploads.
- THE pol-econ-board service SHALL surface retry exhaustion clearly and provide a definitive next step.

### 18.4 Accessibility and Inclusivity
- THE pol-econ-board service SHALL avoid using color-only or icon-only indications for errors.
- THE pol-econ-board service SHALL include concise text alternatives for all alerts.

## 19. Global Error Handling Flow (Mermaid)
```mermaid
graph LR
  subgraph "User Initiated Action"
    A["User Action"] --> B["Validate Input"]
    B --> C{"Valid?"}
    C -->|"No"| D["Return VALIDATION_FAILED"]
    C -->|"Yes"| E["Process Request"]
  end

  subgraph "Error Detection"
    E --> F{"Transient Failure?"}
    F -->|"Yes"| G["Retry with Backoff(≤3)"]
    F -->|"No"| H{"Rate Limit?"}
    H -->|"Yes"| I["Return RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED with retryAfter"]
    H -->|"No"| J{"Permission?"}
    J -->|"Denied"| K["Return PERM_FORBIDDEN"]
    J -->|"Allowed"| L{"Integration Issue?"}
    L -->|"Yes"| M["Return INTEGRATION_PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE"]
    L -->|"No"| N{"System Incident?"}
    N -->|"Yes"| O["Return SYSTEM_* Notice"]
    N -->|"No"| P["Return Specific Error Code"]
  end

  subgraph "User Guidance"
    P --> Q["Attach userAction & supportId"]
    D --> Q
    I --> Q
    K --> Q
    M --> Q
    O --> Q
  end
```

## 20. Rate Limit Handling Flow (Mermaid)
```mermaid
graph LR
  subgraph "Request Handling"
    A["User Action"] --> B["Check Rate Quota"]
    B --> C{"Exceeded?"}
    C -->|"No"| D["Proceed"]
    C -->|"Yes"| E["Return RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED"]
  end
  E --> F["Show Retry Time(retryAfter)"]
  F --> G{"Challenge Allowed?"}
  G -->|"Yes"| H["Present CHALLENGE_REQUIRED"]
  G -->|"No"| I["Wait Cooldown"]
  H --> J{"Challenge Passed?"}
  J -->|"Yes"| D
  J -->|"No"| I
```

---

Business requirements only. All technical implementation decisions, including architecture, APIs, and database design, are under the full autonomy of the development team. Scope is limited to defining user-visible behaviors, rules, and recovery paths for error scenarios in pol-econ-board.
